27055.acip: SPYIR SA BON LA NAS DANG AUTPA LA'I RTZA BA LTA BU PHYI'I SA BON DANG KUN GZHI'I STENG GI BAG CHAGS LTA BU NANG GI SA BON DANG KUN NAS NYON MONGS DANG RNAM BYANG GI MI GSAL BA DANG, ,DGE MI DGE GNYIS KYI MI GSAL BA'AM,
27055.wylie: spyir sa bon la nas dang autpa la'i rtsa ba lta bu phyi'i sa bon dang kun gzhi'i steng gi bag chags lta bu nang gi sa bon dang kun nas nyon mongs dang rnam byang gi mi gsal ba dang, ,dge mi dge gnyis kyi mi gsal ba'am
27055.english: Speaking in a general sense, seeds may be divided into the following types.  There are: [1] First the outer seeds, such as barley seeds—or the roots from which the blue lotus grows. [2] Secondly there are inner seeds, such as the propensities imprinted upon foundation consciousness. [3] Next are those seeds which are unclear as to whether we assign them to the side of existence involved with the negative emotions, or rather to the side involved with purity. [4] And then there are seeds which are unclear in a different sense: that is, which of the two of virtuous or non-virtuous they are considered to be.

27063.english: Next there are what we call [2] “mental seeds for believing in some self-nature.”  These are planted by the learned form of the view of destruction, or such: by whichever form of grasping to a self-nature that it may be, sharing a mental link with the sixth type of consciousness (awareness of the thought); or by negative consciousness, together with its attendants.

27068.acip: YANG GNAS NGAN NI SDIG PA STE, DE LEN PA NI DE KUN NAS SLONG BAR BYED PA STE, NYON MONGS PA RNAMS KYI SA BON DANG, ,SHIN TU SBYANGS PA 'JIG RTEN PA'I CHOS DGE BA'I SA BON DANG SPYAD ZIN PA DGE SDIG GI SA BON RNAM SMIN GYI NGO BOR SMIN ZIN PA DANG, ,SPYAD MA ZIN PA MNGON BRJOD KYI BAG CHAGS TE, DE DANG BCAS PA DRUG TSAN SOGS SU MA ZAD BZHI RU'ANG GSUNGS SO,
27068.wylie: yang gnas ngan ni sdig pa ste, de len pa ni de kun nas slong bar byed pa ste, nyon mongs pa rnams kyi sa bon dang, ,shin tu sbyangs pa 'jig rten pa'i chos dge ba'i sa bon dang spyad zin pa dge sdig gi sa bon rnam smin gyi ngo bor smin zin pa dang, ,spyad ma zin pa mngon brjod kyi bag chags te, de dang bcas pa drug tshan sogs su ma zad bzhi ru'ang gsungs so
27068.english: Not only are the groups of mental seeds counted as six and so forth; they have as well been stated as being an additional set of four: [1] Mental seeds for “taking” a “negative state,” which is a reference to seeds which act to motivate us to perform bad deeds; that is, seeds for a life of negative emotions. [2] Mental seeds for “practiced ease,” referring to seeds for virtue, as a worldly quality. [3] Mental seeds which have “already acted,” a reference to seeds which are either virtuous or non-virtuous and which have already ripened; and now possess the nature of a karmic result. [4] Mental seeds which “have not already acted,” meaning seeds for expression.

27069.acip: ,'ON KYANG DE DAG GI NANG NAS SA BON 'GA' ZHIG NI NANG GI BAG CHAGS BSHAD PA'I ZHAR LA BSTAN PAR DON GSANG BSHAD SBYAR GNYIS DANG, RJE'I DKA' 'GREL LAS GSUNGS PAS THAMS CAD BRTEN PA SA BON GYI KUN GZHI'I DBYE BAR MI SEMS SO,
27069.wylie: 'on kyang de dag gi nang nas sa bon 'ga' zhig ni nang gi bag chags bshad pa'i zhar la bstan par don gsang bshad sbyar gnyis dang, rje'i dka' 'grel las gsungs pas thams cad brten pa sa bon gyi kun gzhi'i dbye bar mi sems so
27069.english: We should note however that a number of the mental seeds just listed are described incidental to the explanation of inner propensities in both Secret Points and the Explication, as well as in the Lord's commentary to difficult points; as such, it doesn't seem to me that all of them can technically be considered divisions to the part of foundation consciousness which is supported (that is, the mental seeds), as opposed to the part of this consciousness which does the supporting. Seeds & foundation, neither one nor separate

27074.acip: ,DANG PO LTAR NA, RTEN DU GYUR PA RNAM SMIN GYI KUN GZHI LA DMIGS RNAM YOD PA BZHIN DU, ,BAG CHAGS KYI MING GI RNAM GRANGS SA BON DE LA'ANG DMIGS RNAM YOD PAR THAL BA DANG,
27074.wylie: dang po ltar na, rten du gyur pa rnam smin gyi kun gzhi la dmigs rnam yod pa bzhin du, ,bag chags kyi ming gi rnam grangs sa bon de la'ang dmigs rnam yod par thal ba dang
27074.english: If the former were the relationship between the propensities and their support, there would be a problem.  The part of foundation consciousness which has already ripened from these propensities—the part which supports the propensities—displays objects of awareness.  If the two shared that first type of relationship, then the propensities (called in this verse “mental seeds,” which is simply a synonym for “propensities”) would also have to display objects of awareness.

27079.acip: BAG CHAGS DE GZUGS SU NI DOGS PA MED LA, KHO RDZAS YOD DU KHAS BLANGS PAS LDAN MIN 'DU BYED DU MI RUNG NA, RNAM PAR SHES PA LAS GZHAN DU 'OS MED DO,
27079.wylie: bag chags de gzugs su ni dogs pa med la, kho rdzas yod du khas blangs pas ldan min 'du byed du mi rung na, rnam par shes pa las gzhan du 'os med do
27079.english: No one could ever imagine that the mental seeds were physical matter.  Neither would it make any sense to say that they belonged to the category of things which are changing but are neither physical nor mental—for they are accepted here as being substantial.  As such, there is no other reasonable choice but to say that they consist of awareness itself.

27088.acip: KUN BTUS LAS, DGE BA'I BAG CHAGS RJES 'BREL GYI DGE BAR BSHAD PA'I LUNG DANG, RNAM SMIN GYI RGYU MI BYED PAR THAL BA DANG, RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU MI BSKYED PAR THAL BA DANG, SDOM PA THOB NAS MA BTANG GI BAR DU DGE BA RGYUN CHAGS SU MI 'BYUNG BAR THAL BA'I RIGS PAS DGE BA DANG MI DGE BA MTSAN NYID PAR, ,BSGRUB NAS DE LTAR 'DOD PA DAG GI DAM BCA' BA'I DON LA LUNG DANG RIGS PA DE RNAMS SGRUB PAR BYED PA YANG DAG TU SONG BA MED DO,,
27088.wylie: kun btus las, dge ba'i bag chags rjes 'brel gyi dge bar bshad pa'i lung dang, rnam smin gyi rgyu mi byed par thal ba dang, rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu mi bskyed par thal ba dang, sdom pa thob nas ma btang gi bar du dge ba rgyun chags su mi 'byung bar thal ba'i rigs pas dge ba dang mi dge ba mtshan nyid par, ,bsgrub nas de ltar 'dod pa dag gi dam bca' ba'i don la lung dang rigs pa de rnams sgrub par byed pa yang dag tu song ba med do
27088.english: We do however see attempts to prove that the nature of the seeds can consist of definitive virtue, or non-virtue.  These arguments cite The Compendium, where it states that virtuous seeds are virtue by association.  Further, they say, these seeds could never act as causes for karmic ripenings, if they were truly this type of neutral entity. Neither could they ever produce a result of the type which stems from a cause of the same general type.  And finally, it would not then be the case that—once we have taken spiritual vows—our good karma continues on in an unbroken stream, until such time as we give them up. The scriptural references and logic for the points in the assertions of people who take such positions though are nothing that constitutes valid proof for these ideas.

27090.acip: ,BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA'I TSUL LA GSUM, ,CHOS NYID KYIS GNAS SNGON MED BSKYED, ,DE DAG GNYIS KAR 'DOD PA 'O,
27090.wylie: bag chags 'jog pa'i tshul la gsum, ,chos nyid kyis gnas sngon med bskyed, ,de dag gnyis kar 'dod pa 'o
27090.english: There are three different opinions On how the seeds are planted: That they reside there By the very nature of things; Or that ones are created Which were not there before; Or that these are both.
27090.raw: {"course": "GK", "acip": ",BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA'I TSUL LA GSUM, ,CHOS NYID KYIS GNAS SNGON MED BSKYED, ,DE DAG GNYIS KAR 'DOD PA 'O,", "wylie": "bag chags 'jog pa'i tshul la gsum, ,chos nyid kyis gnas sngon med bskyed, ,de dag gnyis kar 'dod pa 'o", "english": "There are three different opinions On how the seeds are planted: That they reside there By the very nature of things; Or that ones are created Which were not there before; Or that these are both."}

27091.acip: ,KUN GZHI'I STENG DU BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA'I TSUL LA LUGS GSUM STE, ,BSGO BYED LA MI LTOS PAR CHOS NYID KYIS GNAS PAR 'DOD PA DANG SNGON MED PA'I BAG CHAGS GSAR DU BSKYED, ,PAR 'DOD PA DANG, BAG CHAGS DE DAG GSAR RNYING GNYIS KAR 'DOD PA'O,,
27091.wylie: kun gzhi'i steng du bag chags 'jog pa'i tshul la lugs gsum ste, ,bsgo byed la mi ltos par chos nyid kyis gnas par 'dod pa dang sngon med pa'i bag chags gsar du bskyed, ,par 'dod pa dang, bag chags de dag gsar rnying gnyis kar 'dod pa'o
27091.english: There are three different opinions on how the mental seeds are planted in the foundation consciousness.  Some say that the seeds reside in this consciousness by the very nature of things, without having to depend upon some force which imprints them there.  Others say that seeds which were not present in the foundation consciousness before are created there anew.  And then there are those who believe that these seeds are made up of both old ones, and new ones.

27094.english: As for the position we ourselves hold on this point, the Commentary to Difficult Points says that we agree with the idea about both old and new seeds. 27310.english: Neither could the sensation arise if there were no consciousness providing the site where the mental seeds were imprinted—for in that case, there would be no mental seed acting as the cause or condition for the physical sensation.

27577.acip: RANG GI LUGS NI BDEN 'DZIN GYI MA RIG PA DANG, DE'I BAG CHAGS GANG RUNG GIS BSLAD PA NI ZAG BCAS DANG, BSLAD PA DE DANG BRAL BA'I YE SHES NI ZAG PA MED PA YIN TE,

27577.english: According to our own system, something is “stained” when it is infected either by misunderstanding in the form of believing that things are real, or by the seeds for this tendency—or by both. “Unstained” or “immaculate” then refers to the state of understanding which is free of such infection.

27579.wylie: de yang sangs rgyas kyi sa ma thob tshun chad du ma rig pa'i bag chags kyis ma bslad pa'i shes pa ni, 'phags pa rnams kyi mnyam gzhag mi rtog pa'i ye shes min pa med la, de yang res 'jog pa ste mnyam gzhag las langs pa na bag chags kyis bslad pa can du skye'o
27579.english: Now except for the non-conceptual wisdom of realized beings in their deep state of meditation, there is no state of mind (short of the one possessed by a person who has reached the level of Buddhahood) which is not infected by the seed for the tendency to misunderstand things. Even this wisdom though is variable, in the sense that—when these beings come out of this type of meditation—their mind again takes on that infection by the seed for this tendency.

27580.acip: SA BDUN PA'I BAR DU NI MA RIG PAS SLOD PA YOD LA, SA BRGYAD PA NAS DANG DGRA BCOM PA GNYIS LA NI, SLOD BYED KYI MA RIG PA ZAD PAS, DES BSLAD PA MED KYI MA RIG PA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PA NI YOD DO,,

27580.english: Up through the seventh bodhisattva level, our mind is still infected by the misunderstanding itself. In two cases though—from the eighth level on up, and with enemy destroyers—the misunderstanding which does the infecting is finished off. Thus it is no longer infecting our mind; but we do still have infection going on by the mental seed for this tendency to misunderstand.

27582.acip: SLOB DPON 'DI'I GZHUNG DU MA RIG PA'I RAB RIB DANG BRAL BA'I SHES RAB DANG YE SHES, ZHES DU MA ZHIG GSUNGS PAS MA RIG PA DANG, DE'I BAG CHAGS RIG PA'I KHYAB BYED DU BYAS NAS, DE GNYIS ZAD PA NA YE SHES KYANG LDOG PA SLOB DPON 'DI'I LUGS SU SMRA BA NI,
27582.wylie: slob dpon 'di'i gzhung du ma rig pa'i rab rib dang bral ba'i shes rab dang ye shes, zhes du ma zhig gsungs pas ma rig pa dang, de'i bag chags rig pa'i khyab byed du byas nas, de gnyis zad pa na ye shes kyang ldog pa slob dpon 'di'i lugs su smra ba ni
27582.english: In the classics written by this particular master, we see frequent references to the “wisdom” or “understanding” which is “free of the cataract of misunderstanding.” And then some people have claimed that what this means is that the tendency to misunderstand—and the mental seed which causes this tendency—themselves subsume our very consciousness. They say that when we finish off the two, then, we also put a stop to the understanding itself—and they conclude by stating that this idea expresses the system of the present master.

27589.english: Now it is the case that the deep meditative wisdom of a realized being who is a bodhisattva—and the deep meditative wisdom of realized beings who are listeners & self-made buddhas—are equivalent, in seeing the true nature of things directly, without being infected by mental seeds for the tendency to misunderstand things.

27678.acip: SA BON DE LAS GZHAN PA'I BAG CHAGS KYI SGRIB PA SHES SGRIB TU 'JOG PA NI, SA BRGYAD PA MA THOB BAR DU SPONG BA MIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
27678.wylie: sa bon de las gzhan pa'i bag chags kyi sgrib pa shes sgrib tu 'jog pa ni, sa brgyad pa ma thob bar du spong ba min pa'i phyir ro
27678.english: This is because we say that obstacles represented by mental potentials other than these particular seeds are obstacles to omniscience because they are not eliminated until we attain the eighth level.

28162.acip: BDEN 'DZIN NYON MONGS SU 'JOG PA'I LUGS 'DI LA, NYON MONGS ZAG MED KYI LAM GYIS SPONG BA NA, BDEN 'DZIN RE'I SA BON SPONG DGOS PAS SA BON DE LAS GZHAN PA'I GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS SHES SGRIB TU BZHAG PA'I PHYOGS RE YANG GTAN ZAD MI NUS PAS, NYON MONGS THAMS CAD MA ZAD BAR DU SHES SGRIB MI SPONG BA'I PHYIR, SHES SGRIB NI DAG PA SA GSUM GYI SKABS SU SPONG NGO,,
28162.wylie: bden 'dzin nyon mongs su 'jog pa'i lugs 'di la, nyon mongs zag med kyi lam gyis spong ba na, bden 'dzin re'i sa bon spong dgos pas sa bon de las gzhan pa'i gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags shes sgrib tu bzhag pa'i phyogs re yang gtan zad mi nus pas, nyon mongs thams cad ma zad bar du shes sgrib mi spong ba'i phyir, shes sgrib ni dag pa sa gsum gyi skabs su spong ngo
28162.english: Here in this system, where holding that things are real is classified as a negative emotion, each seed of holding things this way must be eliminated where negativities are eliminated by the path of the immaculate. But not all the different propensities for seeing things in a mistaken way—with a discrepancy—which are other than these seeds, and which we classify as obstacles to omniscience, can at that point be eliminated permanently. As such, we cannot rid ourselves of the obstacles to omniscience until we finish off all the negative emotions; and therefore it is during the three pure levels that we rid ourselves of these omniscience obstacles.

28369.acip: DE YANG THOG MA MED PA'I 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS YONGS SU SMIN PA'I DBANG GIS BYUNG LA, DES KYANG SROG CHAGS THAMS CAD LA YANG DAG PAR DNGOS PO'I BDAG NYID LTA BUR NYE BAR BSTAN PA MTHONG BAR 'GYUR TE, DE'I PHYIR DE DAG GI BSAM PA'I DBANG GIS DNGOS PO BRDZUN PA'I NGO BO THAMS CAD NI, KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA KHO NA'O ZHES BYA'O, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
28369.wylie: de yang thog ma med pa'i 'khrul pa'i bag chags yongs su smin pa'i dbang gis byung la, des kyang srog chags thams cad la yang dag par dngos po'i bdag nyid lta bur nye bar bstan pa mthong bar 'gyur te, de'i phyir de dag gi bsam pa'i dbang gis dngos po brdzun pa'i ngo bo thams cad ni, kun rdzob tu yod pa kho na'o zhes bya'o, zhes gsungs so
28369.english: All of this is coming from the ripening of seeds in our mind which, from time with no beginning, have forced us to see things in a mistaken way. And because of these seeds, what is presented to the minds of every single living creature is a reality that looks as though it is composed of things that exist in & of themselves—and then we see it that way. All these things whose very nature is to lie to us—which are nothing more than creations of our mind—are, the sutra is saying, nothing but things that exist in a deceptive way.

28739.acip: GANG ZHIG GSUNG RAB KYI DON PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR MA RTOGS SHING, 'KHOR BA THOG MA MED PA NAS DNGOS PO BDEN 'DZIN GYI BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA SMIN PA LAS BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YUN RING MO NAS 'DRIS PA'I MDZA' BO DANG BRAL BA STE,
28739.wylie: gang zhig gsung rab kyi don phyin ci ma log par ma rtogs shing, 'khor ba thog ma med pa nas dngos po bden 'dzin gyi bag chags bzhag pa smin pa las byung ba'i dngos po la bden par mngon par zhen pa yun ring mo nas 'dris pa'i mdza' bo dang bral ba ste
28739.english: And so there are those who have yet to grasp the meaning of the highest of all words in an unerring way; in their hearts, the deep seeds for believing that things are real have been sown, for time with no beginning, here in the cycle of pain. These seeds have ripened, and produced a craving for believing that things are real—and these people must learn to leave behind this friend, who has been so close to them, for so very long.

28823.acip: KUN RDZOB NI THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS 'JOG DGOS PA'I PHYIR LOG PA'I KUN RDZOB 'JOG NA YANG DE LA BLTOS NAS 'JOG DGOS NA, MA RIG PA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PA NI 'KHRUL PAR THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS MI 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO,,

28823.english: Deceptive reality is something which must be established by a nominal form of accurate perception; as such, if we were to establish a mistaken form of deceptive reality, that too would have to be established relative to this type of perception. It is not the case then that we could ever use a nominal form of accurate perception to determine that something infected by deep seeds of misunderstanding was mistaken. Views inspired by sleep

28866.acip: 'PHAGS PA SLOB PA'I RJES THOB KYI YE SHES DANG, SO SKYE'I DE KHO NA NYID KYI LTA BA RNAMS, MA RIG PA DANG DE'I BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PA YIN PAS MNGON SUM DU MI SNANG YANG, SPYIR DON DAM BDEN PA SNANG BAR 'DOD DGOS SO,,
28866.wylie: 'phags pa slob pa'i rjes thob kyi ye shes dang, so skye'i de kho na nyid kyi lta ba rnams, ma rig pa dang de'i bag chags kyis bslad pa yin pas mngon sum du mi snang yang, spyir don dam bden pa snang bar 'dod dgos so
28866.english: The wisdom of a realized being who is still learning, during the “aftermath” period subsequent to the direct perception of emptiness; as well as correct views about suchness possessed by common beings; are still infected by misunderstanding, and by the deep seeds for this misunderstanding. As such, they may not take on an aspect of ultimate reality directly; but still we would take the position that—in general—they do take on this aspect.

28926.acip: DE YANG SHES SGRIB KYI MTSAN NYID CAN GYI NYON MONGS CAN MA YIN PA'I MA RIG PA TZAM KUN TU SPYOD PA'I PHYIR, MA RIG PA DANG DE'I BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PA'I SNANG BA DANG BCAS PA'I SPYOD YUL CAN GYI RJES THOB LA GNAS PA'I 'PHAGS PA RNAMS LA SNANG GI, 'PHAGS PA SNANG BA MED PA'I SPYOD YUL MNGA' BA MNYAM GZHAG LA GNAS PA RNAMS LA NI SNANG BA MIN NO,,
28926.wylie: de yang shes sgrib kyi mtshan nyid can gyi nyon mongs can ma yin pa'i ma rig pa tsam kun tu spyod pa'i phyir, ma rig pa dang de'i bag chags kyis bslad pa'i snang ba dang bcas pa'i spyod yul can gyi rjes thob la gnas pa'i 'phags pa rnams la snang gi, 'phags pa snang ba med pa'i spyod yul mnga' ba mnyam gzhag la gnas pa rnams la ni snang ba min no
28926.english: These things make their appearance to realized beings who are in the aftermath period; to those who minds are engaging in objects where there is still an appearance infected by misunderstanding and its deep seeds. And this is because they still engage habitually through simple misunderstanding which is not involved with nedgative emotions; rather, it displays the defining characteristics of an obstacle to omniscience. It is not though the case that these same objects make their appearance to realized beings who possess an object of engagement where there is no impression of self-existence; that is to say, to such beings who are still in that particular deep, balanced meditation.

28928.acip: 'JUG 'GREL LAS, DE LA MA RIG PA'I BAG CHAGS NI SHES BYA YONGS SU GCOD PA'I GEGS SU GYUR PA YIN LA, 'DOD CHAGS LA SOGS PA'I BAG CHAGS YOD PA NI LUS DANG NGAG DAG GI 'JUG PA DE LTA BU'I RGYU YANG YIN TE, MA RIG PA DANG 'DOD CHAGS LA SOGS PA'I BAG CHAGS DE YANG RNAM PA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA DANG, SANGS RGYAS KHO NA LA LDOG PAR 'GYUR GYI, GZHAN DAG LA NI MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR TE,
28928.wylie: 'jug 'grel las, de la ma rig pa'i bag chags ni shes bya yongs su gcod pa'i gegs su gyur pa yin la, 'dod chags la sogs pa'i bag chags yod pa ni lus dang ngag dag gi 'jug pa de lta bu'i rgyu yang yin te, ma rig pa dang 'dod chags la sogs pa'i bag chags de yang rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa dang, sangs rgyas kho na la ldog par 'gyur gyi, gzhan dag la ni ma yin no, zhes gsungs pa ltar te
28928.english: The case here is as we see it described in the autocommentary: As for this, the deep seeds for misunderstanding act as an obstacle to separating out all knowable things; when we still possess the deep seeds for desire and the rest, they further act as a cause for engagement of this type by the two of body & speech. The deep seeds for misunderstanding and desire and the like prevent only the state of omniscience, and enlightenment; but they do not stop the others.

28930.acip: YANG ZHES PAS CHAGS SOGS KYI BAG CHAGS SHES BYA GCOD PA'I GEGS SU YANG BSTAN PAS, NYON MONGS PA'I BAG CHAGS RNAMS SHES SGRIB YIN TE, DE'I 'BRAS BU GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I CHA THAMS CAD KYANG DER BSDU'O,,
28930.wylie: yang zhes pas chags sogs kyi bag chags shes bya gcod pa'i gegs su yang bstan pas, nyon mongs pa'i bag chags rnams shes sgrib yin te, de'i 'bras bu gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i cha thams cad kyang der bsdu'o
28930.english: When the text here says “further” act, it is indicating that deep seeds such as attachment and the like are as well obstacles to separating out all knowable things. Thus we can say that the deep seeds for what is involved with negative emotions are obstacles to knowledge. And as for their results, all states where we make errors due to the discrepancy between what is actually there and what appears to be there can be included here.

28931.acip: NYON MONGS KYI SA BON LA BAG CHAGS SU BZHAG PA CIG DANG, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON MIN PA'I BAG CHAGS GNYIS LAS SHES SGRIB TU 'JOG PA NI PHYI MA STE, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON THAMS CAD ZAD PAS BDEN 'DZIN MI SKYE YANG, BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PAS SNANG YUL LA 'KHRUL PA'I BLO SKYED PA'O,,
28931.wylie: nyon mongs kyi sa bon la bag chags su bzhag pa cig dang, nyon mongs kyi sa bon min pa'i bag chags gnyis las shes sgrib tu 'jog pa ni phyi ma ste, nyon mongs kyi sa bon thams cad zad pas bden 'dzin mi skye yang, bag chags kyis bslad pas snang yul la 'khrul pa'i blo skyed pa'o
28931.english: Deep seeds can be divided into two types: those which can be classified as seeds for negative emotions, and those which are not seeds for negative emotions. Those that we classify as obstacles to knowledge are the latter. That is, when we have finished off all our seeds for negative emotions, the tendency to hold things as real no longer arises; but because we are still infected by deep seeds, we do experience the arisal of states of mind that are mistaken towards the object as it appears to them.

28961.english: But let's consider, instead, those who do not see these same parts to a person, and the rest. Here we are talking about the Buddhas, who are considering these same objects, but free of the obstacles to knowledge: free of the deep seeds for misunderstanding.

28969.wylie: sangs rgyas kyi ji snyed pa mkhyen pa de ma rig pa'i bag chags kyis bslad nas phung sogs snang ba min kyang, gang zag gzhan gyi shes pa ma rig pas bslad pa la snang ba sangs rgyas la snang dgos te, snang ba de med par mi rung la kun rdzob de yod na ji snyed pa mkhyen pas dmigs dgos pa'i phyir ro
28969.english: It is not the case that the knowledge of an Enlightened Being which knows all the things to be known assumes the appearance of the parts to a person and so forth due to some infection by the deep seeds of misunderstanding. Nonetheless, the way it has to work is that the appearance that makes itself known to the perceptions of other individuals whose minds are infected by misunderstanding makes its own appearance to these Buddhas. This is because it would be wrong to say that there were no such appearance at all; while at the same time—if the deceptive is something that exists—then it must be perceived by the knowledge of an Enlightened Being which perceives the total quantity of knowable objects.

28971.acip: GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS MA ZAD KYI BAR DU JI LTA BA DANG, JI SNYED PA MNGON SUM DU 'JAL BA GNYIS NGO BO GCIG TU SKYE MI NUS PAS, MNYAM RJES RES 'JOG TU 'JAL DGOS PAS YE SHES SKAD CIG MA GCIG GI STENG NAS DE GNYIS 'JAL BA MI 'ONG NGO,,
28971.wylie: gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags ma zad kyi bar du ji lta ba dang, ji snyed pa mngon sum du 'jal ba gnyis ngo bo gcig tu skye mi nus pas, mnyam rjes res 'jog tu 'jal dgos pas ye shes skad cig ma gcig gi steng nas de gnyis 'jal ba mi 'ong ngo
28971.english: Until the day when we are able to finish off those deep mental seeds for the mistake—for the discrepancy between what appears and what is actually there—it can never be the case that our direct encounter with the way that all things exist, and with the total quantity of things that exist, could ever arise as a case where to be one were to be the other. That is, we would have to commune with these two in alternation, between states of deep meditation and the periods subsequent to those states. Thus then there would be no instance where we communed with both, within a single millisecond of wisdom.

28972.acip: 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS MA LUS PAR SPANGS PA NA, YE SHES SKAD CIG MA RE RE'I STENG DU YANG YE SHES GNYIS NGO BO GCIG TU SKYE BA RGYUN MI CHAD PAS, DUS GCIG TU SHES BYA GNYIS MNGON SUM DU 'JAL MI 'JAL GYI RES 'JOG MI DGOS SO,,

28972.english: While we have yet to eliminate each & every one of the deep seeds for the mistake, then even relative to each individual instant of wisdom there is an unbroken flow of the two forms of wisdom arising as a single entity; as such, it is not necessary that in any particular moment we alternate, in the sense of both directly engaging in, and not directly engaging in, a particular object of knowledge.

29192.acip: SLOB DPON 'DI'I BZHED PAS NI CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN NYON MONGS YIN PAS, DE'I SA BON SPANGS PA LA TSOGS MTHA' YAS PA GSOG PA'I GROGS MI DGOS LA, GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS KYI SHES SGRIB SBYONG BA LA NI, GROGS DE LTA BU MED PAR SBYONG MI NUS PAR BZHED DO,,
29192.wylie: slob dpon 'di'i bzhed pas ni chos kyi bdag 'dzin nyon mongs yin pas, de'i sa bon spangs pa la tshogs mtha' yas pa gsog pa'i grogs mi dgos la, gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags kyi shes sgrib sbyong ba la ni, grogs de lta bu med par sbyong mi nus par bzhed do
29192.english: The position taken by the current master is that the tendency to grasp to a self-nature to things is a negative emotion; and as such, it is not necessary—if we seek to eliminate the seeds for this tendency—to have the additional help offered by accumulating unlimited masses of good karma. This master would though say that—if we seek to clean ourselves of obstacles to omniscience in the form of deep seeds causing a mistake in the form of the discrepancy—we could not successfully accomplish this purification without just such additional assistance.

29200.acip: KHA CIG NI LAS KYI BAG CHAGS KYIS BSGOS PA'I RNAM SHES KYI RGYUN RTOG PAR BYED LA, DE'I PHYIR LAS 'GAGS KYANG LAS KYIS PHYIS YUN RING PO NAS 'BRAS BU 'BYIN PA MI 'GAL PAR 'DOD DE, LAS KYIS KUN GZHI LA BAG CHAGS 'JOG PAS BAG CHAGS DE LAS KYI 'BRAS BU YIN LA, DE'I RIGS 'DRA BRGYUD PAS MTHAR 'BRAS BU 'BYIN PAS DANG PO'I LAS KYI 'BRAS BU BRGYUD PA LAS 'BYUNG BAR 'DOD PA'O,,
29200.wylie: kha cig ni las kyi bag chags kyis bsgos pa'i rnam shes kyi rgyun rtog par byed la, de'i phyir las 'gags kyang las kyis phyis yun ring po nas 'bras bu 'byin pa mi 'gal par 'dod de, las kyis kun gzhi la bag chags 'jog pas bag chags de las kyi 'bras bu yin la, de'i rigs 'dra brgyud pas mthar 'bras bu 'byin pas dang po'i las kyi 'bras bu brgyud pa las 'byung bar 'dod pa'o
29200.english: Others have an idea about a stream of awareness which is imbued by the deep seed of the karma; as such, they say, there is no contradiction incurred by when we say that a karma gives forth a consequence much, much later, even though the karma itself has stopped. That is, the karma deposits a deep seed in the foundation consciousness; and thus the consequence of the karmic action is that very deep seed. The stream of similar cases of the gives forth, finally, a result. And thus, they believe, the consequence of the original karma is produced from the continuation.

29216.english: This brings us to our third step: explaining additional points that the issues we've discussed here raise, themselves. We proceed in two sections—the way in which the fact that the stopping here does not exist through any nature of its own can actually end up serving as a reason not to accept the concept of foundation consciousness; and the how to posit a foundation for deep seeds even if we don't accept foundation consciousness.

29237.acip: GAL TE KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KHAS MI LEN KYANG DGE MI DGE'I BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA DANG, BAG CHAGS DE SMIN PA LAS 'BRAS BU 'BYUNG BAR 'DOD DGOS TE, 'JUG 'GREL LAS, THOG MA MED PA'I 'KHOR BAR DNGOS PO'I BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA YONGS SU SMIN PA, DNGOS PO LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA, ZHES DANG, DE 'DRA BA GZHAN YANG MANG DU 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
29237.wylie: gal te kun gzhi rnam shes khas mi len kyang dge mi dge'i bag chags 'jog pa dang, bag chags de smin pa las 'bras bu 'byung bar 'dod dgos te, 'jug 'grel las, thog ma med pa'i 'khor bar dngos po'i bag chags bzhag pa yongs su smin pa, dngos po la mngon par zhen pa, zhes dang, de 'dra ba gzhan yang mang du 'byung ba'i phyir ro
29237.english: Even if we don't accept the idea of a foundation consciousness, we still have to agree that virtuous and non-virtuous deep seeds can be planted; and that as these seeds ripen, they give forth results. As the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way puts it, In the cycle of suffering with no beginning, the deep seeds of things have been planted, and have ripened. And we have had a deep belief in those things… And we see many other such references as well.

29239.english: In response, we can say that those who accept the idea of a foundation consciousness would assert that there is a foundation consciousness which functions as the place that negative consciousness focuses upon, and thinks, “This is me.” In the same way, those who follow the present system assert that there is a location that an inborn tendency to think, simply, “me” focuses upon; and that this is the place which is imbued with our deep seeds.

29240.english: “Well then,” one may ask, “what about that reference in the autcommentary to Entering the Middle Way, where it says that the flow of the mind is the location for the deep seeds?”

29241.english: The simple me is itself the “flow” that we talk about relative to the mind, to consciousness. This is why we can even talk about “a flow of the mind.” The mind itself tends to continue on in a series of similar cases; and thus we can speak of its “flow.” From this point of view, this is what provides a place which is imbued with deep seeds, whose own nature is one of coming and going.

29247.english: At this point though, the awareness of our thought is unstained, in the sense that it is not infected by the deep seeds for the error of the discrepancy. 29375.acip: GANG GI PHYIR BYANG SEMS 'DIS NANG GI BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LAS GZUGS SOGS 'BYUNG BAR 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR BA'I RIGS PAS SEMS LA RANG LAS RDZAS GZHAN GYI GZUNG BA MED PAR DE LAS DON GZHAN PA'I DE 'DZIN PAR BYED PA MA MTHONG ZHING, SRID PA KHAMS GSUM PO NI RNAM PAR SHES PA TZAM MO ZHES RAB TU RTOGS PAS TE NAS,
29375.wylie: gang gi phyir byang sems 'dis nang gi bag chags smin pa las gzugs sogs 'byung bar 'chad par 'gyur ba'i rigs pas sems la rang las rdzas gzhan gyi gzung ba med par de las don gzhan pa'i de 'dzin par byed pa ma mthong zhing, srid pa khams gsum po ni rnam par shes pa tsam mo zhes rab tu rtogs pas te nas
29375.english: The bodhisattva utilizes reasoning—which we are about to explain—to understand how physical form and the like come into being through the ripening of deep seeds inside of themselves; which is to say, this logic allows them to understand how there are no objects of perception which are such that to be them is not to be the mind itself. They see no entities which act to hold to these objects and are separate from them. And so—which is to say, first—they come to a deep realization that all three realms of existence are only consciousness itself.

29380.acip: DE BZHIN DU PHYI NANG GI DNGOS PO KUN GYI SA BON KUN GZHI RNAM SHES ZHES BYA BA LAS, CHAGS SOGS DANG DAD SOGS 'GAG BZHIN PAS RANG DANG RJES SU MTHUN PA'I NUS PA KUN GZHI LA BZHAG PA'I BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LAS MA DAG PA'I GZHAN DBANG RNAM SHES TZAM ZHIG 'BYUNG BA
29380.wylie: de bzhin du phyi nang gi dngos po kun gyi sa bon kun gzhi rnam shes zhes bya ba las, chags sogs dang dad sogs 'gag bzhin pas rang dang rjes su mthun pa'i nus pa kun gzhi la bzhag pa'i bag chags smin pa las ma dag pa'i gzhan dbang rnam shes tsam zhig 'byung ba
29380.english: Just so do we have what we call “foundation consciousness”: the all-foundation for the deep seeds of every inner & outer entity. From it come forth things like attachment & such; and faith & the like. As they come to a stop, they leave deep seeds deposited in the foundation consciousness: energies concordant with their various natures. As these seeds ripen, things which are nothing more than consciousness arise from that: impure forms of dominated entitites.

29411.wylie: gzhan dbang de ni phyi rol gyi gzung ba med par rang gi bag chags kho na las 'byung bar 'gyur la, rang bzhin gyis yod pa dang 'di'i lugs kyi don dam par sgra rtog gi spros pa kun te thams cad kyi yul min pa'i rang bzhin can du yod de, phyi nang gi mngon par brjod pa ni dngos su ma brtags pa'i rnam pa 'dzin pa'i phyir ro
29411.english: Dominated entities lack any outer objects which are grasped; they are things that occur only from their deep seeds. And they exist through their own nature and—as being ultimate, in this system—they have a nature where they can never be objects of any, of all, elaboration of word & thought. And so they retain an aspect where they are not direct formulations of outer or inner expression.

29416.english: The expanded description has three sections of its own: denying a metaphor which is meant to show that awareness where there are no outer objects could exist through some nature of its own; denying the referent of the metaphor in a case where awareness arises from the power of a deep seed, and is empty of the referent; and finally a demonstration that there is no contradiction between this particular denial, and the meditation on the repulsive.

29478.wylie: de yang ji ltar gzigs pa'i ngor ni gsum po mi snang la, ji snyed pa gzigs pa'i ngor ni yul can rang nyid ma rig pa'i bag chags kyis bslad pa'i dbang gis snang ba med kyang, gang zag gzhan gyi shes pa bslad pa'i dbang gis snang ba rnams, de la snang ba'i sgo nas sangs rgyas la snang nas mkhyen pa yin no
29478.english: None of the three, moreover, can appear to the perceptions of a person who is seeing the way that all things are. What appears though to the perceptions of a person who is seeing all the things there are? They is no appearance of them to a subject state of mind due to any infection of it by deep seeds for misunderstanding. They can though make their appearance by force of the fact that the awareness of another person's mind is infected; and what is appearing to them then appears to the Buddha, and thus they know them. No strand of hair

29490.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, BAG CHAGS SMIN MA SMIN NYID LAS DON SNANG GI RNAM SHES SKYE BA DANG MI SKYE BA DGAG PA, SLAR YANG PHYI ROL MED PAR RNAM SHES YOD TSUL BRJOD PA DGAG PA, SEMS TZAM GYI LUGS BKAG PA LA LUNG GI GNOD PA MED PAR BSTAN PA'O,,

29490.english: This brings us to our second section from above: denying the referent of the metaphor in a case where awareness arises from the power of a deep seed. Here we proceed in three steps: denying that an awareness that takes on the image of the object and which comes from either the ripening or the lack of ripening of a deep seed could ever grow, or not grow; once more denying the description of how there could be an awareness, in the absence of outer objects; and showing how there is no problem from scripture when we deny the system of the Mind Only.

29495.acip: RNAM SHES SKYE BA'I BAG CHAGS SNGAR BZHAG PA DE SMIN PA DANG MA SMIN PA DE DAG RNAM PAR SHES PA SKYE BA DANG MI SKYE BA'I RGYU YIN TE,

29495.english: A deep seed for the growth of awareness was planted earlier on; and the ripening—or the not ripening—of that seed is the cause for the growth, or the failure to grow, of that awareness.

29497.acip: ,GANG GI PHYIR RAB RIB MED PAR YUL MTHONG BA DAG LA SKRA SHAD DU SNANG BA'I BLO YI NUS PA BAG CHAGS NI SMIN PA MED PA DE'I PHYIR RAB RIB MED PA DE LA SKRA SHAD MTHONG BA'I BLO SKYE BAR MI 'GYUR BA YIN GYI, SHES BYA SKRA SHAD DU YOD PA'I DNGOS PO DANG BRAL BAS BLO DE MI SKYE BA MIN NO ZHE NA,

29497.english: It is not however the case that there would be any ripening of a deep seed—the potential for a state of mind that took on the aspect of a strand of hair—with those who saw the object but had no cataracts. It is not though the case that this state of mind would fail to grow because it was devoid of any entity which possessed an existing object which was a strand of hair. Suppose then that this were your position. The present has no potential on its own

29534.wylie: gal te skyes nas 'gag bzhin pa'i rnam shes kyis rang dang mthun pa'i 'bras bu'i don du, kun gzhi rnam shes la bag chags kyi nus pa'i khyad par bzhag pa
29534.english: Suppose that a consciousness which has grown—and is now in the act of stopping—deposits some type of potential, in the form of a deep seed, into the foundation consciousness—towards creating a result which corresponds to it.

29560.acip: MIG GI BLO STE RNAM PAR SHES PA SKYE BA'I RANG GI NUS PA BAG CHAGS GANG ZHIG KUN GZHI LA, RNAM SHES GZHAN GYIS RANG 'GAG BZHIN PA NA, DE MA THAG TU 'JOG PAR BYED LA,
29560.wylie: mig gi blo ste rnam par shes pa skye ba'i rang gi nus pa bag chags gang zhig kun gzhi la, rnam shes gzhan gyis rang 'gag bzhin pa na, de ma thag tu 'jog par byed la
29560.english: Let's look at how the awareness of the eye—which is to say, that consciousness—has the deep seed for it, that potential for it to grow, planted into the foundation consciousness. This is done by another instance of consciousness as it is in the act of ending, and occurs just after that.

This is done by another instance of consciousness as it is in the act of ending, and occurs just after that."}

29563.acip: DE LA MIG SHES SKYE BA'I RGYU BAG CHAGS NI DE'I RGYU'I RKYEN YIN LA, MIG GI DBANG PO NI MIG SHES KYI BDAG PO'I RKYEN NO,,
29563.wylie: de la mig shes skye ba'i rgyu bag chags ni de'i rgyu'i rkyen yin la, mig gi dbang po ni mig shes kyi bdag po'i rkyen no
29563.english: Here the deep seed which acts as the cause for the arisal of the visual consciousness is the causal factor for it; whereas the sense power of the eye is the dominant factor.
29563.raw: {"course": "ILL", "acip": "DE LA MIG SHES SKYE BA'I RGYU BAG CHAGS NI DE'I RGYU'I RKYEN YIN LA, MIG GI DBANG PO NI MIG SHES KYI BDAG PO'I RKYEN NO,,", "wylie": "de la mig shes skye ba'i rgyu bag chags ni de'i rgyu'i rkyen yin la, mig gi dbang po ni mig shes kyi bdag po'i rkyen no", "english": "Here the deep seed which acts as the cause for the arisal of the visual consciousness is the causal factor for it; whereas the sense power of the eye is the dominant factor."}

29564.acip: 'DIR MIG DBANG MIG SHES KYI DNGOS RGYUR BSTAN PA NI, MIG SHES SKYE BA'I BAG CHAGS SMIN PA'I SKABS LA DGONGS KYI MIG DBANG GANG YIN LA MIN NO,,
29564.wylie: 'dir mig dbang mig shes kyi dngos rgyur bstan pa ni, mig shes skye ba'i bag chags smin pa'i skabs la dgongs kyi mig dbang gang yin la min no
29564.english: When they describe here the sense power of the eye as the direct cause of the consciousness of the eye, what they have in mind is the point at which the deep seed for the visual consciousness ripens; it is not a reference to the power of the eye itself.
29564.raw: {"course": "ILL", "acip": "'DIR MIG DBANG MIG SHES KYI DNGOS RGYUR BSTAN PA NI, MIG SHES SKYE BA'I BAG CHAGS SMIN PA'I SKABS LA DGONGS KYI MIG DBANG GANG YIN LA MIN NO,,", "wylie": "'dir mig dbang mig shes kyi dngos rgyur bstan pa ni, mig shes skye ba'i bag chags smin pa'i skabs la dgongs kyi mig dbang gang yin la min no", "english": "When they describe here the sense power of the eye as the direct cause of the consciousness of the eye, what they have in mind is the point at which the deep seed for the visual consciousness ripens; it is not a reference to the power of the eye itself."}

29572.acip: BSHAD PA'I RNAM PA GCIG TU NA, RMI LAM NA NI GZUGS DON GZHAN DU GYUR PA MED PAR RANG GI BAG CHAGS KYI NUS PA SMIN PA LAS, GZUGS SGRA SOGS DE'I RNAM PA CAN GYI SEMS 'BYUNG BA JI LTA BA DE BZHIN DU, SAD PA'I SKABS LA'ANG 'DIR PHYI ROL GYI DON MED PAR YID NI YOD DO ZHE NA,
29572.wylie: bshad pa'i rnam pa gcig tu na, rmi lam na ni gzugs don gzhan du gyur pa med par rang gi bag chags kyi nus pa smin pa las, gzugs sgra sogs de'i rnam pa can gyi sems 'byung ba ji lta ba de bzhin du, sad pa'i skabs la'ang 'dir phyi rol gyi don med par yid ni yod do zhe na
29572.english: This explanation can take a different twist. In a dream, there are no physical objects which are other entities. Rather, the potential of a deep seed for them ripens, and from that arises a state of mind with the aspects of those visible forms, sounds, and the rest. In this very same way, here during the period when we are awake as well there are no outer objects here; what we have is the thought. Now suppose this is the position that you take. Denying Mind Only objects

29575.acip: DE NI MI RIGS TE, JI LTAR MIG DBANG MED PAR RMI LAM DU SNGO SOGS SNANG BA'I YID SHES KYI SEMS 'BYUNG BA DE LTAR DU, MIG DBANG MED PAR RNAM SHES RANG GI SA BON BAG CHAGS NI SMIN PA LAS, SAD PA'I LONG BA LA YANG MA LONG BA LTA BU'I GZUGS MTHONG BA SOGS CI'I PHYIR MI SKYE STE RMI LAM DANG SAD PA GNYIS KAR YANG MIG DBANG MED PAR MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
29575.wylie: de ni mi rigs te, ji ltar mig dbang med par rmi lam du sngo sogs snang ba'i yid shes kyi sems 'byung ba de ltar du, mig dbang med par rnam shes rang gi sa bon bag chags ni smin pa las, sad pa'i long ba la yang ma long ba lta bu'i gzugs mthong ba sogs ci'i phyir mi skye ste rmi lam dang sad pa gnyis kar yang mig dbang med par mtshungs pa'i phyir ro
29575.english: And yet, that position must be wrong. In a dream, a state of mind comes up which is actually consciousness of the thought, but which takes on an aspect of blue or whatever it may be, even though there is no sense power of the eye there. And suppose it were the same for consciousness, which in the absence of a sense power of the eye has a seed—a deep seed—within it which ripens. In this case, why wouldn't it be the case that—in the waking state—a person who was blind would come to see visible forms just the same as a person who was not blind? After all, the two cases are similar: they have no sense power of the eye, in both the cases: in the dream, and while awake.

29585.acip: DE'I PHYIR MIG MED PA SAD PA'I LONG BA 'DI LA DON SNANG GI BAG CHAGS SMIN PA RGYU MIN PA JI LTA BA DE LTAR RMI LAM DU YANG GNYID NI DON SNANG GI BAG CHAGS SMIN PA'I RGYU MA YIN TE, PHYI ROL MED PAR SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA SKYE NA BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LA MI LTOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
29585.wylie: de'i phyir mig med pa sad pa'i long ba 'di la don snang gi bag chags smin pa rgyu min pa ji lta ba de ltar rmi lam du yang gnyid ni don snang gi bag chags smin pa'i rgyu ma yin te, phyi rol med par shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa skye na bag chags smin pa la mi ltos pa'i phyir ro
29585.english: As such, it's not as if things are happening here as they do when there is no eye: where, for this person who is blind during the waking state, the ripening of a deep seed for the mind to take on the appearance of the object is not acting as a cause. Just so, in a dream as well, sleep could not be a cause for the ripening of the deep seed of the mind taking on the aspect of the object. And that's because—if it were the case that a state of mind that existed through some nature of its own could grow in the absence of outer objects, then it wouldn't have to rely upon the ripening of some deep seed.

29586.acip: GANG GI PHYIR BAG CHAGS BRDZUN PA LAS RMI LAM GYI DON SNANG GI SHES PA BRDZUN PA SKYE BA DE'I PHYIR, RMI LAM DU YANG SAD PA'I SKABS DE LTA BU'I YUL GYI DNGOS PO GZUGS SOGS SU SNANG BA'I RNAM PAR SHES PA BRDZUN PA DANG, RMI LAM GYI MIG RTOGS PA STE RNAM PAR SHES PA'I RGYU STE RTEN DU GYUR PA KHAS BLANG BAR BYA'O,,
29586.wylie: gang gi phyir bag chags brdzun pa las rmi lam gyi don snang gi shes pa brdzun pa skye ba de'i phyir, rmi lam du yang sad pa'i skabs de lta bu'i yul gyi dngos po gzugs sogs su snang ba'i rnam par shes pa brdzun pa dang, rmi lam gyi mig rtogs pa ste rnam par shes pa'i rgyu ste rten du gyur pa khas blang bar bya'o
29586.english: Suppose then that a false state of mind which takes on the aspect of an object in a dream arises from a false version of a deep seed. For that reason then, you would also have to accept the idea that in a dream as well—just as in that waking state—there would be a false consciousness that was taking on the aspect of visible form and such: these types of entities acting as the same sort of objects. And these would act as the cause—which is to say, the support—for the consciousness or perception of the eye in the dream.

31228.acip: SHES BYA THAMS CAD YANG DAG PA PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR RDZOGS PAR TE MA LUS PAR SANGS RGYAS PA STE THUGS SU CHUD DO, ZHES ZHAL GYIS BZHES PA DANG, NGA ZAG PA BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA ZAD DO ZHES PA DANG, NGAS CHAGS SOGS THAR PA'I BAR DU GCOD PA'I CHOS YIN NO ZHES PA DANG, SA LAM 'DI LA NAN TAN DU BYAS NA SDUG BSNGAL ZAD PAR 'GYUR RO ZHES DAM BCAS PA BZHI LA DE LTAR MIN NO,
31228.wylie: shes bya thams cad yang dag pa phyin ci ma log par rdzogs par te ma lus par sangs rgyas pa ste thugs su chud do, zhes zhal gyis bzhes pa dang, nga zag pa bag chags dang bcas pa zad do zhes pa dang, ngas chags sogs thar pa'i bar du gcod pa'i chos yin no zhes pa dang, sa lam 'di la nan tan du byas na sdug bsngal zad par 'gyur ro zhes dam bcas pa bzhi la de ltar min no
31228.english: Here we have the statement about the four declarations: It is not so with these. First there is the declaration that “I have reached that comprehension; I am enlightened towards all the knowable things there are; I grasp each and every one of them, unerringly, and in their entirety.” Then there is the declaration that “I have finished off all impurity, along with the deep seeds for this impurity.” Next there is the declaration, “I assert that craving and the like are things which act as an obstacle to freedom.” And then finally we have the declaration that “If you make devoted efforts in these levels & paths, you will come to the end of your pain.”

31499.acip: BDEN 'DZIN GYI BAG CHAGS MA LUS PA ZAD DE SANGS RGYAS PA NAS DUS RTAG TU DON DAM BDEN PA MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG LA BZHUGS PAS, DE LAS BZHENGS PA'I MNYAM RJES RES 'JOG MED PA'I PHYIR DANG,
31499.wylie: bden 'dzin gyi bag chags ma lus pa zad de sangs rgyas pa nas dus rtag tu don dam bden pa mngon sum du rtogs pa'i mnyam gzhag la bzhugs pas, de las bzhengs pa'i mnyam rjes res 'jog med pa'i phyir dang
31499.english: Then comes a point when we are able to finish off all of the deep seeds for the tendency to hold things as being real, and reach our own enlightenment. From this time on, we are forever in a deep meditation where we are perceiving, directly, ultimate reality. As such, we no longer engage in a successive state, in the sense of first being in deep meditation and then coming out into what is termed the “aftermath” of that meditation.

31503.acip: GANG GI TSE CHOS CAN LA LTOS TE JI SNYED PA MKHYEN PAR SONG BA DE'I TSE, YUL YUL CAN SO SOR SNANG BA'I GNYIS SNANG YOD KYANG, GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL BA'I BAG CHAGS DRUNGS PHYUNG BAS SNANG YUL LA MA 'KHRUL BA'I GNYIS SNANG YIN GYI 'KHRUL BA'I GNYIS SNANG MIN TE, 'DI MA 'KHRUL BA'I TSUL GZHAN DU LEGS PAR BSHAD ZIN TO,,
31503.wylie: gang gi tshe chos can la ltos te ji snyed pa mkhyen par song ba de'i tshe, yul yul can so sor snang ba'i gnyis snang yod kyang, gnyis snang 'khrul ba'i bag chags drungs phyung bas snang yul la ma 'khrul ba'i gnyis snang yin gyi 'khrul ba'i gnyis snang min te, 'di ma 'khrul ba'i tshul gzhan du legs par bshad zin to
31503.english: At some point, relative to the object at hand, our state of mind passes into the knowledge of all the things there are. At this stage, there is present a duality in the sense of the object and the subject state of mind appearing as two different things. By now though we have torn out, from its very roots, the deep seed for error involving duality. As such, we can say that here we have a sense of duality which is not mistaken about the object which is appearing to it; but which is not that sense of duality which is in error. The exact way in which this mental state is not mistaken is something that I have covered quite nicely elsewhere.

31668.acip: ,RNAM KUN MKHYEN PA'I STOBS KYIS MYUR DU RGYAL RNAMS KYI, ,NYON MONGS DAG NI BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS 'JIG 'GYUR DANG, ,SLOB MA LA SOGS NYON MONGS BLO YIS 'GOG PA GANG, ,DE LA MKHYEN [218a] PA CHAGS MED MTHA' YAS STOBS SU 'DOD,
31668.wylie: rnam kun mkhyen pa'i stobs kyis myur du rgyal rnams kyi, ,nyon mongs dag ni bag chags dang bcas 'jig 'gyur dang, ,slob ma la sogs nyon mongs blo yis 'gog pa gang, ,de la mkhyen [218a] pa chags med mtha' yas stobs su 'dod
31668.english: The Victors, Who know all Things there are, Use these forces— With speed— To destroy the Negative emotions, Along with the Deep seeds. Those who are students, And the rest, put a stop To the negative emotions Using their intelligence [f. 218a]; This then constitutes A state of knowledge Which is free of density, And this is what We refer to as the Force of the infinite.

31669.acip: RNAM PA KUN MKHYEN PA'I RGYAL BA RNAMS KYI STOBS KYIS CHAGS SOGS NYON MONGS PA DAG NI, BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA THAMS CAD 'JIG PA STE BCOM PAR 'GYUR BA DANG,
31669.wylie: rnam pa kun mkhyen pa'i rgyal ba rnams kyi stobs kyis chags sogs nyon mongs pa dag ni, bag chags dang bcas pa thams cad 'jig pa ste bcom par 'gyur ba dang
31669.english: The Victors, who know all things there are, use these forces to “destroy,” or conquer—“every one of them”—referring to everything involved with the negative emotions, attachment and the rest, along with the deep seeds for these.

31673.acip: 'DIR NYON MONGS PA'I BAG CHAGS NI, 'GREL PA LAS, GANG GIS SEMS KYI RGYUD 'BAGS PAR BYED CING BSGO BAR BYED LA, RJES SU BGROD PAR BYED PA DE NI BAG CHAGS TE, NYON MONGS PA'I MUR THUG PA DANG, GOMS PA DANG, RTZA BA DANG, BAG CHAGS ZHES BYA BA NI RNAM GRANGS DAG GO, ZHES GSUNGS SHING,
31673.wylie: 'dir nyon mongs pa'i bag chags ni, 'grel pa las, gang gis sems kyi rgyud 'bags par byed cing bsgo bar byed la, rjes su bgrod par byed pa de ni bag chags te, nyon mongs pa'i mur thug pa dang, goms pa dang, rtsa ba dang, bag chags zhes bya ba ni rnam grangs dag go, zhes gsungs shing
31673.english: What does it mean when we refer here to “deep seeds for everything involved with the negative emotions”? The autocommentary puts it this way: What we refer to as a “deep seed” here is that thing which functions to infect the mind; to stain the mind; to trigger influences that take us on. For everything involved with the negative emotions, we can say that the terms “final destination”; and “habit”; and “root”; and “deep seed” are all synonymous.

31676.english: Now according to the present system, the tendency to hold that things are themselves is considered a negative emotion. As such, we would have to say that the most serious of the obstacles to omniscience is the deep seed for the mistake of a perceptual inconsistency.

31680.english: As for the extremely subtle form of the deep seeds here, that point at which the uninterrupted path of the final period in the flow of the tenth level is approaching its arisal, and the point at which the stopping of these extremely subtle forms is just approaching, occur simultaneously. And the path of liberation in which we have first eliminated these represents the first moment of the high knowledge of an Enlightened Being.

31795.acip: DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON ZAB MO SNGAR BSHAD ZIN PA 'JIGS SU RUNG BA 'DI NI SKYE BO YIS, SNGON TSE RABS GZHAN DU STONG PA NYID LA LHAG PAR MOS PA'I BAG CHAGS GOMS PA NYID LAS NGES PAR RTOGS PAR 'GYUR BA SNANG NGO,,

31795.english: Let us consider then this profound idea of suchness, which we have finished explaining here, and which is in fact likely to be frightening. There are individuals who have, in their past—during their previous lifetimes—become highly accustomed to deep seeds created by their intense aspiration for emptiness. And it would certainly appear that, because of these seeds, they did have such realizations.

31797.acip: JI LTAR GZHAN SDE SNGON SEMS RGYUD LA STONG NYID LA LHAG PAR MOS PA'I BAG CHAGS MA BZHAG PA RNAMS KYIS MNGON PA NAS BSHAD PA LTAR SRID RTZE MA GTOGS PA'I KHAMS GSUM GYI NYON MONGS MNGON GYUR RE ZHIG SPANGS SHING, GRUB PA'I MTHA' GZHAN NYE BAR SBYOR NUS PAR MTHONG YANG,
31797.wylie: ji ltar gzhan sde sngon sems rgyud la stong nyid la lhag par mos pa'i bag chags ma bzhag pa rnams kyis mngon pa nas bshad pa ltar srid rtse ma gtogs pa'i khams gsum gyi nyon mongs mngon gyur re zhig spangs shing, grub pa'i mtha' gzhan nye bar sbyor nus par mthong yang
31797.english: And so let's consider members of these other groups, who may not have—at some prior point in time—planted any deep seeds inside their mindstreams that would make them feel some strong aspiration towards emptiness. As explained in the texts on higher knowledge, they might still be able to eliminate—for a certain amount of time—different negative emotions for all three of the realms, except for that level known as the Peak of Existence. And we might observe them being able to apply themselves to other philosophical systems.

34280.acip: CHOS BYANG CHUB LAM GYI RIM PA 'DI LAS ZAB CING RGYA CHE BA NI GZHAN DAG GI CHOS, ZAB ZAB MO DANG RTOGS PA MTHO MTHO MO YIN ZER BA TSO LA'ANG MED PAS GCOD DANG BSKYED RDZOGS RTZA RLUNG THIG LE PHYAG CHEN RDZOGS CHEN SOGS GSANG CHEN SNGAGS KYI YANG RTZE SGROGS PA ZHIG MNGON DU BYED PA SKAD ZER KYANG BYANG CHUB LAM RIM 'DI LA MA BRTEN NA LAM YONGS RDZOGS RGYUD LA SKYE BA LTA CI BAG CHAGS TZAM YANG 'JOG PAR MI NUS
34280.wylie: chos byang chub lam gyi rim pa 'di las zab cing rgya che ba ni gzhan dag gi chos, zab zab mo dang rtogs pa mtho mtho mo yin zer ba tsho la'ang med pas gcod dang bskyed rdzogs rtsa rlung thig le phyag chen rdzogs chen sogs gsang chen sngags kyi yang rtse sgrogs pa zhig mngon du byed pa skad zer kyang byang chub lam rim 'di la ma brten na lam yongs rdzogs rgyud la skye ba lta ci bag chags tsam yang 'jog par mi nus
34280.english: Could any system be more profound or far-reaching than this Dharma, the Steps of the Path? Certainly not those teachings that others claimare oh-so-deep, or oh-so-high and inscrutable. People chatter about attaining some realization, some supposed zenith of some very secret way: they talk of termination; they talk about the levels of creation and completion; about the channels and winds and drops; the great seal, or the great completion, whatever. But if one never makes use of these very Steps, he can never even plant the seeds, much less bring the path in full to grow within his mind.

34376.acip: DE LTAR DAM SDOM LA GNAS PA'I 'OG TU JI LTAR BYA DGOS SNYAM NA RGYAL BA'I DBANG PO, BSKAL BZANG RGYA MTSOS, LAR SKYE 'CHI BAR DO GANG LA YANG DUS DA LTA'I BAG CHAGS GTZO CHE BAS DE SPYOD BYED BSKYED RDZOGS RNAL 'BYOR GYIS SKYABS SKU GSUM RANG NGO SHES BAR MDZOD
34376.wylie: de ltar dam sdom la gnas pa'i 'og tu ji ltar bya dgos snyam na rgyal ba'i dbang po, bskal bzang rgya mtshos, lar skye 'chi bar do gang la yang dus da lta'i bag chags gtso che bas de spyod byed bskyed rdzogs rnal 'byor gyis skyabs sku gsum rang ngo shes bar mdzod
34376.english: One may wonder, "Suppose I am able to maintain my vows and pledges; what must I do after that?" The highest of Victors, Kelsang Gyatso, has spoken the following: The point May be birth or death or the state between them. The time Most important for planting their seeds is now. The way To transformthemis the practice of creation and completion. The refuge You must learn is the three final bodies themselves.

34394.acip: NYUNG MTHA' YANG GZHUNG 'DI TZAM GYI TSIG DON LA 'DRIS PAR BYAS TE BSHAR SGOM, GYIS BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA TSUN LA NAN TAN DU 'BAD PA DANG

34853.english: In actuality, all these things are completely beyond the realm of possibility; there is no chance that they could have really happened. They had about as much reality as a sketch done with a single hair; you have to realize that this pose of being a bodhisattva with roots of non-virtue and then sitting under the tree there was a total impossibility. A being Gone Thus, one who possesses each and every virtuous quality, has eliminated each and every non-virtue; so too have they eliminated the very trace of even the seeds for negativity. How on earth then could One Thus Gone ever have any problem with some karmic obstacle?

34895.acip: 'O NA MTHONG LAM BAR CHAD MED LAM GYI DUS SU DE'I SPANG BYA MTHONG SPANG MED MOD KYANG, SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL YOD DGOS LA DE'I TSE YID KYI SHES PA NI GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS MA BSLAD PA'I ZAG MED YIN PAS DE'I NGO BOR BAG LA NYAL DE GNAS PA MI RIGS LA DBANG SHES KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MED CING GZUGS KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MI RIGS LA KUN GZHI YANG MI 'DOD PAS DE'I RTEN MED PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM NA SKYON MED DE DE'I TSE NGA TZAM ZHIG SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL GYI RTEN YIN PA'I PHYIR TE SPANG GNYEN GZHAN LA YANG DE BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA'O
34895.wylie: 'o na mthong lam bar chad med lam gyi dus su de'i spang bya mthong spang med mod kyang, sgom spang gi bag la nyal yod dgos la de'i tshe yid kyi shes pa ni gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags kyis ma bslad pa'i zag med yin pas de'i ngo bor bag la nyal de gnas pa mi rigs la dbang shes kyang de'i rten du med cing gzugs kyang de'i rten du mi rigs la kun gzhi yang mi 'dod pas de'i rten med par 'gyur ro snyam na skyon med de de'i tshe nga tsam zhig sgom spang gi bag la nyal gyi rten yin pa'i phyir te spang gnyen gzhan la yang de bzhin du shes par bya'o
34895.english: One might wonder about something else: Let's talk about the period while you are in the "uninterrupted" stage of the path of seeing [the actual direct perception of emptiness]. I can accept that at this point the negative thoughts eliminated by this path are no longer present, but we would have to say that the negative things eliminated by the path of habituation are still there, in a dormant way. At this particular point in time, the consciousness of the mind is unstained, unaffected by the mental seed which causes the mistaken state of mind where the appearance and actuality of things are different from one another. As such none of these things could lie dormant here, due to its very quality at the time. There is no consciousness of the senses that could act as the basis for those mental seeds, and it would be improper to say that physical form could ever provide such a basis either. According to you, moreover, there's no foundation consciousness. I would have to think then that there is no basis at all where these dormant things And yet there is no such problem, for at this point in time it is the simple "me" which is providing the basis for the dormant things eliminated by the path of habituation to stay. You can apply this reasoning as well to all the other cases involving things to be eliminated, and the antidotes which eliminate them. Selection Three: The Middle-Way School on the question of where the seeds of karma stay until they give their result

34922.acip: SKYON MED DE DE LTA BU'I BRGAL LAN JI SNYED CIG BYAS PA THAMS CAD PHYI DON 'GOG, PA'I DBANG DU BYAS PA'I PHYIR PHYI DON 'GOG PA'I TSUL YANG YOD DE SNGON PO PHYI ROL DON DU GRUB NA TSUR MTHONG GI RGYUD KYI SNGON 'DZIN DBANG PO'I MNGON SUM LA SNGON PO SNANG BA NA SNGON 'DZIN SNGA MA 'GAGS PA'I TSE SNGON 'DZIN PHYI MA SKYE BA'I BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA SMIN PA LA BRTEN NAS SNANG BA MA YIN PAR SNGON PO PHYI ROL NAS RANG 'DRA'I RNAM PA GTAD PA'I SGO NAS SNANG BA YIN NA 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS NAS DNGOS PO GSUM SNANG BA DE'I TSE NA RANG RANG GI LAS KYIS BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA SMIN PA LA MA BLTOS PAR DNGOS PO GSUM PO DE RANG 'DRA'I RNAM PA GTAD PA'I SGO NAS SNANG DGOS
34922.wylie: skyon med de de lta bu'i brgal lan ji snyed cig byas pa thams cad phyi don 'gog, pa'i dbang du byas pa'i phyir phyi don 'gog pa'i tshul yang yod de sngon po phyi rol don du grub na tshur mthong gi rgyud kyi sngon 'dzin dbang po'i mngon sum la sngon po snang ba na sngon 'dzin snga ma 'gags pa'i tshe sngon 'dzin phyi ma skye ba'i bag chags bzhag pa smin pa la brten nas snang ba ma yin par sngon po phyi rol nas rang 'dra'i rnam pa gtad pa'i sgo nas snang ba yin na 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas nas dngos po gsum snang ba de'i tshe na rang rang gi las kyis bag chags bzhag pa smin pa la ma bltos par dngos po gsum po de rang 'dra'i rnam pa gtad pa'i sgo nas snang dgos
34922.english: And yet there is no such problem. No matter how many arguments of this kind you want to present, they are all made from the point of view of denying the existence of external objects. The way these arguments go is as follows. If the color blue were to exist as an external object, then the following would occur when this color appeared directly to a sense perception grasping blue; that is, with such a perception found in the mental stream of one of those who "only sees this side" [which is another name for those who have not yet perceived emptiness directly]. When an earlier instance of the perception of blue ends, what actually happens is that it plants a mental seed which eventually grows into a later instance of the same perception of blue, when the seed ripens. Suppose the blue were not just this kind of appearance, but rather an appearance where blue as an outer object were transmitting a likeness of itself and thereby appearing to one's perceptions. Something else then would be happening when the three different beings sit down together and look at the glass full of something wet and flowing. The three different objects would be appearing to them because each of the objects was transmitting a likeness of itself to their perception. All of this would be happening independent of any process where each being's karma planted a mental seed, which later ripened and produced the appearance of the

22072.english: And just how is it so wondrous? 9896.acip: ,DUG LNGA YI NYON MONGS MTSANG RIG KYANG , ,NGAN GOMS KYI BAG CHAGS SHUGS DRAG CING , ,GDONG ZLOG GI GNYEN PO NGAR CHUNG BAS, ,MNAR MED KYI ME NANG SREG NYEN GDA'O,
9896.wylie: dug lnga yi nyon mongs mtshang rig kyang , ,ngan goms kyi bag chags shugs drag cing , ,gdong zlog gi gnyen po ngar chung bas, ,mnar med kyi me nang sreg nyen gda'o
9896.english: Oh I'm perfectly aware Of the faults within my heart-- The negative thoughts, the poisons five; But the seeds I have from living with them, The simple habit of wrongness so strong-- And the antidote to them so fragile, So little able to face these thoughts, So impotent to turn them away-- There is danger That I will burn in the realms of hell. [Translator's note: The five mental-affliction poisons are listed as ignorant liking of things; ignorant disliking of things; dark ignorance itself; pride; and jealousy.]

11050.english: (Here is what the real Fourth Initiation is.  It is the indivisible Union of the Two, within a person who has finished all learning. The second of the two is this same wisdom manifesting itself as a holy body, with faces and arms, adorned with all the marks and signs of an Enlightened Being.)

11904.acip: DE NI DE KHO NA NYID THUGS SU CHUD CING SGRIB GNYIS BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA SPANGS PAS NA SANGS RGYAS TE RNAM SNANG LA SOGS PA DANG 'DZIN PAS NA CHOS TE LUNG DANG RTOGS PA DANG 'DUS PAS NA DGE 'DUN TE 'JAM DPAL LA SOGS PA'I BYANG SEMS RNAMS DKON PA'I NANG NAS GTZO BO YIN PAS NA MCHOG YIN LA DES NA BLA NA MED PA STE DE GSUM LA SKYABS SU 'GRO BA LA SOGS PA'O,
11904.wylie: de ni de kho na nyid thugs su chud cing sgrib gnyis bag chags dang bcas pa spangs pas na sangs rgyas te rnam snang la sogs pa dang 'dzin pas na chos te lung dang rtogs pa dang 'dus pas na dge 'dun te 'jam dpal la sogs pa'i byang sems rnams dkon pa'i nang nas gtso bo yin pas na mchog yin la des na bla na med pa ste de gsum la skyabs su 'gro ba la sogs pa'o
11904.english: The Angel of Appearances and the rest are all the Jewel of the Buddha [one who has reached jang-chub, or enlightenment], in the sense that they have grasped [chub] suchness perfectly, and have eliminated [jang] both types of obstacles, along with the mental seeds for these obstacles. There is the Jewel of the Dharma here as well, in that they hold [a reference to dhir, the Sanskrit root of the word "Dharma" which means "to hold"] the teachings, both in the form of the physical books and the mental realizations. In that they combine [du, related to dun] these two previous Jewels, these Angels are also the Jewel [kon-chok] of the Community [gen-dun]; and this in itself is what makes bodhisattvas like Gentle Voice the highest [chok] beings of all: the rarest of the rare [kon].  Thus it is that we go for shelter to the "unsurpassed," meaning these three Jewels. ***

12552.acip: BDAG BYIN RLABS PA'I BSHAD PA LAS, YID LA BYED TSUL GTAM TZAM YANG RNYED DKA' BA'I DON DE SGYU LUS MA GRUB KYANG 'DI'I GDAMS NGAG PHYIN CI MA LOG PA RNYED NA DA LTA NAS GOMS PAS NAM ZHIG NA SGYU MA'I SKU 'JA' LUS RDO RJE SEMS DPA'I GO 'PHANG 'GRUB PA'I BAG CHAGS THUN MONG MA YIN PA 'JOG BYED DU SNANG BAS SHIN TU NGO MTSAR BA'I GNAS SO,,
12552.wylie: bdag byin rlabs pa'i bshad pa las, yid la byed tshul gtam tsam yang rnyed dka' ba'i don de sgyu lus ma grub kyang 'di'i gdams ngag phyin ci ma log pa rnyed na da lta nas goms pas nam zhig na sgyu ma'i sku 'ja' lus rdo rje sems dpa'i go 'phang 'grub pa'i bag chags thun mong ma yin pa 'jog byed du snang bas shin tu ngo mtshar ba'i gnas so
12552.english: This is also described in the treatise called The Blessing of Oneself, where our Lord grants us the following holy words-- Here's the point of saying that it's a difficult thing to come across even a discussion that gets you thinking about these things.  Suppose that--even if you are unable right now to attain the body of illusion--you do come across some unmistaken instructions for doing so.  If right now you begin to habituate yourself to these teachings, then you will see that it acts to plant a unique type of mental seed which will allow you, at a certain point in the future, to actually reach the body of illusion: the rainbow body, the state of the Warrior of Diamond himself.  This is an incredible thing.

12703.english: The four types of drops also reside, respectively, as before, in the four places of the navel, the secret place, the middle of the jewel, and the tip of the jewel.  It is stated that two different mental seeds create the waking state and the state of the fourth at the navel; and that these seeds exist with a single drop--but not that they are separate drops.

12708.acip: LUGS 'DIR SGRIB PA THAMS CAD RIGS BZHI'I SGRIB PAR 'DUS LA, SGRIB PA'I MTSAN GZHIR THIG LE DE RNAMS BSHAD PA NI, THIG LE DE RNAMS LA GNAS PA'I SHIN TU PHRA BA'I RLUNG SEMS RNAMS SGRIB PA'I BAG CHAGS BGO GZHI YIN PA LA DGONGS PAR GSUNGS SO,,

12708.english: In this system, all our spiritual obstacles are subsumed within the obstacles relating to these four types of drops.  The drops then are said to be the expression of these obstacles. 12912.acip: BDUN PA 'GRO BA DAG PA'I RNAL 'BYOR NI, RANG GI SNYING GAR CHOS 'BYUNG DMAR PO GRU GSUM NYIS BRTZEGS KYI NANG DU ZLA BA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI DBUS SU BAm YIG LA SNGAGS 'PHRENG GIS BSKOR BA LAS 'OD ZER 'PHROS TE, BA SPU'I BU GA NAS PHAR SONG , RIGS DRUG GI SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA PHOG PAS SDIG SGRIB BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA SBYANGS, DE THAMS CAD RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA'I SKUR GYUR PAR BSAM,
12912.wylie: bdun pa 'gro ba dag pa'i rnal 'byor ni, rang gi snying gar chos 'byung dmar po gru gsum nyis brtsegs kyi nang du zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi dbus su baM yig la sngags 'phreng gis bskor ba las 'od zer 'phros te, ba spu'i bu ga nas phar song , rigs drug gi sems can thams cad la phog pas sdig sgrib bag chags dang bcas pa sbyangs, de thams cad rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i skur gyur par bsam
12912.english: (Now begin number seven, the Practice of Making All Beings Pure:) In my heart is a dharma star, It is red, made of two Triangular parts stacked together. Inside the star is a moondisk, And in the center of the disk Is a letter vam, surrounded by A string of secret words. Light goes forth from them And leaves from the pores of my skin; It flies and strikes Every living being Of all of the six kinds. The light cleans them Of their wrong deeds and obstacles, Along with the seeds for these. They all turn into The Angel of the Diamond.

14246.acip: YID BZHIN GYI NOR BU 'BUM PHRAG RNYED KYANG TSE 'DIR PHRAN BU LAS PHAN GNOD MED KYANG, RTEN 'DIS NYIN GCIG LA'ANG YAR SANGS RGYAS PA ZHIG DANG, DE TZAM MA BYUNG YANG, BSAGS SBYANG DANG, BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA TSUN BYAR YOD,
14246.wylie: yid bzhin gyi nor bu 'bum phrag rnyed kyang tshe 'dir phran bu las phan gnod med kyang, rten 'dis nyin gcig la'ang yar sangs rgyas pa zhig dang, de tsam ma byung yang, bsags sbyang dang, bag chags 'jog pa tshun byar yod
14246.english: Suppose you discovered hundreds of thousands of precious jewels, jewels that could grant you any wish.  They would be no big help or harm to you, except for a little something in this world.  But the life you now possess can, at the best, give you your own Enlightenment in a single day.  And even if you can't reach that goal, this life can still give you the chance to collect good deeds and purify your wrong ones, or to plant good spiritual seeds in your mind, and every other good beyond all these.

14879.acip: DE GNYIS LA MCHOG DMAN GYI KHYAD PAR GTAN NAS MED DE, DPA' BO RJO RJE CHOS RTOGS PA DMA' BA YOD DAM SNYAM NA DE MIN TE, DPA' BO THAMS CAD KYI MCHOG SGRIB GNYIS BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA LAS DPA' BA'I SANGS RGYAS YIN PAS NA, DPA' BO MCHOG GI SPYOD YUL CAN ZHES SOGS 'BYUNG BA'I RGYU MTSAN DU MA YOD,
14879.wylie: de gnyis la mchog dman gyi khyad par gtan nas med de, dpa' bo rjo rje chos rtogs pa dma' ba yod dam snyam na de min te, dpa' bo thams cad kyi mchog sgrib gnyis bag chags dang bcas pa las dpa' ba'i sangs rgyas yin pas na, dpa' bo mchog gi spyod yul can zhes sogs 'byung ba'i rgyu mtshan du ma yod
14879.english: Now of these two visualizations, it is absolutely not the case that one is higher than the other.  You may think that the Warrior Diamond Dharma might have lesser realizations, but it is not so.  He is the highest of all warriors, for he is a Buddha who has won the war over the two obstacles, along with the seeds for these obstacles.  There are thus many reasons why we see lines such as those which mention the "supreme vision of Warriors supreme."

15155.acip: DE LA BRTEN NAS 'OG MIN GYI RNAL 'BYOR MA SOGS KYANG GLING GZHAN LA MI 'BYON PAR 'DZAM BU GLING GI RNAL 'BYOR PHO MO BYIN GYIS RLOB CING GROGS MDZAD CING, DE'I PHYIR LAM SNA MA ZIN PAS TSE GCIG LA SANGS RGYAS THOB NA 'DZAM BU GLING GI MI MNGAL SKYES KHAMS DRUG LDAN PA YIN PAS KHYAB CING, DMIGS BSAL SNGON GYI BAG CHAGS SAD PA RE GNYIS GZUGS KHAMS SOGS LA'ANG 'BYUNG NGO,
15155.wylie: de la brten nas 'og min gyi rnal 'byor ma sogs kyang gling gzhan la mi 'byon par 'dzam bu gling gi rnal 'byor pho mo byin gyis rlob cing grogs mdzad cing, de'i phyir lam sna ma zin pas tshe gcig la sangs rgyas thob na 'dzam bu gling gi mi mngal skyes khams drug ldan pa yin pas khyab cing, dmigs bsal sngon gyi bag chags sad pa re gnyis gzugs khams sogs la'ang 'byung ngo
15155.english: Due to all this, Angels of Diamond from the Paradise Below No Other don't bother going to other continents.  Rather they come to yogis and yoginis who live in this world of the Jambudvipa, to bless us and befriend us.   We can say then that--if a person who is not already very far along in the path manages to achieve enlightenment within a single lifetime--then they are necessarily someone who is a human, born from the womb, and possessed of the six elements.  There are only very occasional exceptions to this rule: a person or two in the form realm who has seeds from past lives that suddenly ripen, and then they reach Buddhahood.

15279.acip: 'GRO RNAMS BDEN STONG MNYAM PA NYID DU GZIGS PA'I YE SHES KYI SNANG BA 'BAR BAS SGRIB GNYIS BAG CHAGS BCAS BCOM PA'AM BSREGS PAR MTSON PHYIR SKU LAS DUS MTHA'I ME LTA BU'I 'OD ZER DMAR PO 'PHRO ZHING NYI MA 'BUM GYI GZI BRJID DANG LDAN PA,
15279.wylie: 'gro rnams bden stong mnyam pa nyid du gzigs pa'i ye shes kyi snang ba 'bar bas sgrib gnyis bag chags bcas bcom pa'am bsregs par mtshon phyir sku las dus mtha'i me lta bu'i 'od zer dmar po 'phro zhing nyi ma 'bum gyi gzi brjid dang ldan pa
15279.english: Her holy body bursts forth in shafts of crimson light, like the fire of the days of the end of the world, awesome as a million suns shining at once.  This represents the bright burning flame of Her wisdom, which looks upon all living creatures and sees them all the same, empty of any true nature.  The wisdom incinerates, it obliviates, the two obstacles to enlightenment, along with their every seed.

15665.acip: DBANG PHYUG PHUN TSOGS NI SGRIB GNYIS BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA SPANGS SHING GZHAN DBANG DU MA GYUR PA'O, ,GZUGS BZANG NI GONG NA MED PA'I MTSAN DPE'O, ,GRAGS PA NI PHYOGS DUS KUN TU SNYAN PAS KHYAB PA'O, ,DPAL NI 'JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS PA'I PHUN TSOGS 'DOD PA THAMS CAD KYIS BRTAN PAR BYAS PA'O, ,YE SHES NI SHES BYA THAMS CAD LA CHAGS THOGS MED PAR 'JUG PA'O, ,BRTZON 'GRUS NI LHUN GYIS GRUB PA DANG RGYUN MI CHAD PAR GSUNG GIS 'DOMS PA'O,
15665.wylie: dbang phyug phun tshogs ni sgrib gnyis bag chags dang bcas pa spangs shing gzhan dbang du ma gyur pa'o, ,gzugs bzang ni gong na med pa'i mtshan dpe'o, ,grags pa ni phyogs dus kun tu snyan pas khyab pa'o, ,dpal ni 'jig rten las 'das pa'i phun tshogs 'dod pa thams cad kyis brtan par byas pa'o, ,ye shes ni shes bya thams cad la chags thogs med par 'jug pa'o, ,brtson 'grus ni lhun gyis grub pa dang rgyun mi chad par gsung gis 'doms pa'o
15665.english: The phrase "total lord of power" refers to having eliminated both the obstacles, together with all their seeds, and to the fact that one will never again come under their domination. The words "excellent form" refer to the marks and signs on the body of a Buddha, for no higher form exists. "Renown" means that one's fame has reached to every place, and every time that there is. "Glory" refers to the total excellence of having transcended the world, reinforced by achieving all ones' wishes. "Wisdom" is the ability of the mind to engage in every knowable thing that exists, without the slightest obstruction. "Effort" means to give instruction, with words that are totally spontaneous, in an unbroken flow.

15678.english: The Holy Angel is terror to all these demons, and She scorches them with Her fire She splits their skulls apart.  By force of these mighty deeds She overcomes the two obstacles, and all their seeds as well.

15930.wylie: de yang baM yig sngags phreng dang bcas pa las 'od zer dmar po dpag med 'phros, lus dkyil gyi gtso mo'i nang thams cad gang ba spu'i sgo nas 'phros, rang gi lus thams cad 'od zer gyis gang, tshe rabs thog med nas bsags pa'i nad gdon sdig sgrib bag chags dang bcas pa thams cad sbyangs
15930.english: Crimson rays of light fly out from the vam syllable and the string of secret words.  First they fill the body of the central Angel of the secret world of the body, and then begin to come out of the pores of Her skin.  The light then fills your own body, and cleanses you of all the sickness-causing demons, bad deeds, and obstacles--together with every one of their seeds--which you have collected over lives without beginning.

15932.acip: SKABS 'GAR 'OD ZER GYI SNE LA RNAL 'BYOR MA SPROS TE KHA tV'Am GA YAB TU GYUR NAS SEMS CAN RNAMS KYI SPYI BOR SNYOMS 'JUG BYAS PA'I BDUD RTZI'I RGYUN BABS PAS SDIG SGRIB BAG CHAGS THAMS CAD SBYANG PAR BSAM,

15932.english: [1] Sometimes you can picture that on the tips of the light rays, you send out the Angel of Diamond.  She flies to the tip of the head of each living being, Her khatvanga staff turns into Her Husband, and She joins into union with Him.  From Them comes down a stream of pure nectar which purifies each being of all their bad deeds and obstacles, along with all of the seeds for them.

15942.acip: SER PO LAS BDE CHEN NAM DAM TSIG GI 'KHOR LO'I TSOGS SPROS TE SEMS CAN NGA RGYAL DANG SER SNA SHAS CHE BA RNAMS DANG, LJANG KHU LAS SGO MTSAMS MA SPROS TE, SEMS CAN PHRAG DOG SHAS CHE BA RNAMS KYI SDIG SGRIB BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA THAMS CAD SBYANGS TE RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MAR GYUR TE RANG LA THIM PAR BSAM,
15942.wylie: ser po las bde chen nam dam tshig gi 'khor lo'i tshogs spros te sems can nga rgyal dang ser sna shas che ba rnams dang, ljang khu las sgo mtshams ma spros te, sems can phrag dog shas che ba rnams kyi sdig sgrib bag chags dang bcas pa thams cad sbyangs te rdo rje rnal 'byor mar gyur te rang la thim par bsam
15942.english: On rays of yellow light send out the group of the Angels of pledge, or of great bliss, to help those who have a problem with pride or stinginess.  On rays of green light send out the Angels of the gates and corners to help those whose main problem is with jealousy.  Picture that these Angels purify them of all their bad deeds, obstacles, and negative seeds for them; transform them into the Angel of Diamond; and then melt back into you.

16205.acip: MNYAM DU RANG RGYUD KYI NYON MONGS PA 'DOD CHAGS KYIS GTZOS PA'I SGRIB GNYIS BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS BRKYANG MA'I LAM NAS RLUNG DANG 'GROGS PHYIR THON TE,

16205.english: Along with the breath, as you exhale, the negativities you have which are headed by ignorant desire--the two obstacles, along with the seeds for them--exit as well with the breath, via the solitary channel.

17464.acip: BA SPU'I BU GA NAS PHAR SONG STE 'OD ZER GYIS REG PA TZAM GYIS SNOD KYI NYES SKYON RDO DANG, GSEG MA DANG, GYO MO DANG, NGAM GROG DANG, G-YANG SA SOGS DANG, BCUD KYI NYES SKYON SDIG SGRIB BAG CHAGS DANG BCAS PA SKAD CIG LA SBYANGS PAR BSAM PA DANG,

17464.english: The rays of light leave from the pores of your skin. 17672.english: I trained myself In the method, the Wish for enlightenment; I cut the flow Of the seeds for obstacles in my mind. I saw everything That appeared around me as an illusion; And now I've no more fear for the three lower realms.
