18460.acip: DE'I PHYIR NYIN BAR GYI DRAN 'DUN DRAG POS GZHAG PA'I BAG CHAGS RMI LAM DU SAD THUB PA LA NI, RMI LAM GYI SHES PA SHIN TU GSAL BA GCIG DGOS PAS, DE'I THABS KYANG NYIN MO BSGRUB DGOS SO,,
18460.wylie: de'i phyir nyin bar gyi dran 'dun drag pos gzhag pa'i bag chags rmi lam du sad thub pa la ni, rmi lam gyi shes pa shin tu gsal ba gcig dgos pas, de'i thabs kyang nyin mo bsgrub dgos so
18460.english: The point then is that--if you hope to be one of those who can plant a seed in their minds through very strong recollection and will power during the day, and then get this seed to reawaken during their dreams--then you're going to have to have to be one of those people whose perception of their dreams is already extremely vivid. And this means that during the day you're also going to have to undertake various means of becoming one of these latter types of people.

18756.acip: BYED PA'I DUS NI SGYU LUS SGRUB PA'I MGO RTZOM PA'I DUS DANG, SGYU LUS GRUB NAS 'OD GSAL SBYONG BA'I DUS DANG, SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG THOB NAS, MI SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG THOB PA'I PHYIR DU BYED PA'I DUS GSUM MO, ,'DI RNAMS 'DIR SMOS PA NI MAN NGAG GI GNAD TSANG BA LA 'DI RNAMS KYANG DGOS SO,, ZHES KHA BSKANG PA DANG, DE DAG GI BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA'I PHYIR BYAS KYI, RGYA CHER NI TSIG MANGS SU DOGS PAS MA BRIS TE, SHES PAR 'DOD NA 'DUS PA'I MAN NGAG LAS BTZAL BAR BYA'O,,
18756.wylie: byed pa'i dus ni sgyu lus sgrub pa'i mgo rtsom pa'i dus dang, sgyu lus grub nas 'od gsal sbyong ba'i dus dang, slob pa'i zung 'jug thob nas, mi slob pa'i zung 'jug thob pa'i phyir du byed pa'i dus gsum mo, ,'di rnams 'dir smos pa ni man ngag gi gnad tshang ba la 'di rnams kyang dgos so,, zhes kha bskang pa dang, de dag gi bag chags bzhag pa'i phyir byas kyi, rgya cher ni tshig mangs su dogs pas ma bris te, shes par 'dod na 'dus pa'i man ngag las btsal bar bya'o
18756.english: When does one partake of these enjoyments? There are three different periods: 1) when one has just got to the point of producing one's illusory body; 2) when one has already produced their illusory body, and is practicing to reach proficiency in clear light; and 3) as a means for attaining the union of the two beyond all further learning. The reason I have mentioned these practices here is as a sort of addendum, to tell you that "if you really want all the crucial points of these advices in a comprehensive way, you're going to need these as well." I also wanted to plant a seed in you to practice them in the future. I have not written any very detailed description of them here because of a concern that this treatise would become too lengthy. If you would like to know more on this subject, you can seek it in the advices on the Secret Collection. Bringing about the Final Result

18757.english: Here is our third major point; that is, how one brings about the final result. Once one has reached the union of the two where there is still further learning to be done, you practice the clear light. This allows you to clean yourself of the mental seeds for inconsistent, mistaken perception.

19610.acip: BSKYED RIM RAGS PA MTHAR PHYIN NA SKAD CIG GIS BSKYED PAS CHOG KYANG , DE LTAR MIN PAR RDZOGS RIM LA BAG CHAGS 'JOG PA'I PHYIR THUN STOD LA BSKYED RIM DANG THUN SMAD LA RDZOGS RIM BSGOM PA YIN PAS,

19610.english: It is true that if you have perfected your practice of the gross form of the stage of creation, then you can go ahead and bring Her forth in a single instant.  You can though follow a different course which will plant a seed for your practice of the stage of completion.  Here you concentrate on the path of creation during the first part of your practice session, and then on the path of completion during the latter part of the session.

20084.acip: ZHES PA 'KHOR BA DANG DE'I BAG CHAGS LAS LAM GZHAN GYIS GROL BA CHES RING NGO ZHES PA'I DON NO, ,DE NAS TE RGYU MTSAN DE'I PHYIR SGRUB PA POS PHYI NANG SOGS KYI MCHOD PA'I DNGOS PO KUN GYIS RANG DANG PHYAG RGYA MCHOD PAR BYAS PA LAS MYUR DU GROL BAR BYA'O,,
20084.wylie: zhes pa 'khor ba dang de'i bag chags las lam gzhan gyis grol ba ches ring ngo zhes pa'i don no, ,de nas te rgyu mtshan de'i phyir sgrub pa pos phyi nang sogs kyi mchod pa'i dngos po kun gyis rang dang phyag rgya mchod par byas pa las myur du grol bar bya'o
20084.english: What the text is saying here is that--if we try to use any other path--then our liberation from both the circle of pain and the subtle seeds behind it will be delayed for a very, very long time.  As such, a secret practitioner should see that both their spiritual partner, and they themselves, are presented with every kind of offering--whether outer, inner, or any of the rest.  And they must be sure as well to make offerings to their partner themselves.  If they do, then they will quickly be liberated. * * * This prayer to our Heart Lama says it all. 21354.acip: 'O NA, DE YON TAN CI ZHIG DANG LDAN SNYAM NA, BLA MA DE NYID NI PHUN SUM TSOGS PA'I YON TAN DANG LDAN PA YIN TE, (NYES) PA SGRIB GNYIS (KUN) DANG (BAG CHAGS) TE DE BSKYED PA'I GZHI SA BON DANG (BCAS PA DRUNG) STE RTZA BA NAS (PHYUNG ZHING) SPANGS PA'I SPANGS PA DANG,
21354.wylie: 'o na, de yon tan ci zhig dang ldan snyam na, bla ma de nyid ni phun sum tshogs pa'i yon tan dang ldan pa yin te, (nyes) pa sgrib gnyis (kun) dang (bag chags) te de bskyed pa'i gzhi sa bon dang (bcas pa drung) ste rtsa ba nas (phyung zhing) spangs pa'i spangs pa dang
21354.english: "Well then," you may ask, "just what sorts of high qualities does this Lama possess?"  This same Lama is one possessed of most excellent qualities.  They have ripped out every wrong--each of the two obstacles--along with its seeds (the foundation or seed which would produce each wrong), from the very bottom root.  Which is to say, They have achieved the final elimination of these obstacles.

21449.acip: DPER NA, SKYES BU GNYID LOG PA'I TSE BDE SDUG SNA TSOGS ZHIG SNANG BA YOD KYANG, DE DAG 'KHRUL BA'I BAG CHAGS KYI DBANG GIS YIN GYI, DON GYI GNAS TSOD LA MI BDEN TE, RMI LAM GYI MI NI MI MA YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,

21449.english: When a person is asleep, for example, various feelings of pleasure and pain can make their appearance to them--but this is only happening through certain seeds of misperception.  In actual fact none of these things is real, because a person in a dream is not a person.

21571.acip: SDUG BSNGAL GYIS GDUNG BA SHIN TU (BZOD DKA') BA NI, DPER NA NYES CAN 'JUG PA'I GNAS (BTZON RA) DANG ('DRA BA'I 'KHOR BA 'DI) NI, BDAG CAG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS NGAN PA'I DBANG GIS, SKYID PA'I GNAS (DGA' BA'I TSAL LTA) BUR PHYIN CI LOG TU (MTHONG BA'I BLO) NGAN PA 'DI (SPANGS NAS) LHAG PA'I TSUL KHRIMS KYI BSLAB PA SOGS (BSLAB GSUM) DANG, DAD PA, TSUL KHRIMS, THOS PA, GTONG BA, SHES RAB, KHREL YOD, NGO TSA SHES PA'I ('PHAGS PA'I NOR GYI MDZOD) RNAMS LEGS PAR (BZUNG STE,)
21571.wylie: sdug bsngal gyis gdung ba shin tu (bzod dka') ba ni, dper na nyes can 'jug pa'i gnas (btson ra) dang ('dra ba'i 'khor ba 'di) ni, bdag cag 'khrul pa'i bag chags ngan pa'i dbang gis, skyid pa'i gnas (dga' ba'i tshal lta) bur phyin ci log tu (mthong ba'i blo) ngan pa 'di (spangs nas) lhag pa'i tshul khrims kyi bslab pa sogs (bslab gsum) dang, dad pa, tshul khrims, thos pa, gtong ba, shes rab, khrel yod, ngo tsha shes pa'i ('phags pa'i nor gyi mdzod) rnams legs par (bzung ste,)
21571.english: Just how is it that we are tormented so unbearably by this pain?  This cycle of pain that we live in is like a prison: a place where those who have done wrong are detained.  And all of us here--due to negative seeds in our mind that make us see things wrongly--entertain a completely mistaken vision of this place, where we see it as though it were a garden of earthly delights.  What we need then is to relinquish this vision and find, or discover, the treasure of the jewels of the realized: high qualities including all three of the higher trainings (the higher training of leading an ethical life, and so on)--as well as faith, morality, learning, generosity, wisdom, consideration, and shame.

21660.acip: ,NYES KUN BAG CHAGS BCAS PA DRUNGS PHYUNG ZHING, ,DPAG MED YON TAN RIN CHEN TSOGS KYI GTER, ,PHAN BDE MA LUS 'BYUNG BA'I SGO GCIG PU, ,RJE BTZUN BLA MA'I ZHABS LA PHYAG 'TSAL LO,

21660.english: You have ripped out every wrong, Along with its seeds, from the very root; You are a goldmine of jewels, An infinite mass of high qualities. You are the one and only door To all happiness and help; I bow down to the dear feet Of my Lama, the Holy One.

5991.acip: ZER NA MA KHYAB STE, DANG POR YI DVAGS KYIS CHU MA MTHONG NA PHYOGS DER LONGS SPYOD PA'I PHYIR, 'GRO BA YANG MI 'THAD PAS DANG POR CHU MTHONG YANG , PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS CHU MA MTHONG BAR 'OG GZHI GRAM SREG TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING , DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS CHU BSKAMS PAR ZHEN PA DANG , DE BZHIN DU DANG POR LJON SHING GI 'BRAS BU MTHONG YANG PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS 'BRAS BU MA MTHONG BAR YAL GA TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING , DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS 'BRAS BU MED PAR ZHEN PA'I PHYIR,
5991.wylie: zer na ma khyab ste, dang por yi dvags kyis chu ma mthong na phyogs der longs spyod pa'i phyir, 'gro ba yang mi 'thad pas dang por chu mthong yang , phyis las kyi dbang gis chu ma mthong bar 'og gzhi gram sreg tsam zhig mthong zhing , de'i rjes su rtog pas chu bskams par zhen pa dang , de bzhin du dang por ljon shing gi 'bras bu mthong yang phyis las kyi dbang gis 'bras bu ma mthong bar yal ga tsam zhig mthong zhing , de'i rjes su rtog pas 'bras bu med par zhen pa'i phyir
5991.english: Just because we said that about the other case doesn't mean that it's true in every case. If the craving spirit hadn't seen any water in that area in the first place, it wouldn't have made any sense for him to go over in that direction to try to enjoy some of the water. Therefore what happened was that, at first, he saw some water. Later on, he was forced by his karma to stop seeing water and saw only bare, parched earth. Then he had an impression where he thought the water had dried up. The case with the fruit tree is the same. Although at first the craving spirit sees a tree loaded with fruit, later on his karma forces him to stop seeing fruit, and all he sees is bare branches. Then he has an impression where he thinks that the tree has no fruit any more.

27734.acip: LAS KYI NUS PA MTHONG BA YIN, ZHES PA'I LAN DU, ,RE ZHIG NYER LEN SRED PA NI, ,MED CES NGES PA NYID CE NA, ZHES YANG SRID LEN PA'I SRED PA LAM DES ZAD PAR BYED PAS, LAS KYI DBANG GIS YANG SRID PHYI MA MI LEN PAR NGES PA NYID DO,
27734.wylie: las kyi nus pa mthong ba yin, zhes pa'i lan du, ,re zhig nyer len sred pa ni, ,med ces nges pa nyid ce na, zhes yang srid len pa'i sred pa lam des zad par byed pas, las kyi dbang gis yang srid phyi ma mi len par nges pa nyid do
27734.english: In response to the statement that “We can still see the forces / Of karma in them,” we find the lines, And suppose you say it's assured, Since the material cause Of initial desire is absent, For the moment. Which is to say: “Given that these paths have finished off the initial desire which causes us to take our next rebirth, it is assured that we will not be forced by karma to take this rebirth.”

34925.acip: ZER NA MA KHYAB STE DANG POR YI DWAGS KYIS CHU MA MTHONG NA PHYOGS DER LONGS SPYOD, PA'I PHYIR 'GRO BA YANG MI 'THAD PAS DANG POR CHU MTHONG YANG PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG, GIS CHU MA MTHONG BAR 'OG GZHI GRAM SREG TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING DE'I RJES SU RTOG, PAS CHU BSKAMS PAR ZHEN PA DANG DE BZHIN DU DANG POR LJON SHING GI 'BRAS BU MTHONG YANG PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS 'BRAS BU MA MTHONG BAR YAL GA TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS 'BRAS BU MED PAR ZHEN PA'I PHYIR
34925.wylie: zer na ma khyab ste dang por yi dwags kyis chu ma mthong na phyogs der longs spyod, pa'i phyir 'gro ba yang mi 'thad pas dang por chu mthong yang phyis las kyi dbang, gis chu ma mthong bar 'og gzhi gram sreg tsam zhig mthong zhing de'i rjes su rtog, pas chu bskams par zhen pa dang de bzhin du dang por ljon shing gi 'bras bu mthong yang phyis las kyi dbang gis 'bras bu ma mthong bar yal ga tsam zhig mthong zhing de'i rjes su rtog pas 'bras bu med par zhen pa'i phyir
34925.english: Just because we said that about the other case doesn't mean that it's true in every case. If the craving spirit hadn't seen any water in that area in the first place, it wouldn't have made any sense for him to go over in that direction to try to enjoy some of the water. Therefore what happened was that, at first, he saw some water. Later on, he was forced by his karma to stop seeing water and saw only bare, parched earth. Then he had an impression where he thought the water had dried up. The case with the fruit tree is the same. Although at first the craving spirit sees a tree loaded with fruit, later on his karma forces him to stop seeing fruit, and all he sees is bare branches. Then he has an impression where he thinks that the tree has no fruit any more.

1975.wylie: mdor na bdag gam gang zag btags don btsal ba'i tshe mi rnyed kyang tha snyad du sgyu ma dang sprul pa ltar bya byed 'thad pa de bzhin du chos thams cad la'ang 'dra ste, sdud pa las, , bdag ci 'dra bar de 'drar sems can thams cad shes, ,sems can thams cad ci 'dra de 'drar chos kun shes, ,zhes dang
1975.english: In short, when you search for the thing given the name of "self" or "me" you will never find anything; despite this, the fact that things can do something is completely right and proper, in the sense of an illusion, or magic. And this fact applies to each and every existing thing there is. As the Shorter [Sutra on the Perfection of Wisdom] states, You should understand that the nature of every single living is the same as that of the "self." You should understand that the nature of all existing objects is the same as that of every living being.

2055.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni, ma 'ongs pa na sems can gang dag mdo sde 'di bshad pa'i tshig don thos pa na, de ltar thams cad bden par med na las 'bras sogs bya byed mi 'thad cing med par 'gyur ro snyam du yid mi skrag cing mi dngang la, shin tu dngang bar mi 'gyur zhing yid ches te mos pa de dag ni ngo mtshar rab dang ldan par 'gyur ro, , bden par grub na bsgyur du mi rung bas las 'bras la sogs pa'i bya byed thams cad bzhag tu mi rung zhing mi 'thad la, bden par med pa'am rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa la bya byed thams cad dang myang 'das sogs 'thad pa'i tshul ni, rjes rten 'brel bstod pa las, rang bzhin ldog pa med pa'i phyir, , chos rnams rang bzhin 'ga' yod na, , mya ngan 'das pa mi rung zhing , , spros kun ldog pa med par gsungs, , zhes dang , rang bzhin gyis ni stong pa dang , , bya byed 'thad pas mi 'gal zhing , , de las ldog par mthong ba na, , stong la bya ba mi rung zhing , , zhes gsungs pa ltar ro
2055.english: Here is the reason. In future days, certain living beings will receive, they will listen to, an explanation of the meaning of the words of this sutra. And yet they will not be made afraid, and they will not be frightened, and they will not become extremely frightened, by any such thought as: "If this is so, and if nothing at all exists in a true way, then all the ways in which things like karma and its consequences work cannot be right, and so really nothing at all can work." Rather they will find a greater belief, an even greater faith, in all these objects. And beings like this will be truly wondrous. If things did exist in a true way, then it would be improper to say that they ever changed. And then it would be improper, it would never be right, to describe all the workings of things like karma and its consequences. The way in which all things work, and nirvana itself, and everything else are all quite proper. And none of these objects has any true existence, none of them has any nature of their own. How all this can be is described by Lord Tsongkapa in his Praise from Interdependence: Reaching the state of nirvana could never occur, And elaborations too could never be stopped, If objects had any nature of their own, because A nature could not be stopped, You stated. He also says, Since things are empty of any nature And the way things work is right, There is no contradiction between them. Those who see things the opposite Think nothing can work with emptiness...

4201.acip: GSUM PA NI, SRID PA'I 'GRO BA RMI LAM LTA BU STE RANG BZHIN CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PA LA BYA BYED MA 'DRES PA SO SOR GNAS PA'I PHYIR RO, , DE KHO NA NYID LA DPYOD PA'I RIGS PAS RNAM PAR DPYAD NA CHU SHING DANG 'DRA STE TSUGS THUB PA LTAR SNANG YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SNYING PO CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PA'I PHYIR,
4201.wylie: gsum pa ni, srid pa'i 'gro ba rmi lam lta bu ste rang bzhin cung zad kyang med pa la bya byed ma 'dres pa so sor gnas pa'i phyir ro, , de kho na nyid la dpyod pa'i rigs pas rnam par dpyad na chu shing dang 'dra ste tshugs thub pa ltar snang yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i snying po cung zad kyang med pa'i phyir
4201.english: Here is the third point, [which is showing how all this proves that our suffering existence and the state of peace have one quality which is totally equivalent]. The events of this suffering life are like a dream; this is because they lack the slightest bit of any nature of their own, and yet still exhibit all the workings of actions and the objects of actions, without any confusion of the two. If you analyze these events with the logic that examines suchness, then you find that they are just like a hollow piece of cane: although they appear to have some substantial existence, they lack even the tiniest bit of any essence, any nature of their own.

If you analyze these events with the logic that examines suchness, then you find that they are just like a hollow piece of cane: although they appear to have some substantial existence, they lack even the tiniest bit of any essence, any nature of their own.

32892.english: One should, at this point, admittedly give a detailed explanation of how—even though outer objects do not exist—the way in which things do things is still completely reasonable. 28999.acip: BYA BYED GNYIS NI THA SNYAD PA'I BLO KHO NA'I NGOR 'JOG PA'I PHYIR TE, DPER NA RIGS SHES RJES DPAG YUL CAN DANG, DON DAM BDEN PA YUL DU 'JOG NUS KYANG, YUL DANG YUL CAN GYI BYA BYED GNYIS RIGS NGOR MA 'JOG PA BZHIN NO,,
28999.wylie: bya byed gnyis ni tha snyad pa'i blo kho na'i ngor 'jog pa'i phyir te, dper na rigs shes rjes dpag yul can dang, don dam bden pa yul du 'jog nus kyang, yul dang yul can gyi bya byed gnyis rigs ngor ma 'jog pa bzhin no
28999.english: This is due to the fact that the two of an object to an action, and the action itself, can only be established in the perceptions of a nominal state of mind. We can, for example, say that a perception based on logic possesses an object of deduction; or that ultimate reality could act as its object of perception. We could not though establish, to the perceptions of such a deduction, objects of action or actions themselves, between the subject and its object.

32273.acip: MDOR NA BDAG GAM GANG ZAG BTAGS DON BTZAL BA'I TSE MI RNYED KYANG THA SNYAD DU SGYU MA DANG SPRUL PA LTAR BYA BYED 'THAD PA DE BZHIN DU CHOS THAMS CAD LA'ANG 'DRA STE, SDUD PA LAS, ,BDAG CI 'DRA BAR DE 'DRAR SEMS CAN THAMS CAD SHES, ,SEMS CAN THAMS CAD CI 'DRA DE 'DRAR CHOS KUN SHES, ,ZHES DANG,
32273.wylie: mdor na bdag gam gang zag btags don btsal ba'i tshe mi rnyed kyang tha snyad du sgyu ma dang sprul pa ltar bya byed 'thad pa de bzhin du chos thams cad la'ang 'dra ste, sdud pa las, ,bdag ci 'dra bar de 'drar sems can thams cad shes, ,sems can thams cad ci 'dra de 'drar chos kun shes, ,zhes dang
32273.english: In short, when you search for the thing given the name of “self” or “me,” you will never find anything; despite this, the fact that things can do something is completely right and proper, in the sense of an illusion, or magic. And this fact applies to each and every existing thing there is. As the Shorter Sutra on the Perfection of Wisdom states, You should understand that the nature of every single living being is the same as that of yourself. You should understand that the nature of all existing objects is the same as that of every living being.

32419.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA DE DE BZHIN NO ZHES PA DANG, RGYU MTSAN NI, MA 'ONGS PA NA SEMS CAN GANG DAG MDO SDE 'DI BSHAD PA'I TSIG DON THOS PA NA, DE LTAR THAMS CAD BDEN PAR MED NA LAS 'BRAS SOGS BYA BYED MI 'THAD CING MED PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM DU YID MI SKRAG CING MI DNGANG LA, SHIN TU DNGANG BAR MI 'GYUR ZHING YID CHES TE MOS PA DE DAG NI NGO MTSAR RAB DANG LDAN PAR 'GYUR RO,,
32419.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la de de bzhin no zhes pa dang, rgyu mtshan ni, ma 'ongs pa na sems can gang dag mdo sde 'di bshad pa'i tshig don thos pa na, de ltar thams cad bden par med na las 'bras sogs bya byed mi 'thad cing med par 'gyur ro snyam du yid mi skrag cing mi dngang la, shin tu dngang bar mi 'gyur zhing yid ches te mos pa de dag ni ngo mtshar rab dang ldan par 'gyur ro
32419.english: The Conqueror then says to Subhuti, “Thus it is”; and as a reason for this statement continues with the following: In future days, certain living beings will receive, they will listen to, an explanation of the meaning of the words of this sutra. And yet they will not be made afraid, and they will not be frightened, and they will not become extremely frightened, by any such thought as: “If this is so, and if nothing at all exists in a true way, then all the ways in which things like karma and its consequences work cannot be right, and so really nothing at all can work.” Rather they will find a greater belief, an even greater faith, in all these objects. And beings like this will be wondrous in the highest.

22088.acip: BDEN PAR GRUB NA BSGYUR DU MI RUNG BAS LAS 'BRAS LA SOGS PA'I BYA BYED THAMS CAD BZHAG TU MI RUNG ZHING MI 'THAD LA, BDEN PAR MED PA'AM RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA LA BYA BYED THAMS CAD DANG MYANG 'DAS SOGS
22088.wylie: bden par grub na bsgyur du mi rung bas las 'bras la sogs pa'i bya byed thams cad bzhag tu mi rung zhing mi 'thad la, bden par med pa'am rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa la bya byed thams cad dang myang 'das sogs
22088.english: If things did exist in a true way, then it would be improper to say that they ever changed. And then it would be improper, it would never be right, to describe all the workings of things like karma and its consequences. The way in which all things work, and nirvana itself, and everything else are all quite proper. And none of these objects has any true existence, none of them has any nature of their own.

2715.english: Next is the contemplation that there is no certainty when we will die, for the reason that (6) our bodies are extremely fragile. Our bodies really are very fragile, very much like a bubble, and it requires no great injury to destroy our life-force: even something like the prick of a thorn, if we disregard it, can kill us. The point is that none of the things that can kill us has to try very hard to kill us. 3594.english: "But it is right for me to be angry," one may insist, "because the other person has hurt me." Now if you are going to be angry at what hurt you directly, then you should feel anger for the stick or the weapon or whatever it was that delivered the injury directly, since they are what caused the pain. Or suppose you say that you're not going to get angry at the stick or whatever, since it didn't act on its own accord, but rather at what made it move: at the person who impelled the stick. This other person though is not acting on his own accord either; rather, he himself is set into motion by the force of anger. So if you really must be angry--if you have no choice, if you cannot help yourself--then you should get mad at anger itself. Contemplation Twelve Who it is that actually created the objects that bring us anger

3610.acip: BZLOGDNG PO NI, RANG NYID LA GNOD PA BYED PA LA KHRO BAR MI RIGS KYANG DKON MCHOG LA GNOD PA BYED PA LA KHROS KYANG NYES PA MED DO ZHE NA, SANGS RGYAS KYI SKU GZUGS DANG BYANG CHUB CHEN PO'I MCHOD RTEN SOGS DANG DAM PA'I CHOS LA NGAG GIS 'KHYAL ZHING SKYON BRJOD PA DANG , LUS KYIS 'JIG PAR BYED PA LA'ANG BDAG GIS ZHE SDANG BYA BAR MI RIGS TE SANGS RGYAS SOGS DKON MCHOG GSUM LA GNOD PA MI MNGA' ZHING GNOD BYED NI SNYING RJE'I GNAS YIN PAS BRTZE BA BYA BAR RIGS SO, , DKON MCHOG GSUM LA YID MI BDES SEMS GZIR BA'I RKYEN LAS MI 'BYUNG BA'I DON TO,
3610.wylie: bzlogdng po ni, rang nyid la gnod pa byed pa la khro bar mi rigs kyang dkon mchog la gnod pa byed pa la khros kyang nyes pa med do zhe na, sangs rgyas kyi sku gzugs dang byang chub chen po'i mchod rten sogs dang dam pa'i chos la ngag gis 'khyal zhing skyon brjod pa dang , lus kyis 'jig par byed pa la'ang bdag gis zhe sdang bya bar mi rigs te sangs rgyas sogs dkon mchog gsum la gnod pa mi mnga' zhing gnod byed ni snying rje'i gnas yin pas brtse ba bya bar rigs so, , dkon mchog gsum la yid mi bdes sems gzir ba'i rkyen las mi 'byung ba'i don to
3610.english: Here is the first point, which covers the reasons why it is wrong to feel anger at those who are doing harm to holy images and the like. Someone may make the following argument: "I can admit that it is wrong to feel anger for someone who has hurt me personally. But there is nothing wrong with getting angry at those who have harmed the Three Jewels." Suppose though that someone expresses themselves, speaking against sacred images of the Buddhas, the shrines of great bodhisattvas and the like, or else the holy Dharma. Or suppose that they even act bodily to try to destroy these things. It's completely wrong for me to feel anger even at these kinds of people, since the Buddhas and such, the Three Jewels, cannot be hurt. In fact, the one who attempts to harm them is someone who deserves our pity, and so it is more appropriate to feel love for them. The point here is that the Three Jewels are incapable of sustaining any kind of injury brought about by mental discomfort due to feeling upset.

24512.acip: [C113] GLANG PO CHE RNAMS KHYU MCHOG GI RJES SU 'BRANG NA GNOD PA SOGS MED PA LTAR, SANGS RGYAS KYI RJES SU ZHUGS NA LAM MI GOL BAR DRANG POR 'GRO BA NYID KYIS
24512.wylie: [c113] glang po che rnams khyu mchog gi rjes su 'brang na gnod pa sogs med pa ltar, sangs rgyas kyi rjes su zhugs na lam mi gol bar drang por 'gro ba nyid kyis
24512.english: (M12) When elephants follow behind the head of the herd, they are protected from injury and the like.  When we follow behind the Buddha, we can go straight to our goal, without mistaking the way.

28066.acip: GAL TE GNOD PA BYAS PA LAS, DER TE GNOD BYED LA BKON PA STE KHRO NA, DE'I TSE GNOD PA BYAS ZIN PA LDOG TU MED PA'I PHYIR, DE LA BKON PA STE DE LA DMIGS PA'I ZHE 'KHAM PA BYAS PAS, GNOD PA BYAS ZIN PA LDOG GAM CI STE MI LDOG GO ,DE'I PHYIR DE LA BKON PA 'DIR NGES PAR DON MED DO,,
28066.wylie: gal te gnod pa byas pa las, der te gnod byed la bkon pa ste khro na, de'i tshe gnod pa byas zin pa ldog tu med pa'i phyir, de la bkon pa ste de la dmigs pa'i zhe 'kham pa byas pas, gnod pa byas zin pa ldog gam ci ste mi ldog go ,de'i phyir de la bkon pa 'dir nges par don med do
28066.english: Suppose then that a person hurts you, and you feel enmity towards them—meaning that you get angry. There's no way that this is then somehow going to prevent the hurt that they have inflicted upon you, and which is already done & gone. And so the question arises: If you feel enmity towards them—if you take umbrage at what they have done—then do you think that this will somehow prevent that injury, which is already done & gone? The answer, of course, is that it will not. We can conclude then that feeling this enmity now over what they did is without question pointless.

15647.english: After all this, we next don our armor.  And what does it mean to say  "armor" here? 2375.english: Someone else could hear that the person had such an ability, and gain desire towards this state of mind. Or the person himself could begin to worry that he might lose the ability and thus gain desire towards it. Still again, someone might catch sight of some exquisite emanation, think how wonderful the state of mind behind it was, and thereby start to desire it. Finally, even if this state of mind doesn't directly cause mental affliction to develop in someone's mind, it is still "an object with which mental affliction can develop"--since smells and tastes of the desire realm can be emanated in this state.

2472.acip: ,YANG YANG LUS 'DOR BA NI, LUS BZANG PO JI TZAM THOB KYANG ZHES SOGS TE LUS 'TSO SKYONG BYA BA'I PHYIR SDIG PA SNA TSOGS SHIG BSAGS KYANG MTHAR LUS NI NGES PAR 'DOR ZHING DE'I CHED DU BSAGS PA'I SDIG PA THAMS CAD SEMS STENG DU KHYER TE 'BRAS BU SDUG BSNGAL MI BZAD PA MYONG LA, GZHAN YANG RE RE'I BDAG NYID RUS PA'I PHUNG PO NI, , LHUN PO MNYAM PA SNYED GCIG 'DAS GYUR TE, , ZHES SEMS CAN RE RE'I LUS BLANGS NAS DOR BA'I RUS PA RNAMS BSAGS NA RI RAB LHUN PO LAS KYANG MANG BA STE, SNYED CIG CES PA NI LHUN PO DANG MNYAM PA JI SNYED CIG 'DAS ZHES PA'I DON,
2472.wylie: yang yang lus 'dor ba ni, lus bzang po ji tsam thob kyang zhes sogs te lus 'tsho skyong bya ba'i phyir sdig pa sna tshogs shig bsags kyang mthar lus ni nges par 'dor zhing de'i ched du bsags pa'i sdig pa thams cad sems steng du khyer te 'bras bu sdug bsngal mi bzad pa myong la, gzhan yang re re'i bdag nyid rus pa'i phung po ni, , lhun po mnyam pa snyed gcig 'das gyur te, , zhes sems can re re'i lus blangs nas dor ba'i rus pa rnams bsags na ri rab lhun po las kyang mang ba ste, snyed cig ces pa ni lhun po dang mnyam pa ji snyed cig 'das zhes pa'i don
2472.english: The next suffering is [3] the fact that we have to shed our bodies, over and over. This is indicated in the lines that include, "It doesn't matter what wonderful kind of body I may be able to attain..." The point here is that, regardless of all the bad deeds we might accumulate in order to maintain this body we have now, it is an absolute certainty that--in the end--we will be forced to shed it. The power of the wrong deeds we did for the sake of the body though we carry along in our mind, and they bring to us the eventual result of unbearable pain. Beyond this are the lines that say, The size of the stack of rotting corpses belonging to each of us Would exceed an equivalent to the height of Mount Supreme itself. Suppose that you could put together a huge stack of all the skeletons left from the bodies that any particular person had ever taken on, and then left behind. This stack would be more immense than Summit, the great mountain at the middle of the world. The difficult expression nyechik here is meant to indicate "a quantity equivalent to the height," which is then exceeded.

2700.wylie: de ltar na tshe 'di'i phun tshogs thams cad ni rmi lam thun gcig na bde ba spyad bsad nas dran pa ltar 'chi ba'i dus su dran pa'i yul tsam du 'gyur la, 'chi ba'i dgra ni dgag tu med par nges par 'ong na ci'i phyir tshe 'di'i bslu brid la dga' bar bya snyam du bsams te chos bya dgos pa la thag bcad cing zhe dam mang du bya ste, skyes rabs las, kye ma'o 'jig rten nyon mongs dag, gnas pa mi brtan dga' mi 'gyur, , ku mu ta yi dpal 'di yang , , dran par bya ba nyid du 'gyur, , 'gro ba 'di lta bur ni 'khod pa la, , skye bo 'jigs pa med pa ngo mtshar kye, , lam rnams thams cad 'chi bdag nyid kyis bkag, dogs pa med par rab tu dga' zhing spyod, , na dang rga dang 'chi ba'i gnod byed dgra, , mthu chen dgag tu mi nus yod bzhin la, , 'jig rten pha rol nyam ngar nges 'gro na, , sems shes su zhig 'di la dga' bar sems, , zhes dang
2700.english: And so all the good things of this life are like the happiness within one night's dream: you wake, and then it's nothing more than a memory. The time comes to die, and everything good you ever had lives only in a dim remembrance. This great enemy, death, will surely come; nothing can stop him. You should contemplate this fact--try to wonder, "Why do I take such pleasure in the lie of this life?" Make up your mind that you absolutely must now practice some Dharma; swear it to yourself, continually. Remember the Birth Stories, where it says: Alas, you worldly ones so full of affliction of the mind; Why do you take such pleasure in a land of shifting sands? The shining glory of the kumuda bloom, opening to the moon, Soon enough turns nothing more than a simple memory. It's something of a pure amazement too that all of us Thrust into a life like this are not consumed by total fear; Damn the Lord of Death, who stands and blocks all pathways out, While we oblivious feel content, and have an enjoyable day. We all share enemies, dreadfully powerful, ones we cannot stop: Their names are sickness, age, and death; they attack us even now. If it's certain that we are headed for agony in the world beyond, How could anyone with a mind be content in the one here now?

3016.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, SU GA TA'I SGRA SPANGS PA DANG RTOGS PA GNYIS LA BSHAD DU YOD PAS SPANGS PA PHUN TSOGS KYI YON TAN NI, SKYES BU GZUGS LEGS PA BZHIN DU NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA ZAD PAR SPANGS PAS LEGS PA'AM MDZES PAR GSHEGS PA DANG , RIMS NAD LEGS PAR BYANG BA BZHIN DU NYON MONGS PA'I DBANG GIS SLAR 'KHOR BAR MI LDOG PAR GSHEGS PA DANG , BUM PA LEGS PAR GANG BA BZHIN DU NYON MONGS PA CAN MA YIN PA'I MA RIG PA ZAD PAR SPANGS PAS MA LUS PAR GSHEGS PAS BDE BAR GSHEGS PA'O, , BDE BA NI LEGS PA SOGS DANG , GSHEGS PA NI DE'I BDAG NYID DU SON PA'O,
3016.wylie: gsum pa ni, su ga ta'i sgra spangs pa dang rtogs pa gnyis la bshad du yod pas spangs pa phun tshogs kyi yon tan ni, skyes bu gzugs legs pa bzhin du nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa zad par spangs pas legs pa'am mdzes par gshegs pa dang , rims nad legs par byang ba bzhin du nyon mongs pa'i dbang gis slar 'khor bar mi ldog par gshegs pa dang , bum pa legs par gang ba bzhin du nyon mongs pa can ma yin pa'i ma rig pa zad par spangs pas ma lus par gshegs pas bde bar gshegs pa'o, , bde ba ni legs pa sogs dang , gshegs pa ni de'i bdag nyid du son pa'o
3016.english: The Sanskrit word Sugata [Those Who have Gone to Well-Being] can be explained in two ways. We can explain it in reference to either the things which an Enlightened Being has eliminated, or in reference to the things which he or she has realized. First I will explain it in terms of that excellent virtue an Enlightened Being possess of having totally eliminated every single bad quality there is. Because an Enlightened Being has completely cleaned Himself of all the obstacles which are related to bad thoughts, we can say that he has gone well, or beautifully, and is like someone who has an well-formed body. Because he will never have to return back to this cycle of suffering life by force of things poisoned with the afflictions of the mind, we can say that he has gone like someone who has been completely cured, or made well, from an illness. And because he has totally removed all of those kinds of ignorance which are not related to the mental afflictions, we can say that he has totally gone like a vase which is well-filled. It is in this way that we call such a being One Who Has Gone to Well-Being. We say "well-being" to refer to the different qualities described above with the word "well", and we say "gone" to indicate that these beings have gone to the nature which embodies those very qualities.

3282.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, GZHAN RGYUD KYI NYON MONGS GZHOM BAR KHAS BLANGS PA YIN MOD, RANG RGYUD KYI NYON MONGS GZHOM PA'I CHED DU BRTZON PAR MI RIGS TE, DE LTAR NA ZHI BA'I MTHAR LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BAS SO ZHE NA PHYOGS BCU NAM MKHA'I MTHAS GTUGS PA'I 'GRO BA THAMS CAD NYON MONGS LAS SGROL BAR SEMS BSKYED CING DAM BCAS NAS GANG GI TSE BDAG NYID KYANG NYON MONGS RNAMS LAS MA GROL BA YIN NA GZHAN DON LTA ZHOG RANG DON YANG RDZOGS PAR MI NUS PAS NYON MONGS PA'I GZHAN DBANG DU GYUR PA'I BDAG GI TSOD KYANG MI SHES PAR GZHAN MTHA' DAG NYON MONGS LAS SGROL BAR SMRA BA JI LTAR SMYON PA MIN TE, RANG 'KHOR BAR BCINGS PAS GZHAN DON RDZOGS PAR MI NUS PAS RANG RGYUD KYI NYON MONGS GZHOM PA LA BRTZON PAR BYA'O,
3282.wylie: gsum pa ni, gzhan rgyud kyi nyon mongs gzhom bar khas blangs pa yin mod, rang rgyud kyi nyon mongs gzhom pa'i ched du brtson par mi rigs te, de ltar na zhi ba'i mthar ltung bar 'gyur bas so zhe na phyogs bcu nam mkha'i mthas gtugs pa'i 'gro ba thams cad nyon mongs las sgrol bar sems bskyed cing dam bcas nas gang gi tshe bdag nyid kyang nyon mongs rnams las ma grol ba yin na gzhan don lta zhog rang don yang rdzogs par mi nus pas nyon mongs pa'i gzhan dbang du gyur pa'i bdag gi tshod kyang mi shes par gzhan mtha' dag nyon mongs las sgrol bar smra ba ji ltar smyon pa min te, rang 'khor bar bcings pas gzhan don rdzogs par mi nus pas rang rgyud kyi nyon mongs gzhom pa la brtson par bya'o
3282.english: Here is the third point. Someone might make the following statement: "I admit that I am a person who has agreed to undertake the destruction of the mental afflictions within the minds of other persons. It would be wrong though for me to work to destroy the mental afflictions in my own mind, because if I succeeded in doing so I would have fallen into what is called the 'extreme of personal peace.'" You have though pledged yourself, and developed the wish, to free all living beings, beings as vast in extent as the ten different directions of space itself, from their mental afflictions. If at the same time you have failed to free you yourself from all your own mental afflictions, then you have failed even in the endeavor of accomplishing all your own needs, much less those of others. Are you not some kind of madman then, to say that you are going to free every other living being from their mental afflictions, while at the very same moment you have failed completely to judge your own level--the fact that you yourself are still at the mercy of your own mental afflictions? No one chained in the cycle of suffering of life themselves could ever accomplish all the goals of other living beings, and so you should rather make efforts to destroy the mental afflictions within your own mind. 118 The Asian Classics Institute Course X: Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life, Part I Reading Eight: How to Fight the Mental Afflictions, Part Two; Why the Perfections are Mental The following readi

3650.acip: BRTZON 'GRUS DE'I MI MTHUN PHYOGS BSHAD PAR BYA'O, , GANG ZHE NA, LUS DANG YID LAS SU MI RUNG BA SNYOM LAS KYI BDE BA LA ZHEN PA'I LE LO DANG , BYA BA NGAN PA LA ZHEN PA DANG , DGE BA BSGRUB PA LA SGYID LUG NAS NGAS MI NUS SNYAM DU BDAG NYID LA BRNYAS PA'O,
3650.wylie: brtson 'grus de'i mi mthun phyogs bshad par bya'o, , gang zhe na, lus dang yid las su mi rung ba snyom las kyi bde ba la zhen pa'i le lo dang , bya ba ngan pa la zhen pa dang , dge ba bsgrub pa la sgyid lug nas ngas mi nus snyam du bdag nyid la brnyas pa'o
3650.english: Here next I will explain the things that work against "it"--meaning effort. What exactly are they? First there is laziness, which is feeling attracted to the pleasant feeling of sloth, a condition where the mind and body become unfit to function well. Next there is an attraction to actions which are bad, and then finally the feeling of being discouraged when you try to accomplish some virtuous act--where you belittle yourself by saying, "This is something I could never accomplish."

3671.acip: SBYOR BAS TSOGS GNYIS KYI DPUNG TSOGS GSOG PA SBYOR BA'I BRTZON 'GRUS DANG , DNGOS GZHI DRAN PA DANG SHES BZHIN GYIS NYAMS SU LEN PA LHUR BLANG BA DANG , LUS SEMS LAS RUNG DU GYUR PA'I SGO NAS BDAG NYID DBANG DU BYA BA DANG STE BYAS NAS 'OG NAS 'CHAD PA LTAR BDAG DANG GZHAN DU MNYAM PA DANG , GZHAN DANG BDAG TU BRJE BAR GYIS SHIG PA'O,
3671.wylie: sbyor bas tshogs gnyis kyi dpung tshogs gsog pa sbyor ba'i brtson 'grus dang , dngos gzhi dran pa dang shes bzhin gyis nyams su len pa lhur blang ba dang , lus sems las rung du gyur pa'i sgo nas bdag nyid dbang du bya ba dang ste byas nas 'og nas 'chad pa ltar bdag dang gzhan du mnyam pa dang , gzhan dang bdag tu brje bar gyis shig pa'o
3671.english: Then they make use of "working effort," where they work or apply themselves to the task of assembling the two great armed forces, the two collections. Then when the actual fight begins, they use engaged effort, where as they actually undertake their virtues they engage themselves gladly with constant recollection and awareness. Lastly they bring to bear their self-command, a state of complete control where you find yourself able to make your body and mind do anything that you ask them to do. When you have done all this then you must as well undertake the practices of seeing yourself and other people as equal, and finally exchanging yourself and others, in the manner that we will describe these two below [in the chapter on meditation]. Contemplation Ten On feeling discouraged

3712.acip: NYON MONGS 'JOMS PA LA GNYEN PO'I STOBS BSKYED PAR BYA STE, SHI BA'I SBRUL DANG PHRAD PAR GYUR NA BYA KHVA TA YANG MKHA' LDING LTA BUR SPYOD PA DE BZHIN DU GAL TE BDAG NYID GNYEN PO NYAMS STOBS CHUNG NA, LTUNG BA CHUNG NGU'ANG LAM LA BAR CHAD KYIS GNOD PAR BYED PAS BSAM PA ZHUM PAR BYAS NAS DON GNYIS SGRUB PA'I RTZOM BA DOR BA LA PHONGS PA'I GNAS SKABS LAS, NAM YANG THAR PA YOD DAM CI LE LOS BCOM NAS LUS SEMS KYI 'JUG PA NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,
3712.wylie: nyon mongs 'joms pa la gnyen po'i stobs bskyed par bya ste, shi ba'i sbrul dang phrad par gyur na bya khva ta yang mkha' lding lta bur spyod pa de bzhin du gal te bdag nyid gnyen po nyams stobs chung na, ltung ba chung ngu'ang lam la bar chad kyis gnod par byed pas bsam pa zhum par byas nas don gnyis sgrub pa'i rtsom ba dor ba la phongs pa'i gnas skabs las, nam yang thar pa yod dam ci le los bcom nas lus sems kyi 'jug pa nyams par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
3712.english: One should raise the power of the antidotes, in order to destroy one's mental affliction. If he encounters a snake that's dead already, then even the small crow can emulate the deeds of that great mythical bird, the garuda. The situation with me is the same: suppose that I continue to act like a weakling in the level of strength with which I apply the antidotes. Even a minor slip in a vow will be able to lay an obstacle in the path, and thus do me damage. This will lead me to discouragement, and then eventually I will lose my ability to make efforts towards achieving the goals of myself and others. And how could I really think I could ever be free then, living in such destitution? How could it ever come, where laziness has destroyed me, and torn down all the efforts I make with my body and mind? Contemplation Nineteen Determination, but not pride

3835.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, DPER NA BDAG NYID KYIS NI RANG GI ZAS ZOS NAS LAN LA RE BAS MI 'BYUNG BA BZHIN NO, , PHAN YON MTHA' YAS PA YOD PA DE BAS NA JI LTAR CHUNG NGU NA TSIG MI SNYAN PA LAS KYANG BDAG BSRUNG BA DE BZHIN DU 'GRO BA LA SDUG BSNGAL LAS BSRUNG SEMS DANG SNYING RJE'I SEMS NI GOMS PAR BYA'O,
3835.wylie: gnyis pa ni, dper na bdag nyid kyis ni rang gi zas zos nas lan la re bas mi 'byung ba bzhin no, , phan yon mtha' yas pa yod pa de bas na ji ltar chung ngu na tshig mi snyan pa las kyang bdag bsrung ba de bzhin du 'gro ba la sdug bsngal las bsrung sems dang snying rje'i sems ni goms par bya'o
3835.english: Here is the second point, which is advice to make efforts in this practice without hoping for any good karmic result. Think for example of when you eat your dinner, for yourself. You don't expect any congratulations from yourself for doing so. The case here is just the same. Consider how well you protect yourself even from the very least unkind word that someone might ever say to you. You must try to get used to having a state of mind where you protect all beings in just the same way, from every pain; you must as well get used to thoughts of compassion, for the reason that this is of infinite benefit. Contemplation Twenty-Five The enemy of the body

You must try to get used to having a state of mind where you protect all beings in just the same way, from every pain; you must as well get used to thoughts of compassion, for the reason that this is of infinite benefit. Contemplation Twenty-Five The enemy of the body"}

3854.acip: 'JIG RTEN DAG NA MI DANG MI MA YIN PA'I 'TSE BA GANG YOD DANG , SEMS KYI 'JIGS PA DANG LUS KYI SDUG BSNGAL JI SNYED YOD PAR GYUR PA DE KUN BDAG TU DMIGS NAS BDAG GCES PAR 'DZIN PA LAS BYUNG BAR BAR GYUR NA, MI 'DOD PA THAMS CAD BSKYED PA'I BDAG GCES 'DZIN GYI 'DRE CHEN DES KHO STE DES NI BDAG LA CI ZHIG BYA NAN GYIS SPANG BAR BYA'O, , BDAG NYID GCES PAR 'DZIN PA YONGS SU MA BTANG NA RANG GIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI SDUG BSNGAL SPANG BAR MI NUS TE JI LTAR TE DPER NA ME NI LAG PAS BZUNG NAS MA BTANG NA BSREG PA SPONG BAR MI NUS PA BZHIN NO,
3854.wylie: 'jig rten dag na mi dang mi ma yin pa'i 'tshe ba gang yod dang , sems kyi 'jigs pa dang lus kyi sdug bsngal ji snyed yod par gyur pa de kun bdag tu dmigs nas bdag gces par 'dzin pa las byung bar bar gyur na, mi 'dod pa thams cad bskyed pa'i bdag gces 'dzin gyi 'dre chen des kho ste des ni bdag la ci zhig bya nan gyis spang bar bya'o, , bdag nyid gces par 'dzin pa yongs su ma btang na rang gis sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal spang bar mi nus te ji ltar te dper na me ni lag pas bzung nas ma btang na bsreg pa spong bar mi nus pa bzhin no
3854.english: Consider every single harm that comes in this entire world, whether it be from humans or from non-human creatures. Think too of every fear that comes in the mind, and so too every pain that ever comes in the body. All of them come from grasping to, from cherishing, myself. What use for me then is this single greatest demon, this cherishing of myself that causes everything there is that I don't want to happen? I should stamp it out. Until the day that you give up this habit of cherishing your own self only, you'll not be able to stop the suffering of all living kind; it's like, for example, the following example: until the day that you let go of some coal of fire that you're holding in your hand, you will not be able to stop your hand from burning. Contemplation Thirty-One The master and the servant

3860.acip: BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS SEMS CAN RANG LAS DMAN PA DANG MNYAM PA DANG RANG LAS LHAG PA SOGS DMIGS YUL DU BYAS NAS BDAG TU BYAS PA DANG , BDAG NYID GZHAN NYID DU NI BYAS NAS TE BDAG GZHAN DU 'DZIN PA'I BLO GO SA SPOS NAS NGES SHES DRANGS TE THE TSOM GYI RNAM RTOG MED PA'I SEMS KYIS SU BDAG GZHAN RJE BA SGOM PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' LHA SBYIN YIN NA, LHA SBYIN DE LA PHRAG DOG DANG NI MNYAM PA YIN NA 'GRAN SEMS DANG DMAN PA YIN NA NGA RGYAL BSGOM PAR BYA'O,
3860.wylie: byang chub sems dpas sems can rang las dman pa dang mnyam pa dang rang las lhag pa sogs dmigs yul du byas nas bdag tu byas pa dang , bdag nyid gzhan nyid du ni byas nas te bdag gzhan du 'dzin pa'i blo go sa spos nas nges shes drangs te the tshom gyi rnam rtog med pa'i sems kyis su bdag gzhan rje ba sgom pa'i byang chub sems dpa' lha sbyin yin na, lha sbyin de la phrag dog dang ni mnyam pa yin na 'gran sems dang dman pa yin na nga rgyal bsgom par bya'o
3860.english: Here you, the bodhisattva, should focus upon those living beings who are inferior to you, those who are equal, those who are superior, and so on. Then you should make them be yourself, and you should make yourself now be none other than these others; that is, you should reverse the states of mind which hold to "me" and "other." When you engage in this practice of exchanging yourself and others then you should do so with a state of mind which is resolved, which is free of any idea such as hesitation about what you're doing. If you are the bodhisattva named "John" then you should practice feeling jealous of John; or if you're equal to him you should practice feeling competitive towards him; or if he's inferior to you, you should practice feeling proud towards him. Contemplation Thirty-Three Bodhisattva talking to yourself

4039.acip: ,SHEL GYI DPE DGAG PA NI DPER NA SHEL BZHIN DU SHEL DKAR PO GZHI'I DBANG GIS SNGON POR SKYES PA NI GZHAN LA LTOS NAS YIN GYI RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS MA YIN LA, BEEd'AU {ry}A SNGON PO NYID LA RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS SNGON POR SKYES PA YIN GYI, GZHAN LA LTOS PA YOD PA MA YIN PA DE BZHIN DU GZUGS LA SOGS PA 'GA' ZHIG RIG PA NI SHES PA GZHAN LA NI LTOS PAS DANG , SHES PA NI RANG GIS RANG RIG PA YIN PAS RIG BYED GZHAN LA LTOS PA MED PA YANG MTHONG ZHE NA, BEEd'AU {ry}A SNGON PO SNGON PAR RGYU GZHAN LAS MA SKYES PA'I DPE DE MI 'THAD PAR THAL, SNGON PO NYID DU RGYU LAS SKYES PA MIN PA LA SNGON PO DE RANG GI BDAG GIS SNGON PO'I BDAG NYID DU BYAS PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO,
4039.wylie: shel gyi dpe dgag pa ni dper na shel bzhin du shel dkar po gzhi'i dbang gis sngon por skyes pa ni gzhan la ltos nas yin gyi rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis ma yin la, beeDAu a sngon po nyid la rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis sngon por skyes pa yin gyi, gzhan la ltos pa yod pa ma yin pa de bzhin du gzugs la sogs pa 'ga' zhig rig pa ni shes pa gzhan la ni ltos pas dang , shes pa ni rang gis rang rig pa yin pas rig byed gzhan la ltos pa med pa yang mthong zhe na, beeDAu a sngon po sngon par rgyu gzhan las ma skyes pa'i dpe de mi 'thad par thal, sngon po nyid du rgyu las skyes pa min pa la sngon po de rang gi bdag gis sngon po'i bdag nyid du byas pa med pa'i phyir ro
4039.english: We turn now to a refutation of the illustration of a piece of crystal. One may make yet another claim, as follows: It's like a piece of crystal. Think of a clear piece of crystal: considered in its original condition, it could never assume a blue hue unless it were due to the influence of some other object--never by virtue of its own essence. The blueness of a piece of lapis though is something that assumes a blue hue by its own essence; it is not something which must rely upon another thing to be the way it is. Just so, the perception of certain objects like visible forms must rely on something else, upon a mind; whereas the mind itself can be seen even without our relying on anything else to perceive it, for it perceives itself. Your example though, of a blueness of lapis which assumes its blueness without any other cause to help it do so, has to be incorrect. This is true because the blueness of blue itself is not something which has not come about through its own causes; blueness is not something that could ever make itself something blue, all by itself.

4092.acip: ,GAL TE BDAG 'GA' RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YOD NA NI DER ZHEN PA LAS YUL CI YANG RUNG BA LAS 'JIGS PA SKYE RIGS PAR 'GYUR NA BDAG NYID 'GA' YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MIN PAS 'JIGS PAR 'GYUR BA PO DE SU ZHIG YIN TE, RANG BZHIN SEMS PA'I BLOS KHA NANG DU LOG LA SOMS SHIG DANG BDAG MED PA KHONG DU CHUD PAS 'JIGS PA MTHA' DAG LAS GROL BAR 'GYUR BA YIN NO,
4092.wylie: gal te bdag 'ga' rang bzhin gyis grub pa yod na ni der zhen pa las yul ci yang rung ba las 'jigs pa skye rigs par 'gyur na bdag nyid 'ga' yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa cung zad kyang yod pa min pas 'jigs par 'gyur ba po de su zhig yin te, rang bzhin sems pa'i blos kha nang du log la soms shig dang bdag med pa khong du chud pas 'jigs pa mtha' dag las grol bar 'gyur ba yin no
4092.english: Only if it were true that there were any self-nature of anything at all then would it be right for you to feel fear towards any object at all, since this fear comes from believing in a self-nature. But since it is not the case that anything has any nature at all which exists by nature, how could there be anyone who is afraid in the first place? Take this state of mind where you think that things have any nature of their own, and turn it around: look inside, and think! You will come to comprehend fully what it means when we say that nothing is itself at all, and you will liberate yourself from every fear there could ever be. An Outline of the Explanation of the Chapter on Wisdom from the Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life, to accompany the Contemplations in Reading Four b. 7341.acip: ,YANG YANG LUS 'DOR BA NI, LUS BZANG PO JI TZAM THOB KYANG ZHES SOGS TE LUS 'TSO SKYONG BYA BA'I PHYIR SDIG PA SNA TSOGS SHIG BSAGS KYANG MTHAR LUS NI NGES PAR 'DOR ZHING DE'I CHED DU BSAGS PA'I SDIG PA THAMS CAD SEMS STENG DU KHYER TE 'BRAS BU SDUG BSNGAL MI BZAD PA MYONG LA, GZHAN YANG RE RE'I BDAG NYID RUS PA'I PHUNG PO NI, , LHUN PO MNYAM PA SNYED GCIG 'DAS GYUR TE, , ZHES SEMS CAN RE RE'I LUS BLANGS NAS DOR BA'I RUS PA RNAMS BSAGS NA RI RAB LHUN PO LAS KYANG MANG BA STE, SNYED CIG CES PA NI LHUN PO DANG MNYAM PA JI SNYED CIG 'DAS ZHES PA'I DON,
7341.wylie: yang yang lus 'dor ba ni, lus bzang po ji tsam thob kyang zhes sogs te lus 'tsho skyong bya ba'i phyir sdig pa sna tshogs shig bsags kyang mthar lus ni nges par 'dor zhing de'i ched du bsags pa'i sdig pa thams cad sems steng du khyer te 'bras bu sdug bsngal mi bzad pa myong la, gzhan yang re re'i bdag nyid rus pa'i phung po ni, , lhun po mnyam pa snyed gcig 'das gyur te, , zhes sems can re re'i lus blangs nas dor ba'i rus pa rnams bsags na ri rab lhun po las kyang mang ba ste, snyed cig ces pa ni lhun po dang mnyam pa ji snyed cig 'das zhes pa'i don
7341.english: The next suffering is [3] the fact that we have to shed our bodies, over and over. This is indicated in the lines that include, "It doesn't matter what wonderful kind of body I may be able to attain..." The point here is that, regardless of all the bad deeds we might accumulate in order to maintain this body we have now, it is an absolute certainty that--in the end--we will be forced to shed it. The power of the wrong deeds we did for the sake of the body though we carry along in our mind, and they bring to us the eventual result of unbearable pain. Beyond this are the lines that say, The size of the stack of rotting corpses belonging to each of us Would exceed an equivalent to the height of Mount Supreme itself. Suppose that you could put together a huge stack of all the skeletons left from the bodies that any particular person had ever taken on, and then left behind. This stack would be more immense than Summit, the great mountain at the middle of the world. The difficult expression nyechik here is meant to indicate "a quantity equivalent to the height," which is then exceeded.
7341.raw: {"course": "C17", "acip": ",YANG YANG LUS 'DOR BA NI, LUS BZANG PO JI TZAM THOB KYANG ZHES SOGS TE LUS 'TSO SKYONG BYA BA'I PHYIR SDIG PA SNA TSOGS SHIG BSAGS KYANG MTHAR LUS NI NGES PAR 'DOR ZHING DE'I CHED DU BSAGS PA'I SDIG PA THAMS CAD SEMS STENG DU KHYER TE 'BRAS BU SDUG BSNGAL MI BZAD PA MYONG LA, GZHAN YANG RE RE'I BDAG NYID RUS PA'I PHUNG PO NI, , LHUN PO MNYAM PA SNYED GCIG 'DAS GYUR TE, , ZHES SEMS CAN RE RE'I LUS BLANGS NAS DOR BA'I RUS PA RNAMS BSAGS NA RI RAB LHUN PO LAS KYANG MANG BA STE, SNYED CIG CES PA NI LHUN PO DANG MNYAM PA JI SNYED CIG 'DAS ZHES PA'I DON,", "wylie": "yang yang lus 'dor ba ni, lus bzang po ji tsam thob kyang zhes sogs te lus 'tsho skyong bya ba'i phyir sdig pa sna tshogs shig bsags kyang mthar lus ni nges par 'dor zhing de'i ched du bsags pa'i sdig pa thams cad sems steng du khyer te 'bras bu sdug bsngal mi bzad pa myong la, gzhan yang re re'i bdag nyid rus pa'i phung po ni, , lhun po mnyam pa snyed gcig 'das gyur te, , zhes sems can re re'i lus blangs nas dor ba'i rus pa rnams bsags na ri rab lhun po las kyang mang ba ste, snyed cig ces pa ni lhun po dang mnyam pa ji snyed cig 'das zhes pa'i don", "english": "The next suffering is [3] the fact that we have to shed our bodies, over and over. This is indicated in the lines that include, \"It doesn't matter what wonderful kind of body I may be able to attain...\" The point here is that, regardless of all the bad deeds we might accumulate in order to maintain this body we have now, it is an absolute certainty that--in the end--we will be forced to shed it. The power of the wrong deeds we did for the sake of the body though we carry along in our mind, and they bring to us the eventual result of unbearable pain. Beyond this are the lines that say, The size of the stack of rotting corpses belonging to each of us Would exceed an equivalent to the height of Mount Supreme itself. Suppose that you could put together a huge stack of all the skeletons left from the bodies that any particular person had ever taken on, and then left behind. This stack would be more immense than Summit, the great mountain at the middle of the world. 7482.wylie: de ltar na tshe 'di'i phun tshogs thams cad ni rmi lam thun gcig na bde ba spyad bsad nas dran pa ltar 'chi ba'i dus su dran pa'i yul tsam du 'gyur la, 'chi ba'i dgra ni dgag tu med par nges par 'ong na ci'i phyir tshe 'di'i bslu brid la dga' bar bya snyam du bsams te chos bya dgos pa la thag bcad cing zhe dam mang du bya ste, skyes rabs las, kye ma'o 'jig rten nyon mongs dag, gnas pa mi brtan dga' mi 'gyur, , ku mu ta yi dpal 'di yang , , dran par bya ba nyid du 'gyur, , 'gro ba 'di lta bur ni 'khod pa la, , skye bo 'jigs pa med pa ngo mtshar kye, , lam rnams thams cad 'chi bdag nyid kyis bkag, dogs pa med par rab tu dga' zhing spyod, , na dang rga dang 'chi ba'i gnod byed dgra, , mthu chen dgag tu mi nus yod bzhin la, , 'jig rten pha rol nyam ngar nges 'gro na, , sems shes su zhig 'di la dga' bar sems, , zhes dang
7482.english: And so all the good things of this life are like the happiness within one night's dream: you wake, and then it's nothing more than a memory. The time comes to die, and everything good you ever had lives only in a dim remembrance. This great enemy, death, will surely come; nothing can stop him. You should contemplate this fact--try to wonder, "Why do I take such pleasure in the lie of this life?" Make up your mind that you absolutely must now practice some Dharma; swear it to yourself, continually. Remember the Birth Stories, where it says: Alas, you worldly ones so full of affliction of the mind; Why do you take such pleasure in a land of shifting sands? The shining glory of the kumuda bloom, opening to the moon, Soon enough turns nothing more than a simple memory. It's something of a pure amazement too that all of us Thrust into a life like this are not consumed by total fear; Damn the Lord of Death, who stands and blocks all pathways out, While we oblivious feel content, and have an enjoyable day. We all share enemies, dreadfully powerful, ones we cannot stop: Their names are sickness, age, and death; they attack us even now. If it's certain that we are headed for agony in the world beyond, How could anyone with a mind be content in the one here now?

7707.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, GZHAN RGYUD KYI NYON MONGS GZHOM BAR KHAS BLANGS PA YIN MOD, RANG RGYUD KYI NYON MONGS GZHOM PA'I CHED DU BRTZON PAR MI RIGS TE, DE LTAR NA ZHI BA'I MTHAR LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BAS SO ZHE NA PHYOGS BCU NAM MKHA'I MTHAS GTUGS PA'I 'GRO BA THAMS CAD NYON MONGS LAS SGROL BAR SEMS BSKYED CING DAM BCAS NAS GANG GI TSE BDAG NYID KYANG NYON MONGS RNAMS LAS MA GROL BA YIN NA GZHAN DON LTA ZHOG RANG DON YANG RDZOGS PAR MI NUS PAS NYON MONGS PA'I GZHAN DBANG DU GYUR PA'I BDAG GI TSOD KYANG MI SHES PAR GZHAN MTHA' DAG NYON MONGS LAS SGROL BAR SMRA BA JI LTAR SMYON PA MIN TE, RANG 'KHOR BAR BCINGS PAS GZHAN DON RDZOGS PAR MI NUS PAS RANG RGYUD KYI NYON MONGS GZHOM PA LA BRTZON PAR BYA'O,
7707.wylie: gsum pa ni, gzhan rgyud kyi nyon mongs gzhom bar khas blangs pa yin mod, rang rgyud kyi nyon mongs gzhom pa'i ched du brtson par mi rigs te, de ltar na zhi ba'i mthar ltung bar 'gyur bas so zhe na phyogs bcu nam mkha'i mthas gtugs pa'i 'gro ba thams cad nyon mongs las sgrol bar sems bskyed cing dam bcas nas gang gi tshe bdag nyid kyang nyon mongs rnams las ma grol ba yin na gzhan don lta zhog rang don yang rdzogs par mi nus pas nyon mongs pa'i gzhan dbang du gyur pa'i bdag gi tshod kyang mi shes par gzhan mtha' dag nyon mongs las sgrol bar smra ba ji ltar smyon pa min te, rang 'khor bar bcings pas gzhan don rdzogs par mi nus pas rang rgyud kyi nyon mongs gzhom pa la brtson par bya'o
7707.english: Here is the third point. Someone might make the following statement: "I admit that I am a person who has agreed to undertake the destruction of the mental afflictions within the minds of other persons. It would be wrong though for me to work to destroy the mental afflictions in my own mind, because if I succeeded in doing so I would have fallen into what is called the 'extreme of personal peace.'" You have though pledged yourself, and developed the wish, to free all living beings, beings as vast in extent as the ten different directions of space itself, from their mental afflictions. If at the same time you have failed to free you yourself from all your own mental afflictions, then you have failed even in the endeavor of accomplishing all your own needs, much less those of others. Are you not some kind of madman then, to say that you are going to free every other living being from their mental afflictions, while at the very same moment you have failed completely to judge your own level--the fact that you yourself are still at the mercy of your own mental afflictions? No one chained in the cycle of suffering of life themselves could ever accomplish all the goals of other living beings, and so you should rather make efforts to destroy the mental afflictions within your own mind. 7 Hating your Mental Afflictions

7896.wylie: brtson 'grus de'i mi mthun phyogs bshad par bya'o, , gang zhe na, lus dang yid las su mi rung ba snyom las kyi bde ba la zhen pa'i le lo dang , bya ba ngan pa la zhen pa dang , dge ba bsgrub pa la sgyid lug nas ngas mi nus snyam du bdag nyid la brnyas pa'o
7896.english: Here next I will explain the things that work against "it"--meaning effort. What exactly are they? First there is laziness, which is feeling attracted to the pleasant feeling of sloth, a condition where the mind and body become unfit to function well. Next there is an attraction to actions which are bad, and then finally the feeling of being discouraged when you try to accomplish some virtuous act--where you belittle yourself by saying, "This is something I could never accomplish." Contemplation Four What causes laziness?

8092.acip: ,GAL TE BDAG 'GA' RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YOD NA NI DER ZHEN PA LAS YUL CI YANG RUNG BA LAS 'JIGS PA SKYE RIGS PAR 'GYUR NA BDAG NYID 'GA' YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MIN PAS 'JIGS PAR 'GYUR BA PO DE SU ZHIG YIN TE, RANG BZHIN SEMS PA'I BLOS KHA NANG DU LOG LA SOMS SHIG DANG BDAG MED PA KHONG DU CHUD PAS 'JIGS PA MTHA' DAG LAS GROL BAR 'GYUR BA YIN NO,
8092.wylie: gal te bdag 'ga' rang bzhin gyis grub pa yod na ni der zhen pa las yul ci yang rung ba las 'jigs pa skye rigs par 'gyur na bdag nyid 'ga' yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa cung zad kyang yod pa min pas 'jigs par 'gyur ba po de su zhig yin te, rang bzhin sems pa'i blos kha nang du log la soms shig dang bdag med pa khong du chud pas 'jigs pa mtha' dag las grol bar 'gyur ba yin no
8092.english: Only if it were true that there were any self-nature of anything at all then would it be right for you to feel fear towards any object at all, since this fear comes from believing in a self-nature. But since it is not the case that anything has any nature at all which exists by nature, how could there be anyone who is afraid in the first place? Take this state of mind where you think that things have any nature of their own, and turn it around: look inside, and think! You will come to comprehend fully what it means when we say that nothing is itself at all, and you will liberate yourself from every fear there could ever be. Contemplation Sixteen The Two Kinds of Grasping to Self-Existence

35501.wylie: khyod la chod chod mang yod pas, ,bsam blo thong la lan cig thog ,sva bhA wa yi sngags don ni, ,chos rnams kun gyi rang bzhin ni, ,rnam par dag pa'i bdag nyid de
35501.english: What you want to do Is slice things and dissect them In way too many ways. You need to sit down And give it some thought: If just a single time You were to pronounce The secret word svabhava, Then that would represent The true nature Of all the things there are; For this is embodiment Of every form of purity. Now we're transitioning into a concept from the secret traditions of Buddhism.  This is where—so that we come to appreciate emptiness more fully, during all of our life—we do a meditation where we imagine that we are that emptiness, of all the things there are in the whole universe. There are some obvious dangers here if our understanding of emptiness is still not fully matured.  People—and the parts of people, body & mind—are changing things, in a state of constant flux as the causes & conditions that have created them come & go. Emptiness, on the other hand—like that fact that 2 and 2 is 4—is a never-changing truth: the fact that nothing in the universe is coming from its own side, rather than from our own mental seeds, planted by how we have behaved towards other people. Pretending that we are emptiness though would at the very least have the result of getting us to think about it pretty constantly! The term used for emptiness in this context is the Sanskrit word svabhava.  The sva here means “self,” while the bhava means “nature”—the point being that emptiness is the ultimate self-nature of everything there is.  Or, to put it the other way around, it is the nature of

35514.wylie: shU n+ya tA yi sngags don yang, ,yul ni stong dang yul can ni, ,rang bzhin dbyer ni mi phyed pa'i, ,bdag nyid nga'o zhes bsgom na, ,yul can su yis byas nas ni, ,nga rgyal ci 'dra zhig gis bsgom
35514.english: Now suppose You try to explain The meaning of this Secret expression, Shunyata, Still further— And you say You are doing a meditation Where “I am a combination Of the object, emptiness, And the subject, Joined together in a single Nature, indivisible.” Who was it though That created this Subject state of mind? And just what kind Of divine pride Is doing the meditation? Back in verse 481, we saw the Sanskrit word svabhava—or “self-nature”—as a term for the emptiness which all entities in the universe possess.  Here in this part of our text, Sanskrit words like this are being utilized with an almost mystical connotation, which indeed they well deserve. Now we have reached the word shunyata used in a similar way—with the status of a high secret mantra.  Shunyata of course is the original Sanskrit for “emptiness.” That is, the ending -ta on any Sanskrit word can connote a state of being, or -ness.  The root shu, referring to “being empty,” relates to an old Indo-European root connected to kshu.  This then came into words for places with empty space, like “cave” and “cavity”—and even “church,” as a place swollen with holy power. In this case, our author is referring to a practice in the secret teachings where we now equate ourselves with the union of the mighty concept of emptiness, and the wisdom which sees it directly. This recalls the sacred union of the female and the male, both in the universe as a whole, and within our own inner body.  And again there is this diabolical hesi
35514.raw: {"course": "DDA", "acip": ",SH'U N+YA T'A YI SNGAGS DON YANG, ,YUL NI STONG DANG YUL CAN NI, ,RANG BZHIN DBYER NI MI PHYED PA'I, ,BDAG NYID NGA'O ZHES BSGOM NA, ,YUL CAN SU YIS BYAS NAS NI, ,NGA RGYAL CI 'DRA ZHIG GIS BSGOM,", "wylie": "shU n+ya tA yi sngags don yang, ,yul ni stong dang yul can ni, ,rang bzhin dbyer ni mi phyed pa'i, ,bdag nyid nga'o zhes bsgom na, ,yul can su yis byas nas ni, ,nga rgyal ci 'dra zhig gis bsgom", "english": "Now suppose You try to explain The meaning of this Secret expression, Shunyata, Still further— And you say You are doing a meditation Where “I am a combination Of the object, emptiness, And the subject, Joined together in a single Nature, indivisible.” Who was it though That created this Subject state of mind? And just what kind Of divine pride Is doing the meditation? Back in verse 481, we saw the Sanskrit word svabhava—or “self-nature”—as a term for the emptiness which all entities in the universe possess.  Here in this part of our text, Sanskrit words like this are being utilized with an almost mystical connotation, which indeed they well deserve. Now we have reached the word shunyata used in a similar way—with the status of a high secret mantra.  Shunyata of course is the original Sanskrit for “emptiness.” That is, the ending -ta on any Sanskrit word can connote a state of being, or -ness.  The root shu, referring to “being empty,” relates to an old Indo-European root connected to kshu.  This then came into words for places with empty space, like “cave” and “cavity”—and even “church,” as a place swollen with holy power. In this case, our author is referring to a practice in the secret teachings where we now equate ourselves with the union of the mighty concept of emptiness, and the wisdom which sees it directly. 24045.english: Here next is that second point, on the literal meaning of the name of this system.  They are, first of all, known as the “Mind Only” school because they say that no outer objects exist—that all three realms of the universe are nothing more than part & parcel with the mind itself.  For this same reason, they are sometimes referred to as the “Mentalist” belief system.  We also see them called the school of “Precise Practice.”

24080.acip: DE'I TSE SNGON PO LTA BU DE 'DZIN PA'I SHES PA LAS RDZAS GZHAN DU MED DE, DPER NA, RMI LAM DU RI RAB SOGS SNANG BA'I TSE SEMS MA YIN KYANG SEMS KYI BDAG NYID DU GYUR PA'I RI SOGS YOD CING, SEMS LAS DON GZHAN PA'I RI SOGS MED PA BZHIN NO,,
24080.wylie: de'i tshe sngon po lta bu de 'dzin pa'i shes pa las rdzas gzhan du med de, dper na, rmi lam du ri rab sogs snang ba'i tshe sems ma yin kyang sems kyi bdag nyid du gyur pa'i ri sogs yod cing, sems las don gzhan pa'i ri sogs med pa bzhin no
24080.english: It is not though the case, at this moment in time, that something like the blue is such that to be it is not to be the very awareness which is holding to it.  Let's say, as an illustration, that a mountain appears to us in a dream.  It's not that the mountain is our own mind; but we can say that there are mountains there in the dream which are part & parcel with our mind.  Or, we can say, there is no mountain or something of the like in the dream which is an entity that is distinct from our mind.

24668.acip: [E61] CI'I PHYIR BYANG CHUB YAN LAG CES BYA ZHE NA, DBUS MTHA'I 'GREL BSHAD LAS, MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR BYANG CHUB NI RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I YE SHES SO, ,DE LA DRAN PA LA SOGS PA BDUN NI BYANG CHUB DANG MTHUN PA'I PHYIR DE'I YAN LAG GO, CHOS RAB TU RNAM 'BYED NI RTOGS PA'I BDAG NYID YIN PAS NA BYANG CHUB STE, DE DAG GI GROGS SU GYUR PAS NA YAN LAG GO, ZHES PA LTAR RO,,

24668.english: You might wonder why we refer to these seven as “components of enlightenment.”  The answer to this question may be found in the Explication of “Distinguishing between the Middle and the Extremes,” where it says— What does it mean to reach total enlightenment?  It means reaching the wisdom beyond all thinking this or that.  And clear awareness and the rest of the seven—in that they are conducive to reaching this enlightenment—are referred to as its “components.”  The very identity of the ability to make final distinctions about reality is one of realization; and, as such, it is enlightenment.  All the states of mind that are tied to this ability we can refer to then as its “components.” G. The eight components of the path of the realized (aspects 30–37)

27256.wylie: [d12] ngag don ni, lhan cig dmigs nges kyi rtags las sngon po sngo snang dbang shes dang rdzas gzhan min par nges pa'i blo chos can, khyod kyis sngon po phyi rol gyi don du zhen pa'i sgro 'dogs kun brtags mngon gyur mgo gnon nus te, khyad kyis sngon po sems kyi dang gnyid {%kyi bdag nyid} yin par nges pa'i blo tshad ma gzhan la ltos med du 'dren nus pa'i phyir
27256.english: Here then is how we express the meaning of the statement here, in a syllogism: Let us consider the state of mind where we ascertain—through a reason which helps us ascertain that they are perceived together—the fact that the blue does not consist of any substance separate from the sense awareness which has taken on an aspect of the blue. This state of mind acts to suppress the manifest appearance of the learned tendency to exaggerate the reality of the situation, where we believe that the blue is an outer object; Because this state has the power to elicit—without depending on any other factor—an accurate state of mind where we ascertain that the blue is part and parcel with the mind itself. The third level of deep practice

29428.english: Our reasoning above is further supported by the fact that—when, in both the root text and the autocommentary the Master denies this type of reasoning—there are many examples where qualifications are placed upon the object that we deny with emptiness. And we do see as well that part in the root text which says— …And then how Could it be in it For the Great Being To state that the mind Was born from Dark ignorance And karma? That is, the statement that misunderstanding triggers fresh karma, and then fresh karma in turn triggers consciousness, also represents our own system. As such, nobody with good understanding would entertain the suspicion that people in the school we're discussing here would assert that there was no consciousness.

29666.acip: SNGAR RGYAS PAR BSHAD PA RNAMS KYI DON MDOR BSDU NA SHES BYA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA JI LTA BA DE BZHIN DU SHES BYA'I RNAM PA CAN GYI BLO YANG RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS SKYES PA MED CES DON 'DI SHES PAR GYIS SHING GCES GSUNGS PAS,

29666.english: Suppose then we were to summarize the points that we have covered in detail so far. The fact is that there is nothing in the universe which exists through some nature of its own. Just so, there is no state of mind which takes on the aspect of these existing entities which could arise in & of itself. This, the root text is telling us, is the point which we need to understand.

29738.acip: CI STE DE LTAR RNAM PAR DPYOD PA BTANG NAS KYANG, SHES PAS RANG GI BDAG NYID RIG PA DANG, YUL RIG PAR BYED PA NI GRUB LA RAG MOD KYI STE GRUB TU CHUG KYANG, DRAN PA'I SHES PAS YUL DANG YUL CAN DE DAG DRAN PA NI RIGS PA MIN TE, PHYIS KYI DRAN SHES DANG SNGAR GYI YUL MYONG GI SHES PA GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN NYID DU KHYED KYIS KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
29738.wylie: ci ste de ltar rnam par dpyod pa btang nas kyang, shes pas rang gi bdag nyid rig pa dang, yul rig par byed pa ni grub la rag mod kyi ste grub tu chug kyang, dran pa'i shes pas yul dang yul can de dag dran pa ni rigs pa min te, phyis kyi dran shes dang sngar gyi yul myong gi shes pa gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan nyid du khyed kyis khas blangs pa'i phyir ro
29738.english: You may undertake some different forms of examination, but in the end your proofs are going to rely upon the idea of a state of mind knowing itself—its own self—and also knowing the particular object. But still it is not logical to say that the state of mind of recollection can recall both the subject and the object involved. And this is simply because you have accepted the idea that both the later recollecting state of mind and the earlier awareness which perceived the object are objects that are other than each other and which exist through some nature of their own.

29983.wylie: gal te 'di dag sems tsam zhes mkhyen nas, ,de las gzugs nyid dgag par mdzad na ni, ,slar yang de las bdag nyid chen pos sems, ,gti mug las las skyes par ci phyir gsungs
29983.english: Suppose all these Were referred to As “only the mind,” And the Buddha Knew this, and so Meant in this To deny “form itself.” And then how Could it be in it For the Great Being To state that the mind Was born from Dark ignorance And karma?

29985.acip: SLAR YANG SA BCU PA DE LAS BDAG NYID CHEN PO SANGS RGYAS KYIS SEMS TE RNAM SHES DE MA RIG PA'I RKYEN GYIS 'DU BYED, 'DU BYED KYI RKYEN GYIS RNAM SHES ZHES GTI MUG MA RIG PA DANG, 'DU BYED LAS GNYIS LAS SKYES PAR CI'I PHYIR GSUNGS PA RIGS TE MI RIGS SO,,
29985.wylie: slar yang sa bcu pa de las bdag nyid chen po sangs rgyas kyis sems te rnam shes de ma rig pa'i rkyen gyis 'du byed, 'du byed kyi rkyen gyis rnam shes zhes gti mug ma rig pa dang, 'du byed las gnyis las skyes par ci'i phyir gsungs pa rigs te mi rigs so
29985.english: And then how could it be correct for The Ten Levels to go further, and in it for the Great Being—the Buddha—to state that the mind, which is to say consciousness, triggered (through the factor of misunderstanding) fresh karma; and that then the factor of fresh karma triggered consciousness? That is, how could it be correct for him to have stated that these things were born from the two of misunderstanding—dark ignorance—and the fresh type of karma? It could not have then been correct!

30197.acip: ,'BYUNG BA DE DAG BDAG NYID GANG ZHIG GIS NI KHYOD KYI BLO'I, ,YUL DU 'GYUR BA DE YI BDAG NYID CAN NI MA YIN NA, ,GANG LA YID KYI MUN PA 'THUG PO 'DI NYID DU YOD PA, ,DES NI JI LTAR 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL YANG DAG RTOGS PAR 'GYUR,
30197.wylie: 'byung ba de dag bdag nyid gang zhig gis ni khyod kyi blo'i, ,yul du 'gyur ba de yi bdag nyid can ni ma yin na, ,gang la yid kyi mun pa 'thug po 'di nyid du yod pa, ,des ni ji ltar 'jig rten pha rol yang dag rtogs par 'gyur
30197.english: It is only constructs Of these elements Which can serve as The object of your mind. And if things Were not such constructs, Then how on earth Could that which is The thick darkness Of your mind itself Ever come to grasp, In a correct way, A world beyond This one?

30198.acip: SA LA SOGS PA'I 'BYUNG BA BZHI PO DE DAG KHYOD KYI GZHUNG LAS BSHAD PA'I BDAG NYID GANG ZHIG GIS NI KHYOD KYI BLO'I YUL DU GYUR PA DE LTAR DE YI BDAG NYID CAN DU NI YOD PA MA YIN NA SHIN TU RAGS PA'I DON GANG LA YID KYI MUN PA 'THUG PO 'DI NYID DU YOD PA DES NI, JI LTAR NA SHIN TU PHRA BA'I 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL YOD PA DANG MED PA GANG YANG YANG DAG PAR RTOGS PAR 'GYUR TE RTOGS PA MED DO,,
30198.wylie: sa la sogs pa'i 'byung ba bzhi po de dag khyod kyi gzhung las bshad pa'i bdag nyid gang zhig gis ni khyod kyi blo'i yul du gyur pa de ltar de yi bdag nyid can du ni yod pa ma yin na shin tu rags pa'i don gang la yid kyi mun pa 'thug po 'di nyid du yod pa des ni, ji ltar na shin tu phra ba'i 'jig rten pha rol yod pa dang med pa gang yang yang dag par rtogs par 'gyur te rtogs pa med do
30198.english: According to your scriptures, it is only constructs of these four elements of earth and the rest which can serve as the object of your mind. And if it happened to be the case that there were things that did not exist as such constructs, then let's think about what is that thick darkness of your mind itself, holding on to its forms that are so gross in their nature. How on earth then could it ever come to grasp, in a correct way, the existence or lack of existence of an extremely subtle world beyond this one? The fact is that it could not.

11259.acip: DBYER MED DU MOS TSUL YANG, MA 'ONGS PA NA RANG RGYUD LA 'BYUNG RUNG GI YE SHES PA DANG BDAG NYID DBYER MED DU MOS PA GTZO BO DANG, DA LTA GZHAN RGYUD LA BYUNG ZIN GYI YE SHES PA DANG BDAG NYID DBYER MED DU MOS PA GDUL BYA BAR MA'I DBANG DU BYAS PAR GSUNGS,
11259.wylie: dbyer med du mos tshul yang, ma 'ongs pa na rang rgyud la 'byung rung gi ye shes pa dang bdag nyid dbyer med du mos pa gtso bo dang, da lta gzhan rgyud la byung zin gyi ye shes pa dang bdag nyid dbyer med du mos pa gdul bya bar ma'i dbang du byas par gsungs
11259.english: Exactly how is it that we think of Them and us as being indivisible?  The main thing to keep in mind is that we are indivisible from the Wisdom Being that we ourselves will become in the future.  Our Lama made sure to say that this idea of imagining that we are indivisible from some Wisdom Being outside of us, a Wisdom Being that someone else has already become, is an idea meant only for disciples of moderate spiritual intelligence. 13 Mantra for Outer Offerings to the Slayer (Sadhana) The mantra
