11696.acip: GAL TE DE LTA YIN NA, RDO RJE THEG PA'I RTZA LTUNG NI GRANGS MANG LA 'BYUNG NYE BAR SNANG LA BSTAN PA 'GRIB PA LA NYE BAR SLEB PAS GONG MA GNYIS KYI THA NA RTZA BA'I BSLAB TSIGS TZAM YANG NGES PAR BYAS NAS BSRUNG BA SHIN TU DKON PAR SNANG BAS THEG PA MCHOG GI SDOM PA DANG LDAN PA MED PAR MI 'GYUR RAM SNYAM NA, DE'I SKYON MED DE SLOB MA DBANG BSKUR BA RNAMS LA SNGON DU SLOB DPON BDAG NYID DKYIL 'KHOR DU ZHUGS NAS DBANG DANG DAM TSIG DANG SDOM PA RNAMS LEN PA'I PHYAG LEN YOD,
11696.wylie: gal te de lta yin na, rdo rje theg pa'i rtsa ltung ni grangs mang la 'byung nye bar snang la bstan pa 'grib pa la nye bar sleb pas gong ma gnyis kyi tha na rtsa ba'i bslab tshigs tsam yang nges par byas nas bsrung ba shin tu dkon par snang bas theg pa mchog gi sdom pa dang ldan pa med par mi 'gyur ram snyam na, de'i skyon med de slob ma dbang bskur ba rnams la sngon du slob dpon bdag nyid dkyil 'khor du zhugs nas dbang dang dam tshig dang sdom pa rnams len pa'i phyag len yod
11696.english: Now the following thought may come up in your mind: Suppose that what you've just said is true.  The fact though is that there are a great many different root downfalls here in the diamond way; and we can see that at any given point in the day we are not very far from committing one.  We are moreover living in the twilight days of the teaching itself, and people are bound at some point to overstep some small detail of these root guidelines within the two higher sets of vows. As such it would appear that a person who has not committed a root downfall is extremely rare to find; you could practically say that, according to you, there's not a single person around who does possess the vows of the highest way. And yet there is no such problem, for a practice has developed where, when they are about to grant their own disciples an empowerment, the Master first enters the mandala themselves, to re-take the empowerment, the pledges, and the vows. ***

11805.acip: LAS DANG PO PAS GSUNG RAB MTHA' DAG LA MOS PA SKYE DKA' BAS, MOS PA MA SKYES KYANG SKUR PA MI 'DEBS NA NYES PA MED PAR BYANG SA LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD DU YANG GSUNGS TE JI SKAD DU, MOS PA DU MA'I SEMS CAN LA, ,SPYOD PA SNA TSOGS STON MDZAD DE, ,SNA TSOGS TSUL GYIS GDUL BYA LA, ,THABS NI SNA TSOGS STON PA YIN, ,ZAB MO'I CHOS NI STON PA LA, ,GAL TE MOS PAR MA GYUR KYANG , ,SMOD PA DAG NI MI BYA STE, ,CHOS NYID BSAM MI KHYAB DRAN BYA, ,GANG GIS 'DI BDAG YUL MIN PA, ,BDAG GIS CHOS NYID MI SHES YIN, ,RDZOGS SANGS RGYAS DANG DE SRAS NI, ,BDAG NYID CHEN PO RNAMS KYIS MKHYEN, ,ZHES GSUNGS SHING MDO SDE RGYAN DANG RIN CHEN PHRENG BA LAS KYANG , BTANG SNYOMS SU BZHAG PA LA NYES PA MED PAR GSUNGS PA 'DI GNAD CHE'O, ,THEG PA GSUM GYI CHOS SDONG BA DE NI RTZA LTUNG DRUG PA YIN NO,
11805.wylie: las dang po pas gsung rab mtha' dag la mos pa skye dka' bas, mos pa ma skyes kyang skur pa mi 'debs na nyes pa med par byang sa las gsungs pa ltar bde mchog rtsa rgyud du yang gsungs te ji skad du, mos pa du ma'i sems can la, ,spyod pa sna tshogs ston mdzad de, ,sna tshogs tshul gyis gdul bya la, ,thabs ni sna tshogs ston pa yin, ,zab mo'i chos ni ston pa la, ,gal te mos par ma gyur kyang , ,smod pa dag ni mi bya ste, ,chos nyid bsam mi khyab dran bya, ,gang gis 'di bdag yul min pa, ,bdag gis chos nyid mi shes yin, ,rdzogs sangs rgyas dang de sras ni, ,bdag nyid chen po rnams kyis mkhyen, ,zhes gsungs shing mdo sde rgyan dang rin chen phreng ba las kyang , btang snyoms su bzhag pa la nyes pa med par gsungs pa 'di gnad che'o, ,theg pa gsum gyi chos sdong ba de ni rtsa ltung drug pa yin no
11805.english: It's very difficult for those who are just starting out to right away feel a deep belief for each and every teaching of the Buddha.  As such, we should follow the advice of the Levels of the Bodhisattva, where it says that "There's no problem if they don't believe it; as long as they don't discount it." This same point is made in the root tantra of Highest Bliss" Living beings possess a wide variety of propensities; And so They teach them a variety of activities. They teach a wide variety of different methods To beings, in a whole variety of ways. What They teach is a Dharma that's profound; And so even if it doesn't attract us immediately, We should never think of disparaging it-- Remind yourself how inconceivable The nature of things really is: If there's something that we can't get just yet, It's because we don't grasp reality. These great beings, the Buddhas And Their daughters and sons, Know perfectly what we need. The Jewel of Realizations and the String of Jewels also state that there is no problem if we simply leave, for the time being, a teaching which we cannot yet accept; it's a crucial point of practice for us to understand this.  The sixth of the root downfalls is to give up then any Dharma of the three different ways. *** We return to the String of Shining Jewels, for the seventh root downfall:

12163.acip: ,DAM TSIG SPYOD PA 'DAS PA YI, ,RMONGS PA'I BDAG NYID DE 'THOB BO, ,SLOB MA DE YANG DE BZHIN DU, ,BLO ZHAN SDUG BSNGAL 'THOB 'GYUR TE,

12163.english: This is the kind of goal That this very embodiment Of stupidity, a person Who transgresses the life Of the pledges they have taken, Will achieve. And their disciples Will turn out the same, Their only attainment A feeble state of mind And pain.

12268.acip: YANG KHO NA RE, LTA BA DANG RGOD PA SOGS LAS BYUNG BA'I BDE BA GSUM GYIS STONG NYID RTOGS PA MED PAR THAL, DE DAG LAM DU BYED PA NI STONG NYID RTOGS PA'I YUL CAN KHYAD PAR CAN SKYED PA'I DON DU MA YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA DPYAD PAR BYA STE, RJES 'JUG PHAL CHER GYIS DE 'DRA YOD PAR BSHAD KYANG , RJE BDAG NYID CHEN PO'I LEGS BSHAD RNAMS SU DE LTAR GSAL BAR GSUNGS PA'I SHES BYED YOD MED TSOL DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
12268.wylie: yang kho na re, lta ba dang rgod pa sogs las byung ba'i bde ba gsum gyis stong nyid rtogs pa med par thal, de dag lam du byed pa ni stong nyid rtogs pa'i yul can khyad par can skyed pa'i don du ma yin pa'i phyir zer na dpyad par bya ste, rjes 'jug phal cher gyis de 'dra yod par bshad kyang , rje bdag nyid chen po'i legs bshad rnams su de ltar gsal bar gsungs pa'i shes byed yod med tshol dgos pa'i phyir ro
12268.english: In response to all this, someone else may come and say, Are you saying then that we don't use the three different kinds of pleasure that we feel from looking into each other's eyes, flirting, and the rest to perceive emptiness?  Because you have stated that using these as a path is not something which is done in order to give rise to the extraordinary state of mind which perceives emptiness. Our reply is that this is a question which needs to be looked into further.  Later generations of writers have, for the most part, expressed the opinion that in those classes of teachings the pleasure is used in that way.  We have to see though whether or not in the high writings of the Lord himself there is any clear statement that this is the case.

15003.acip: 'DI NI NGES DON GYI BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR KYANG YIN ZHING, LAM 'DI LTA BUR NAN DU 'BAD NA BLA MCHOD KYI, BDAG NYID BLA MA LHAR GYUR NAS, SOGS LTAR THUGS YID GCIG 'DRES DANG RANG NYID BLA MA'I GO 'PHANG 'THOB PA'ANG RING POR MI THOGS PAR NGES PAR 'ONG BA YIN GSUNGS,
15003.wylie: 'di ni nges don gyi bla ma'i rnal 'byor kyang yin zhing, lam 'di lta bur nan du 'bad na bla mchod kyi, bdag nyid bla ma lhar gyur nas, sogs ltar thugs yid gcig 'dres dang rang nyid bla ma'i go 'phang 'thob pa'ang ring por mi thogs par nges par 'ong ba yin gsungs
15003.english: And this, said our Lama, is the real Practice of the Lama; if we make great efforts in this path, He said, we shall surely in short time reach the state of our Lama, where our own mind and Theirs are mixed as one; where the words of the Offering to Lamas have come true: "I too become The Angel, my Lama..." *  *  *  *  * Here begins the continuation of Master Quicksilver's commentary-- The Offering of Kusali

15038.acip: SNANG BA SNA TSOGS 'CHAR BA BLA MA SPRUL SKU, BDE BA CHEN PO BLA MA LONGS SKU, STONG PA NYID BLA MA CHOS SKU, STONG NYID LA GNYIS SNANG GIS MA BSLAD PA NGO BO NYID SKU STE BLA MA SKU BZHI'I BDAG NYID RANG SEMS LA TSANG BA YIN PAS DE NI NGES DON GYI BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR RAM, RANG SEMS BLA MAR BLTA BA'ANG DE YIN NO,
15038.wylie: snang ba sna tshogs 'char ba bla ma sprul sku, bde ba chen po bla ma longs sku, stong pa nyid bla ma chos sku, stong nyid la gnyis snang gis ma bslad pa ngo bo nyid sku ste bla ma sku bzhi'i bdag nyid rang sems la tshang ba yin pas de ni nges don gyi bla ma'i rnal 'byor ram, rang sems bla mar blta ba'ang de yin no
15038.english: See your own mind as perfectly embodying the combination of your Lama's four holy bodies.  Her or His Emanation Body is represented by the appearance of various forms in your mind.  Their Enjoyment Body is represented by the great bliss you feel, and Their Dharma Body by the emptiness you perceive.  Their Essence Body is represented by the fact that this emptiness is totally free of the infection of things appearing in a dualistic way.  The true Practice of the Lama is to think in this way.  It is to see your own mind as your Lama.

15225.acip: SNGAGS DON NI, AOm NI SNGAGS KYI MGO 'DREN, SH'U N+YA T'A YUL STONG PA YID, DZNY'A NA YE SHES TE YUL CAN BDE BA CHEN PO, BADZRA RDO RJE STE BDE STONG DBYER MI PHYED PA, SVA BH'A WA RANG BZHIN, A'ATMA KA BDAG NYID, AA HAm NI NGA'O ZHES PA'O,
15225.wylie: sngags don ni, aoM ni sngags kyi mgo 'dren, shU n+ya tA yul stong pa yid, dznyA na ye shes te yul can bde ba chen po, badzra rdo rje ste bde stong dbyer mi phyed pa, sva bhA wa rang bzhin, a'atma ka bdag nyid, aa haM ni nga'o zhes pa'o
15225.english: The meaning of the secret words are as follows.  Om alerts you to the beginning of the secret words.  Shunyata refers to the object, which is emptiness; jnana means wisdom, and refers to the subject state of mind, or great bliss.  Vajra means diamond, or indivisible bliss and voidness.  Svabhava means nature, and atmako means the embodiment.  Aham means I am.

15574.acip: DON DU PHYOGS BCU'I ZHING RAB 'BYAMS KYI SANGS RGYAS BYANG SEMS DPA' BO DPA' MO THAMS CAD KYI SKU GSUNG THUGS GCIG TU BSDUS PA'I BDAG NYID DE NGA'O ZHES BSHAD TSUL GCIG DANG ,

15574.english: The whole line, according to one tradition of commentary, means "I am the holy body, holy speech, and holy mind of each and every Buddha, and bodhisattva, and man and woman Warrior in the vast myriad of paradises in every direction of space; I am all of them, joined in a single being."

16497.wylie: de ltar yig 'bru rnams las 'od zer 'phros pas phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas byang sems rnams kyi sku gsung thugs kyi byin rlabs thams cad rdo rje gsum gyi lha dang 'od zer gyi rnam par bkug nas rang gi gnas gsum du thims pas sgo gsum rdo rje gsum gyi bdag nyid du byin gyis brlab par gyur
16497.english: From the three syllables Come rays of light Which fly out like hooks To all the Enlightened Beings And to all the Warrior Saints In every corner of space. They bring back the blessings Of Their holy words, thoughts, and deeds In the form of rays of light, And the Angels of the three diamonds. These then dissolve into me At the three places on my body, And bless my body, speech, and mind To become the very embodiment Of these three diamonds.

17315.acip: YANG SEMS BSKYED KYI KHONGS SU TSAD MED BZHI 'DUS PA LA DGONGS NAS SEMS BSKYED DANG TSAD MED NGO BO GCIG TU N'A RO PA DANG SA CHEN BZHED PA LAS 'DIR NI PHYI MA BZHIN YIN PAR GSUNGS KYANG, SEMS BSKYED KYI KHONGS SU TSAD MED BZHI TSANG TSUL GZHUNG SNGA MA RNAMS SU MA GSAL YANG, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA DHARMA BHA DRA DPAL BZANG POS RJE BDAG NYID CHEN PO'I DGONGS PA BZHIN GSAL BAR GSUNGS PA ZIN BRIS SU 'KHROD PA LTAR DANG,
17315.wylie: yang sems bskyed kyi khongs su tshad med bzhi 'dus pa la dgongs nas sems bskyed dang tshad med ngo bo gcig tu nA ro pa dang sa chen bzhed pa las 'dir ni phyi ma bzhin yin par gsungs kyang, sems bskyed kyi khongs su tshad med bzhi tshang tshul gzhung snga ma rnams su ma gsal yang, thams cad mkhyen pa dharma bha dra dpal bzang pos rje bdag nyid chen po'i dgongs pa bzhin gsal bar gsungs pa zin bris su 'khrod pa ltar dang
17315.english: On the other hand, the four limitless thoughts can be considered part of the Wish for enlightenment, and it is with this in mind that holy Naropa and Sachen assert that the Wish and the limitless are one and the same.  In our present context, it has been stated that they are taken in this latter way.  But it is unclear in the earlier scriptures exactly how all four limitless thoughts are found within the Wish for enlightenment.  However, the all-knowing glorious pure one, Dharma Bhadra, has made this clear in his Notes,17 in keeping with the true intent of that high Lord himself, Tsongkapa.

However, the all-knowing glorious pure one, Dharma Bhadra, has made this clear in his Notes,17 in keeping with the true intent of that high Lord himself, Tsongkapa."}

1518.english: There is not. In general, all motivation may be divided into two types: the motivation had during the causal stages of a deed and the one we give the name of "motivation at the time." The first of the two acts to set you off: this is where you say before any particular action, "I'm going to do this or that." The second's function is to make you continue on: this is where you say to yourself after you've already started, "Now I'll do this act."

1680.acip: DE LTAR BYAS NA, ZAS SKOM NYID LA YOD PA'I SGRIB PA CAN GYI YI DVAGS KYIS LONGS SPYOD PA LA MA BRTZAMS KYI BAR DU BZA' BTUNG DNGOS YIN KYANG , DES LONGS SPYOD PAR BRTZAMS PA NA, ZAS DE'I RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA YIN GYI, RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED PA MA YIN TE, DE YIN NA LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, DE LTA BU'I YI DVAGS KYIS LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR,
1680.wylie: de ltar byas na, zas skom nyid la yod pa'i sgrib pa can gyi yi dvags kyis longs spyod pa la ma brtsams kyi bar du bza' btung dngos yin kyang , des longs spyod par brtsams pa na, zas de'i rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba yin gyi, rnag khrag tu snang ba'i snang ba tsam gyis bza' btung gi bya ba byed pa ma yin te, de yin na las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir, der thal, de lta bu'i yi dvags kyis las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir
1680.english: Given all this, consider craving spirits that have obstacles that relate to their food and drink itself. The food and drink there really is food and drink, until such time as the spirit starts trying to eat or drink it. When he does try to do so, then the continuum of the food into the next moment starts becoming pus and blood. It is not though that it is the simple appearance of something as pus and blood that could ever function as something to eat or drink. If this were the case, then the rules of karma and its consequences would have to be less that what they really are. And this is true, for if a craving spirit like this ever existed it would represent a failure of the laws of karma and its consequences.

1681.acip: GZHAN YANG , SNANG GZHIR GYUR PA'I RNAG KHRAG MED CING DER SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED NA, RAB RIB CAN LA BSE RU'I NANG DU SKRA SHAD SNANG BAS 'CHING BA DANG , DE LA SNANG BA'I SBRANG BUS LUS ZA BA DANG , SMIG RGYU'I CHUS CHU'I BYA BA BYED NUS PA SOGS YIN PAR THAL, SNANG GZHIR GYUR PA'I RNAG KHRAG MED KYANG , RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED NUS PA'I PHYIR,

1681.english: Suppose moreover that there were no pus and blood out there to appear as the pus and blood, and suppose that the mere appearance of something looking like pus and blood could ever function as something to eat or drink. Well then, you would also have to be able to use a comb on the hair that appears on a porcelain sink to a person with cataracts. And a horsefly that appeared to the same person would have to be able to give him a bite. And the water of a mirage would have to provide all the normal functions of water, and so on. Why so? Well because, according to you, there is no pus and blood out there to appear as pus and blood; according to you, the mere appearance of something looking like pus and blood can provide all the functions of things that you eat and drink.

1777.acip: [IV.377] CI LAS GCIG GIS SKYE BA GCIG KHO NA 'PHEN NAM, 'ON TE DU MA 'PHEN, DE BZHIN DU LAS DU MAS SKYE BA DU MA KHO NA 'PHEN NAM, 'ON TE GCIG RKYANG PA 'PHEN ZHE NA, LAS GCIG GIS SKYE BA GCIG 'PHEN GYI SKYE BA DU MA 'PHEN PA MED LA, RIS MTHUN DUM BUR 'PHEN DU 'ONG BAS NA, LAS DU MAS SKYE BA GCIG 'PHEN PA'ANG MED DO ZHES BYA BA NI BYE BRAG SMRA BA'I LUGS SO,
1777.wylie: [iv.377] ci las gcig gis skye ba gcig kho na 'phen nam, 'on te du ma 'phen, de bzhin du las du mas skye ba du ma kho na 'phen nam, 'on te gcig rkyang pa 'phen zhe na, las gcig gis skye ba gcig 'phen gyi skye ba du ma 'phen pa med la, ris mthun dum bur 'phen du 'ong bas na, las du mas skye ba gcig 'phen pa'ang med do zhes bya ba ni bye brag smra ba'i lugs so
1777.english: Does a single deed project but a single birth, or many different births? And do a number of deeds project a number of births, or just a single birth? The answer is that a single deed projects a single birth; it cannot project a number of births. And since they would function to project a whole group of similar births, a number of deeds on the other hand is never something that projects but a single birth. This by the way is all the Detailist system.

1833.english: One might ask the following question: "Suppose a person kills a father or mother whose sexual organ has changed. Is it still an `immediate' misdeed?" Even should the sexual organ of one's father or mother switch (and they thus become a female or a male, respectively), it is still the "immediate" deed of patricide or matricide if he kills them. This is because one has still killed the person who performed the function of a father or mother: the one who endowed him with his very special body.

2546.english: "If something produces a deleterious effect upon the powers and their basis," one may assert, "it could never be referred to as `solid food.'" This is because the food is performing a function on two different occasions.

2841.acip: ,DE YANG NYES LTUNG DE DAG GI SGRA BSHAD NI, SDOM PA NYAMS PAR BYED PA'I NYES SPYOD MTHAR THUG YIN PAS NA RTZA BA DANG , PHA ROL NYON MONGS PAS RANG PHAM PAR BYAS PAS NA PHAM PA DANG , GSO BA'I LHAG MA CUNG ZAD TZAM LUS PAS NA LHAG MA DANG , NYES PA DE PHYIR BCOS PA LA SPANG BRAL SNGON DU 'GRO DGOS PAS NA SPANG LTUNG DANG , BYED PA PO NGAN 'GROR LTUNG BAR BYED PAS NA LTUNG BYED DANG , NYES PA DE PHYIR BCOS PA LA DGE SLONG SO SOR MTHOL BA SNGON DU BTANG NAS BSHAGS DGOS PAS NA SO SOR BSHAGS PA DANG , BYA BA LEGS PAR MA BYAS PAS NA NYES BYAS DANG , YON TAN GONG MA SKYE BA LA SGRIB PAS NA SGRIB PA DANG , 'BRAS BU YI DU MI 'ONG BA 'BYIN PAS NA SDIG PA DANG , DAM PA RNAMS KYI SPYAN SNGAR KHA NAS SMRA MI NUS PA'I LAS YIN PAS NA KHA NA MA THO BA ZHES BRJOD PA YIN NO,

2841.english: Here finally is a literal explanation of the names of the different offenses and downfalls. The word "root" is used to describe those ultimate wrong actions which function to damage one's vows. "Defeats" are so named because, in committing them, one has been defeated by the enemy; that is, by mental afflictions and the things they involve. "Remainders" take their name from the fact that, if you perform one of them, there is nonetheless the slightest bit of a vow remaining that can be restored. "Downfalls of release" are spoken of this way because, in order to repair them, one must first release some object. "Downfalls" are so called because they make a person who commits them fall down into the lower births. "Deeds for individual confession" are types of wrong actions that must be confessed by each full monk individually first. "Offenses" or bad deeds are so called because one has done something which was not good. "Obstacles" take their name from the fact that they present an obstacle to the further development of one's good qualities. "Non-virtues" [literally "deeds that we are threatened against"] derive their name from the fact that they give unpleasant consequences. 3581.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, DE LTAR 'BRAS BU BSKYED PA'I BYA BA THAMS CAD GZHAN GYI DBANG CAN YIN LA RKYEN DE RNAMS KYANG RGYU RKYEN SNGA MA SNGA MA DE'I DBANG GIS 'BYUNG BAS 'BRAS BU DE 'BYUNG MI 'BYUNG GI DBANG MED PA SGYU MA DANG SPRUL PA LTA BU'O, , DNGOS PO THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG BZHIN DU BYA BA BYED PA DE LTAR SHES NAS SPRUL PA LTA BU'I DNGOS PO KUN LA KHRO BAR MI 'GYUR BAS, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON 'JOMS PA'I RTEN 'BYUNG RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS PA LA BSLAB PAR BYA'O,
3581.wylie: gsum pa ni, de ltar 'bras bu bskyed pa'i bya ba thams cad gzhan gyi dbang can yin la rkyen de rnams kyang rgyu rkyen snga ma snga ma de'i dbang gis 'byung bas 'bras bu de 'byung mi 'byung gi dbang med pa sgyu ma dang sprul pa lta bu'o, , dngos po thams cad rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong bzhin du bya ba byed pa de ltar shes nas sprul pa lta bu'i dngos po kun la khro bar mi 'gyur bas, nyon mongs kyi sa bon 'joms pa'i rten 'byung rang bzhin med par rtogs pa la bslab par bya'o
3581.english: Here is the third point from before, which is an explanation of why it is improper to feel anger once you have understood that all beings are like a magical show. And so it is that everything in the production of a result depends on other influences, while these influences depend themselves on other, previous causes and influences, they on theirs, and so on. In a sense then it is inevitable whether a particular result will come out or not, it is all up to the causes, and so these things are like a magical show, like pictures of illusion. You must understand this fact, that each and everything which does something is empty of any nature of its own, and yet still functions perfectly well. If you do so, then you will feel no anger towards any of these things that are like pictures of illusion. Thus you must train yourself in the realization of the fact that dependent origination has no nature of its own, for it is this realization which destroys the very seeds of mental affliction. Contemplation Nine People do so much harm to themselves that it is no surprise if they hurt us

4188.acip: ,DNGOS MED RGYU'I BYED PA'I YUL DU MI RUNG BAR BSGRUB PA NI YOD PA GRUB ZIN PAS BSKYED MI DGOS KYANG MED PA CI'I PHYIR MI 'BYUNG ZHE NA BYE BA BRGYA PHRAG RGYU YIS KYANG DNGOS PO MED PA DNGOS POR BSGYUR DU MED DE, DNGOS MED DNGOS POR SU GANG GIS KYANG BYA BAR MI NUS PA'I PHYIR,
4188.wylie: dngos med rgyu'i byed pa'i yul du mi rung bar bsgrub pa ni yod pa grub zin pas bskyed mi dgos kyang med pa ci'i phyir mi 'byung zhe na bye ba brgya phrag rgyu yis kyang dngos po med pa dngos por bsgyur du med de, dngos med dngos por su gang gis kyang bya bar mi nus pa'i phyir
4188.english: What follows next is a proof that a thing without any function could never be the object of the functioning of a cause. In this regard, someone might make the following claim: Since a result that already existed would already have occurred, there would be no need for its cause to produce it. Why though is it that you say a result which does not exist cannot occur? The fact though is that you could have literally billions of causes involved, but you could still never turn something that was not a functioning thing into something that was: there is nothing at all that could ever make something that was not a functioning thing into something that was.

5994.acip: DE LTAR BYAS NA, ZAS SKOM NYID LA YOD PA'I SGRIB PA CAN GYI YI DVAGS KYIS LONGS SPYOD PA LA MA BRTZAMS KYI BAR DU BZA' BTUNG DNGOS YIN KYANG , DES LONGS SPYOD PAR BRTZAMS PA NA, ZAS DE'I RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA YIN GYI, RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED PA MA YIN TE, DE YIN NA LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, DE LTA BU'I YI DVAGS KYIS LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR,
5994.wylie: de ltar byas na, zas skom nyid la yod pa'i sgrib pa can gyi yi dvags kyis longs spyod pa la ma brtsams kyi bar du bza' btung dngos yin kyang , des longs spyod par brtsams pa na, zas de'i rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba yin gyi, rnag khrag tu snang ba'i snang ba tsam gyis bza' btung gi bya ba byed pa ma yin te, de yin na las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir, der thal, de lta bu'i yi dvags kyis las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir
5994.english: Given all this, consider craving spirits that have obstacles that relate to their food and drink itself. The food and drink there really is food and drink, until such time as the spirit starts trying to eat or drink it. When he does try to do so, then the continuum of the food into the next moment starts becoming pus and blood. It is not though that it is the simple appearance of something as pus and blood that could ever function as something to eat or drink. If this were the case, then the rules of karma and its consequences would have to be less than what they really are. And this is true, for if a craving spirit like this ever existed it would represent a failure of the laws of karma and its consequences.

5995.acip: GZHAN YANG , SNANG GZHIR GYUR PA'I RNAG KHRAG MED CING DER SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED NA, RAB RIB CAN LA BSE RU'I NANG DU SKRA SHAD SNANG BAS 'CHING BA DANG , DE LA SNANG BA'I SBRANG BUS LUS ZA BA DANG , SMIG RGYU'I CHUS CHU'I BYA BA BYED NUS PA SOGS YIN PAR THAL, SNANG GZHIR GYUR PA'I RNAG KHRAG MED KYANG , RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED NUS PA'I PHYIR,

5995.english: Suppose moreover that there were no pus and blood out there to appear as the pus and blood, and suppose that the mere appearance of something looking like pus and blood could ever function as something to eat or drink. Well then, you would also have to be able to use a comb on the hair that appears to exist on a porcelain sink to a person with cataracts. And a horsefly that appeared to the same person would have to be able to give him a bite. And the water of a mirage would have to provide all the normal functions of water, and so on. Why so? Well because, according to you, there is no pus and blood out there to appear as pus and blood; according to you, the mere appearance of something looking like pus and blood can provide all the functions of things that you eat and drink.

6292.wylie: spyi don las, lnga pa rigs pa'i rgyal po rten 'brel gyi gtan tshigs bshad pa la, rtags 'god pa dang , tshul sgrub pa gnyis, dang po la phyi nang gi dngos po chos can, bden par med de, rten 'brel yin pa'i phyir, zhes ba'am, yang na phyi nang gi dngos po rnams chos can, bden par mi skye ste, rang gi rgyu rkyen gzhan la bltos nas skye ba'i phyir, snga phyi gnyis la, dper na me long nang gi byad bzhin gyi gzugs brnyan bzhin, zhes 'god par bya ba yin te
6292.english: [From the Overview:] Here we will explain the fifth type of reasoning, the one based on interdependence, and known as the "King of Reasons." First we will present the reasoning, and then secondly prove the validity of its elements. Consider all inner and outer things that perform a function. They are not real, For they are interdependent. The reasoning can also be stated as: Consider all inner and outer things that perform a function. They do not arise really, For they arise in dependence on other things which act as their causes and conditions. Either way you state the reasoning, the following part should be added at the end: They are, for example, like the reflection of a figure in a mirror. 34 Who is Maitreya

6929.wylie: [iv.377] ci las gcig gis skye ba gcig kho na 'phen nam, 'on te du ma 'phen, de bzhin du las du mas skye ba du ma kho na 'phen nam, 'on te gcig rkyang pa 'phen zhe na, las gcig gis skye ba gcig 'phen gyi skye ba du ma 'phen pa med la, ris mthun dum bur 'phen du 'ong bas na, las du mas skye ba gcig 'phen pa'ang med do zhes bya ba ni bye brag smra ba'i lugs so
6929.english: Does a single deed project but a single birth, or many different births? And do a number of deeds project a number of births, or just a single birth? The answer is that a single deed projects a single birth; it cannot project a number of births. And since they would function to project a whole group of similar births, a number of deeds on the other hand is never something that projects but a single birth. This by the way is all the Detailist system.

6979.acip: [IV.411-12] ,'O NA, PHA MA MTSAN GYUR PA BSAD NA MTSAMS MED DU 'GYUR RAM MI 'GYUR ZHE NA, PHA MA GNYIS NI MTSAN GZHAN DU GYUR TE BUD MED DANG SKYES PAR GYUR PA BSAD KYANG , PHA MA BSAD PA'I MTSAMS MED DU 'GYUR TE, RANG GI LUS KHYAD PAR CAN SKYED PA'I PHA MA'I BYA BA BYAS PA DE BSAD PA'I PHYIR,
6979.wylie: [iv.411-12] ,'o na, pha ma mtshan gyur pa bsad na mtshams med du 'gyur ram mi 'gyur zhe na, pha ma gnyis ni mtshan gzhan du gyur te bud med dang skyes par gyur pa bsad kyang , pha ma bsad pa'i mtshams med du 'gyur te, rang gi lus khyad par can skyed pa'i pha ma'i bya ba byas pa de bsad pa'i phyir
6979.english: One might ask the following question: "Suppose a person kills a father or mother whose sexual organ has changed. Is it still an `immediate' misdeed?" 7853.english: Here is the third point from before, which is an explanation of why it is improper to feel anger once you have understood that all beings are like a magical show. And so it is that everything in the production of a result depends on other influences, while these influences depend themselves on other, previous causes and influences, they on theirs, and so on. In a sense then it is inevitable whether a particular result will come out or not, it is all up to the causes, and so these things are like a magical show, like pictures of illusion. You must understand this fact, that each and everything which does something is empty of any nature of its own, and yet still functions perfectly well. If you do so, then you will feel no anger towards any of these things that are like pictures of illusion. Thus you must train yourself in the realization of the fact that dependent origination has no nature of its own, for it is this realization which destroys the very seeds of mental affliction. Contemplation Seven People do so much harm to themselves that it is no surprise if they hurt us

8166.acip: ,DNGOS MED RGYU'I BYED PA'I YUL DU MI RUNG BAR BSGRUB PA NI YOD PA GRUB ZIN PAS BSKYED MI DGOS KYANG MED PA CI'I PHYIR MI 'BYUNG ZHE NA BYE BA BRGYA PHRAG RGYU YIS KYANG DNGOS PO MED PA DNGOS POR BSGYUR DU MED DE, DNGOS MED DNGOS POR SU GANG GIS KYANG BYA BAR MI NUS PA'I PHYIR,
8166.wylie: dngos med rgyu'i byed pa'i yul du mi rung bar bsgrub pa ni yod pa grub zin pas bskyed mi dgos kyang med pa ci'i phyir mi 'byung zhe na bye ba brgya phrag rgyu yis kyang dngos po med pa dngos por bsgyur du med de, dngos med dngos por su gang gis kyang bya bar mi nus pa'i phyir
8166.english: What follows next is a proof that a thing without any function could never be the object of the functioning of a cause. In this regard, someone might make the following claim: Since a result that already existed would already have occurred, there would be no need for its cause to produce it. Why though is it that you say a result which does not exist cannot occur? The fact though is that you could have literally billions of causes involved, but you could still never turn something that was not a functioning thing into something that was: there is nothing at all that could ever make something that was not a functioning thing into something that was.

30657.english: As for the rest of functioning things, we can follow the words of A Clarification of the Verses: We deny that any functional entity at all could ever exist through some nature of its own, whether we're talking about things that start or the things that start them; or goings or the one who goes; or what is viewed, and the the one who views it; or definitions or things defined; or the fact of things happening or what makes them happen; or the component parts of things or the wholes made up of those parts; or specific qualities and those that possess those qualities; or accurate perceptions and the objects which those perceptions hold under their consideration. And this is all because those who possess wisdom understand that all these are nothing but things which occur in mutual reliance.

30839.acip: 'DIR RANG GI SDE PA GONG 'OG GZHAN RNAMS YAN LAG TSOGS PA LA SOGS PA YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PAR 'DOD PA NI, DE RNAMS YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PAR MA BZHAG NA DE RNAMS LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'I YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA YANG MED PAR MTHONG NAS BYA BA BYED NUS KYI YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA 'JOG MA SHES PAS
30839.wylie: 'dir rang gi sde pa gong 'og gzhan rnams yan lag tshogs pa la sogs pa yan lag can la sogs par 'dod pa ni, de rnams yan lag can la sogs par ma bzhag na de rnams las ngo bo tha dad pa'i yan lag can la sogs pa yang med par mthong nas bya ba byed nus kyi yan lag can la sogs pa 'jog ma shes pas
30839.english: Now others of the higher & lower schools of our own group take the position that the collection of the component parts and the like are the whole of the parts and such. If they do not posit thus the whole of the parts and so on, then they see that there is no such whole of the parts or the like that could exist as essentially different from these. Thus then they cannot understand how to establish a whole of the component parts, or anything of the like, that would have the capacity to perform the relevant functions.

31535.english: The following question then might occur to one. 12463.wylie: der rdor bzlas mthar thug tu bshad pa na 'grel pa bzhi sbrag gi mtha' gcod las, rdor bzlas 'dis zung 'jug skyed pa rdor bzlas kyi las su bya ba'i sgo nas mthar thug tu gsungs pa'am, yang na zung 'jug gi skabs su yang ngag dben gyi skabs dang 'dra ba'i rdor bzlas byed pa phyogs gcig la dgongs nas de ltar bshad do, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar yin no
12463.english: As for the explanation that this constitutes the ultimate form of the recitation of the diamonds, the dialectic analysis of the Combination of the Four Commentaries says, Given that this form of the recitation of the diamonds gives birth to the combination of the two, it is said to be "ultimate," with reference to the function of the reciting the diamonds.  You can also say that it is spoken of this way from the point of view of a part of what it entails; that is, even when we reach the combination of the two, we continue to practice a recitation of the diamonds which is similar to that which we do during the stage of transcendent speech.

14696.acip: DE YANG KHYAD CHOS GSUM LDAN ZHES BYA BA, NGO BO'I KHYAD PAR BDE STONG GI RANG BZHIN YIN PA, RNAM PA'I KHYAD PAR MCHOD RDZAS SO SO'I RNAM PAR SHAR BA, BYED LAS KYI KHYAD PAR DBANG PO DRUG GI SPYOD YUL DU ZAG MED KYI BDE BA KHYAD PAR CAN STER BAR BYED PA STE,
14696.wylie: de yang khyad chos gsum ldan zhes bya ba, ngo bo'i khyad par bde stong gi rang bzhin yin pa, rnam pa'i khyad par mchod rdzas so so'i rnam par shar ba, byed las kyi khyad par dbang po drug gi spyod yul du zag med kyi bde ba khyad par can ster bar byed pa ste
14696.english: It is said that these offering substances have three features.  The feature of their essence is that their nature is bliss and voidness.  Their feature of their appearance is that they appear in the respective forms of each of the offering substances.  And the feature of their function is that as the objects of the six senses they are able to produce great, immaculate bliss.

15799.acip: DGU PA BZLAS BA BYA BA LA, BZLAS PA'I DGOS PA NI, YI DAM GYI LHA NYE BAR BYED PA DANG, SDIG PA ZAD PA DANG, NGAG NUS PA DANG LDAN PA, LAS 'GRUB PA, GSUNG RDO RJE 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA 'JOG PA, RDOR BZLAS KYI SMIN BYED DU 'GYUR BA, SNGAGS BZLAS PAS LHA'I THUGS RGYUD BSKUL TE DNGOS GRUB MYUR DU STZOL BA SOGS KYI CHED DU YIN,
15799.wylie: dgu pa bzlas ba bya ba la, bzlas pa'i dgos pa ni, yi dam gyi lha nye bar byed pa dang, sdig pa zad pa dang, ngag nus pa dang ldan pa, las 'grub pa, gsung rdo rje 'grub pa'i nus pa 'jog pa, rdor bzlas kyi smin byed du 'gyur ba, sngags bzlas pas lha'i thugs rgyud bskul te dngos grub myur du stsol ba sogs kyi ched du yin
15799.english: We have now reached the ninth of the eleven practices: the practice of recitation.  What is the purpose of this recitation?  It has many functions, among them the following: it brings the Close Angels closer to us; wears out the power of our bad deeds; gives our speech power; helps us accomplish our spiritual work; plants in us the ability to achieve the diamond of enlightened speech; ripens the power of our practice of the recitation of the Warrior of Diamond; and, as we recite the secret words, it calls in the holy minds of the Angels, asking that They quickly bestow upon us all our spiritual aims.

18041.acip: RO MA'I KHA STENG DANG RKYANG MA'I KHA 'OG TU PHYOGS PAR BSHAD PA'I RGYU MTSAN YOD DE, RO MAS MGRIN PA'I PHYOGS NAS SKYES PA LA STENG DU KHRAG 'PHEN 'DZIN GYI BYA BA BYED CING , RKYANG MAS LTE BA'I PHYOGS NAS 'OG TU KHU BA 'PHEN 'DZIN GYI BYA BA BYED PAS DE LTAR BSHAD PA YIN GYI, SPYIR DE GNYIS KYI STENG 'OG GI BUG PA NAS RLUNG 'BYUNG 'JUG BYED BA LA KHYAD PAR MED PA'I PHYIR,
18041.wylie: ro ma'i kha steng dang rkyang ma'i kha 'og tu phyogs par bshad pa'i rgyu mtshan yod de, ro mas mgrin pa'i phyogs nas skyes pa la steng du khrag 'phen 'dzin gyi bya ba byed cing , rkyang mas lte ba'i phyogs nas 'og tu khu ba 'phen 'dzin gyi bya ba byed pas de ltar bshad pa yin gyi, spyir de gnyis kyi steng 'og gi bug pa nas rlung 'byung 'jug byed ba la khyad par med pa'i phyir
18041.english: Now there is a reason why they say that the channel of taste faces upwards, while the solitary channel faces downwards.  In a male, the channel of taste performs the function of releasing and retaining the flow of the blood element from the throat on up.  The solitary channel then performs the same function for the flow of the semen element, from the navel on down. And although this is the case, there is in general no difference between these two channels insofar as the how the inner wind is made to exit and enter through their upper and lower openings.

18042.acip: RO RKYANG DBU MA GSUM LUS KYI NANG G-YAS G-YON GSUM NA YOD PAR BSHAD PA NI, DE GSUM DANG POR 'CHAGS PA'I TSE DE LTAR GNAS KYANG , LUS RIM GYIS GRUB PA'I TSE LTE 'OG NAS G-YAS G-YON DU 'KHYOG NAS GNAS PA YIN TE, DE YANG RKYANG MA NI LTE 'OG NAS DBUS SU 'KHYOG STE RTAGS KYI RTZER SONG NAS PHO MO GNYIS KA LA DRI CHU 'PHEN 'DZIN GYI BYA BA BYED CING KHYAD PAR SKYES PA LA KHU BA 'PHEN 'DZIN BYED,
18042.wylie: ro rkyang dbu ma gsum lus kyi nang g-yas g-yon gsum na yod par bshad pa ni, de gsum dang por 'chags pa'i tshe de ltar gnas kyang , lus rim gyis grub pa'i tshe lte 'og nas g-yas g-yon du 'khyog nas gnas pa yin te, de yang rkyang ma ni lte 'og nas dbus su 'khyog ste rtags kyi rtser song nas pho mo gnyis ka la dri chu 'phen 'dzin gyi bya ba byed cing khyad par skyes pa la khu ba 'phen 'dzin byed
18042.english: Now when we say that the trio of the channel of taste, the solitary channel, and the central channel are situated on the inside or right or left of the body, this is with reference to how they are laid out when they first form in the body. As the body though goes through its various stages of development, these three channels start to curve right or left in the area below the navel.  That is--below the navel--the solitary channel curves in towards the center and extends to the tip of the sexual organ.  Here, in both males and females, it performs the function of releasing or retaining urine.  And in males in particular, it also performs this function for the semen.

18043.acip: RO MA G-YON DU 'KHYOG STE GSANG GNAS KYI 'OG NAS CHA GNYIS SU GYES TE CHA GCIG RTAGS KYI RTZER SONG NAS BUD MED LA KHRAG 'PHEN 'DZIN GYI BYA BA BYED CING CHA GCIG BSHANG LAM GYI RTZER SONG STE PHO MO GNYIS KA LA BSHANG BA 'PHEN 'DZIN BYED,
18043.wylie: ro ma g-yon du 'khyog ste gsang gnas kyi 'og nas cha gnyis su gyes te cha gcig rtags kyi rtser song nas bud med la khrag 'phen 'dzin gyi bya ba byed cing cha gcig bshang lam gyi rtser song ste pho mo gnyis ka la bshang ba 'phen 'dzin byed
18043.english: Also below the navel, the channel of taste curves to the left, where below the secret place it splits into two sections.  One section extends then to the tip of the sexual organ, where in women it provides the function of releasing or retaining blood.  The other section extends to the very end of the anus, where it performs the function of the release and retention of feces, in both men women.

18044.acip: DBU MA G-YAS SU 'KHYOG STE RTAGS KYI RTZER SONG NAS SKYES PA LA KHU BA 'PHEN 'DZIN GYI BYA BA BYED PA YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,

18111.acip: GSUM PA RLUNG RNAMS KYIS THUN MONG DU JI LTAR BYED PA'I TSUL YOD DE, SPYIR RLUNG BCU MNGAL DU 'CHAGS PAR BSHAD KYANG PHYIR MA BTZAS BAR DU DBANG PO'I SGOR 'BYUNG 'JUG MI BYED CING, BTZAS NAS AA THUNG GI GZHIR GYUR TE NGAG SMRA BRJOD KYI BYA BA BYED LA,
18111.wylie: gsum pa rlung rnams kyis thun mong du ji ltar byed pa'i tshul yod de, spyir rlung bcu mngal du 'chags par bshad kyang phyir ma btsas bar du dbang po'i sgor 'byung 'jug mi byed cing, btsas nas aa thung gi gzhir gyur te ngag smra brjod kyi bya ba byed la
18111.english: This brings us then to our third section, which covers how these primary and secondary winds work together. Now generally speaking, it is taught that the ten different inner winds form while we are still inside the womb. Until we actually come out of the womb though, these winds do not function to proceed to or retreat from the gateways of the senses. Once we are born from the womb, they then begin to function as the foundation of that most basic sound, the short vowel ah, thus enabling us for the act of speech.

18112.acip: KHYAD PAR DU RTZA BA'I RLUNG GIS NI LUS G-YO 'GUL GYI BYA BA BYED, YAN LAG GI RLUNG GIS NI DBANG SHES YUL LA 'JUG PA'I BYA BA BYED CING, RNAL 'BYOR BA LA YI GE GSUM GYI GZHIR GYUR NAS RDOR BZLAS KYI BYA BA BYED PA DANG, SNYING GA'I MI SHIGS PA LA THIM NAS GZHI LAM GYI 'OD GSAL 'CHAR BA SOGS KYI BYA BA BYED PA'I PHYIR,
18112.wylie: khyad par du rtsa ba'i rlung gis ni lus g-yo 'gul gyi bya ba byed, yan lag gi rlung gis ni dbang shes yul la 'jug pa'i bya ba byed cing, rnal 'byor ba la yi ge gsum gyi gzhir gyur nas rdor bzlas kyi bya ba byed pa dang, snying ga'i mi shigs pa la thim nas gzhi lam gyi 'od gsal 'char ba sogs kyi bya ba byed pa'i phyir
18112.english: In a more particular sense, the primary winds perform the function of enabling the body to move; while the secondary winds make the sense consciousnesses capable of engaging in their objects. These winds further provide the foundation for the three sacred syllables, thus enabling yogis and yoginis to perform the practice of diamond recitation.  And among still other functions, they make possible the appearance of the clear light (both in the natural state of things and for a person engaged in spiritual practice), by virtue of these winds' dissolving into the indestructible drop at the heart.

21205.acip: 'DA' KA MA'I GNAS 'DIS NI MTHO RIS ZHES BYA BA THAR PA'I GROGS SU 'GRO BA LAS, THAR PA KHO NA 'GRUB PA NI MA YIN ZHES GSUNGS NGO, ,TSE 'DI LA DBU MA CUNG ZAD KHA BYE BA RNAMS BAR DO NYID DU PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA YIN NO, GNAD KYI MAN NGAG LA BRTEN NAS RIM GYIS CHOS KYI DBYINGS RTOGS PA'I THABS BSTAN ZIN TO,,
21205.wylie: 'da' ka ma'i gnas 'dis ni mtho ris zhes bya ba thar pa'i grogs su 'gro ba las, thar pa kho na 'grub pa ni ma yin zhes gsungs ngo, ,tshe 'di la dbu ma cung zad kha bye ba rnams bar do nyid du phyag rgya chen po 'grub par 'gyur ba yin no, gnad kyi man ngag la brten nas rim gyis chos kyi dbyings rtogs pa'i thabs bstan zin to
21205.english: This crucial point, to be practiced at the moment of death, is said to refer to "higher births"; the idea being that it functions to aid you in reaching freedom, rather than leading itself to this goal.  Those who are able to open the central channel just a bit in this life achieve the realization of the great seal only during the inbetween state. This concludes our presentation of the method for perceiving ultimate reality through a successive process, by utilizing the advices on the crucial points.

21285.wylie: gdong dngos dang sbar mo bzhis 'dzin pa sogs gdong gi bya ba byed nus pas na, (gdong lnga) pa ste sengge brgyad kyis btegs cing, gzi 'od ('bar ba'i rin chen) te rin po che las grub pa'i (khri) phun sum tshogs pa'i (steng) du, (chu skyes) te padma dang
21285.english: Atop the tree is an excellent throne of magnificent, sparkling jewels; that is, a throne carved itself out of gemstone.  The throne is held aloft by eight lions--which are referred to in the original Tibetan with the poetic name of "beasts of the five faces."  The point here is that they are supporting the throne for example both with their head and with their four paws, which are thus performing the same function as the head.  This throne is set with cushions, beginning with one made of a lotus, which in the original Tibetan is again referred to with a poeticism: the child of the lake.
